entries.title: Host application keyboard, pointer and composition
entries.summary: Published Floe controllers own keyboard, composition and pointer gestures; product adapters bind them to painted window generations. Clients own IME and hosts deliver confirmed keys/Unicode. Cancellation releases held input without replay, while qualification distinguishes generated events from real applications/devices.

entries.title: Host application viewing, display and resource lifetime
entries.summary: Runtime/native events own application facts; bootstrap and published SDK own viewing, geometry and immutable resources. Decode current pixels before input and preserve process identity through reconnect. Transport loss never proves exit; incompatible loaded protocols require explicit save/quit/reopen.

entries.title: Managed service release discovery and version selection
entries.summary: Registries provide release candidates; Manager validates immutable identity, compatibility and reviewed update plans. Discovery and selection execute nothing. One drawer retains browsing, selection and failures, while admitted work outlives it and rollback preserves verified prior release/binding.

entries.title: Managed service template publication, acquisition and formats
entries.summary: Published templates own definitions, formats and passive resources; Redeven validates offline bundles and authorizes imported original directories. Historical syntax adapts in memory to one executor without rewriting stored bytes. Failed acquisition or review preserves active source and grants no lifecycle effects.

entries.title: Service management recovery and resource ownership
entries.summary: Registry owns transactions, allocations and identities; fresh backend facts govern recovery and deletion. Names, cached reachability and uncertain legacy resources grant no destructive authority. Retain data by default, preserve unavailable facts and require reviewed ownership/consent before execution.

entries.title: Web service browser routing and authorization
entries.summary: Registry access mode selects protected unified proxy or Desktop loopback; current Environment/forward authority governs every handoff. Browser cookies, Electron credentials and service authentication stay separate. Reject stale routes without direct-target fallback or durable substitute sessions.

entries.title: Independent Web Environment Center
entries.summary: Desktop combines an environment center with its existing local Runtime lifecycle. Web Center deploys independently; Runtime never requires Center or Desktop to start. Both hosts share Contracts/Core/Controller/UI. Web Center has one administrator, with no registration, users, roles, organizations or user ACL service.

entries.title: Flower startup and recovery presentation
entries.summary: Both carriers project one readiness owner and typed Stop/Retry, retaining drafts/navigation. Close failure needs restart; contradictory facts are nonretryable. Initial content admits workspace, then refresh/reconnect preserves mounted state without another availability controller.

entries.title: Tessiven immutable canvases, DSL and display compatibility
entries.summary: Runtime owns immutable canvas YAML and contiguous version migration; clients render a frozen data-only display contract. Reads preserve historical bytes, digests and revisions while writes create current validated snapshots. Display projection never grants resource authority or rewrites topology.

entries.title: Native Runtime bridge
entries.summary: native-bridge --state-root attaches only to existing Runtime via owner socket. Stdio uses redeven-native-runtime-h2/1 and native-runtime CONNECT. Missing/stopped/incompatible targets fail without install/start/address fallback/Desktop credentials; disconnect releases client only.

entries.title: Flower browser source ownership
entries.summary: Runtime authorizes targets; source Host owns CDP/extension adapters. Discovery grants no input. Each page has one debugger/input order; opener ancestry stays private. Source loss retires affected bindings only; unknown effects never replay or create replacement authority.

entries.title: Flower browser Linux preparation
entries.summary: Runtime discovers installs/registers Native Messaging; Host Applications owns graphical lifecycle. Linux guide prepares persistent Chrome profiles without launch/target authority. Clients pass opaque IDs. Personal profiles remain; missing/unsafe/unsupported sources fail before launch.

entries.title: Database schema migration ownership
entries.summary: Each repository migrates its own opaque stores. Validate full SQLite/WAL before readiness; contiguous atomic edges preserve records. Future, drifted, wrong-kind or unsupported state remains untouched. Failure blocks only its service without upstream repair or database replacement.

entries.title: AI readiness and service generation lifecycle
entries.summary: One process-local Redeven controller owns AI construction/retry/publication/leases/drain/close; Floret owns durable facts. Non-AI surfaces stay usable. Requests bind one generation; failed readiness returns typed sanitized state without partial publication or Store repair.

entries.title: Runtime startup presentation
entries.summary: `redeven run` startup is modeled as a lifecycle event stream. Human terminal output and public machine events are renderers over the same state snapshot, while a separate private Desktop report carries machine-only attach data and stable failure codes needed to open or recover the local Env App safely.

entries.title: Observation and target action events
entries.summary: Target actions are ordinary Flower tool observations. The workspace stream remains the only lifecycle and replay channel; screenshot descriptors are canonical keyframes, while short-lived live frames are target-scoped media and may be dropped without changing thread state.

entries.title: Local UI surface
entries.summary: Local UI supports independent concurrent Desktop/browser sessions. Public HTTP(S)/WS(S) shares a port; Desktop private uses numeric loopback protocol. Versioned SQLite owns one-shot authorization/spend; network policy owns exposure/password/certificates/migrations.

entries.title: Env App session event transport
entries.summary: One Floe HTTP proxy runtime serves each Env App session and all built-in/plugin logical event streams. Features cannot consume parallel native HTTP/1.1 slots, retarget upstream identity or create another transport. Session replacement cancels observations; stopping observation never cancels business work.

entries.title: Web Services interface
entries.summary: Activity/Workbench share service list/drawer: identity, state, action, facts. Retain narrow/localized/large-text usability. Historical failure never replaces current state; failed checks preserve facts and authorized recovery. Resource cache grants no lifecycle or route authority.

entries.title: Human remote desktop sessions
entries.summary: Redeven owns authorization/sessions/placement/audit; Floe Native Apps owns OS capture/input/codecs/playback and Linux acquisition/service. Share signed-in desktop without private replacement or policy changes. Disconnect preserves work; unavailable media revokes input until fresh frame.

entries.title: Administrator-authorized remote desktop deployment over SSH
entries.summary: Desktop owns SSH authorization/UI lifetime, Floe Native Apps privileged preparation and Runtime service authorization/audit. Every connection ensures current policy and authenticates actual Runtime. Unknown state is preserved. Cancellation reports rollback; verified completion may win but cannot auto-open after cancel.

entries.title: Persistent remote desktop sharing approval
entries.summary: Redeven owns sharing preference/reset; Floe Native Apps owns OS consent/private recovery. Logged-in Runtime may reuse saved approval, which proves no admission and never reaches viewers/URLs/audits. This user Portal path is separate from SSH system-service deployment.

entries.title: Remote desktop connection launcher
entries.summary: One Host Applications/Workbench flow identifies host, readiness and primary action, continuing consent in place under session policy. Failure retains recovery; dismissing pending creation releases its session. Once opened, viewer lifetime is independent of the launcher.

entries.title: Flowersec transport for graphical windows
entries.summary: Flowersec owns encrypted multiplexed transport/backpressure; Redeven resources/authorization/routes. Graphical state, tickets, input, clipboard/audio/pixels/disconnect use native proxy; static acquisition stays authenticated browser traffic. No missing-authority or raw HTTP/WS bypass.

entries.title: Remote desktop viewer interaction
entries.summary: Published input/playback and session contracts own current-frame authority. Separate cursors permit immediate movement; embedded cursors hide local pointer. Recovery keeps controls usable; disconnect stops media/input with confirmed removal or Retry. Frozen pixels never imply connection.

entries.title: Remote desktop media and input scheduling
entries.summary: Published native packages own capture/encode/playback; session contract owns authority/generations. Bound media work and align cursors to painted pixels. Input admission proves no delivery; capture/input failures retire authority and late work cannot replace successors.

entries.title: Host application catalog, platforms and preparation
entries.summary: Redeven authorizes catalog, instances and independent shares; published native libraries own platform execution and preparation. Applications survive viewer release and compatible Runtime restart. Capability probes govern readiness, explicit controls govern termination and uncertainty never launches replacements.

entries.title: Host application lifecycle and Linux instance recovery
entries.summary: Viewing, sharing, closing windows and ending processes remain distinct across platforms. Ordinary controls preserve save/cancel; only confirmed Force quit bypasses saving. Linux instances survive clients and Runtime only while verified user, kernel generation and private display identity remain intact.

entries.title: macOS application authority, capture and lifecycle
entries.summary: Redeven opens installed macOS bundles as the Runtime user and binds remote capture to actual windows/process generations. One helper owns independent sharing channels; decoded current pixels precede input. OS/app facts govern quit and closure, preserving unsaved work through viewing failures.

entries.title: Portable native Runtime binaries
entries.summary: Shared builder owns Runtime/Gateway terminal linkage: Linux runs on glibc/musl without host loader; Darwin requires matching Apple build. Missing tools fail preflight. Static LGPL Linux releases must include matching source/relink materials or publication fails.

entries.title: Managed Web Service opening
entries.summary: Templates parse entrances; Runtime verifies/persists preparation; Desktop navigates and Env App presents. Open verified Host/Container/Compose entrances through Forward without lifecycle/data changes. HTTP401 proves availability only; failures offer recovery and never stop healthy apps.

entries.title: Independent Host service lifecycle
entries.summary: Apps own execution; Redeven owns authorized lifecycle/native identity/launch records/opening. Restart preserves PID/generation. No supervisor or PID-only authority. Distinguish absent/mismatched/uninspectable: only absence permits launch; opening failure never stops app.

entries.title: Managed Web Services
entries.summary: Redeven owns instances/resources/bindings/operations/forwards; verified templates define behavior. One engine serves Host/Container/Compose lifecycle. Registry and exact resource identity authorize actions; invalid provenance, ownership, permission or health never adopts unknown resources.

entries.title: Managed Service operation progress
entries.summary: Manager Reporter owns live output; Registry owns history. One operation ID retains disclosure/completion through refresh. Redact command templates before storage; output grants no identity. Capture/storage/transport failures must not expose secrets, queries, private paths or control bytes.

entries.title: Managed Service Instance Configuration
entries.summary: Verified template owns baseline; Redeven owns overrides, release/digest, resources, secrets and rebuilds. One resolver combines baseline/differences. Apply requires stopped state, current revision/plan/risk checks; failure preserves prior state or explicitly reports rollback failure.

entries.title: Runtime Service snapshot
entries.summary: Typed Runtime snapshots expose protocol/version, compatibility epoch, capabilities, readiness and workload identity to Desktop/Local UI. Gateway attachment is optional routing, never a prerequisite for independent access or authenticated host lifecycle management.

entries.title: Runtime session permission gates
entries.summary: Runtime validates session metadata and supported app/channel pairs before intersecting control-plane and local policy. Code App and Port Forward add their own gates. Read permits existing monitor/process observations; process termination independently requires execute and cannot inherit authority from visibility.

entries.title: Runtime system monitoring
entries.summary: Monitor owns one CPU/memory/network/process snapshot for page and Workbench. All OS-marked loopback interfaces are excluded from the shared network counters/rates. Failed network samples never enter history or fall back to unfiltered totals; later samples recover independently while other metrics remain usable.

entries.title: Runtime transport composition and Env App recovery
entries.summary: Published Flowersec owns acquisition, framing, retries and connection replacement; Redeven maps exact product authorization onto one current Env App session. Views and consumers share that session without reconnecting or replaying business requests, while epochs fence obsolete Desktop observations.

entries.title: Runtime artifact spend and control pool
entries.summary: Opaque single-spend control/data artifacts bind each Lease to a digest-global tombstone. Persist idempotent bootstrap/top-up identities; reject stale, duplicate, malformed, expired or cross-environment responses. Replenishment/relink are explicit terminal transitions, never silent fallback.

entries.title: Runtime terminal lifecycle
entries.summary: Floeterm owns PTY/Ghostty VT, geometry/controller epoch, input encoding, history/reset and atomic Presentation. Redeven maps permission/session metadata/placement. Browser consumes bounded semantic streams without parsing bytes or introducing a second terminal state machine.

entries.title: Product RPC request encoding
entries.summary: Redeven codecs construct JSON; Flowersec validates/dispatches. File creation preserves empty content and omitted encoding; absent options stay omitted, explicit false/empty retain meaning. Invalid input fails before dispatch and needs codec repair, not retries or weaker validation.

entries.title: Git workspace inventory lifecycle
entries.summary: Git queries expose bounded immutable snapshots with revision-bound paging. Git/Files mutations coordinate topology and invalidate snapshots around effects; display grants no authority. Oversized/stale/malformed/exhausted reads return bounded typed errors without losing Flowersec session.

entries.title: Env App upstream web dependencies
entries.summary: Env App adapts published Floe UI/runtime/protocol, FloeBrowser projection, Floeterm terminal-web and Flowersec helpers. Manifest/lock pins define the consumed release; Floe owns asset monitoring and per-view recovery, while Redeven supplies authenticated product integration.

entries.title: Env App terminal and surface composition
entries.summary: Env App adapts Floeterm PTY facts and Floe shell, focus, selection and KeepAlive. Redeven owns views/localized controls. Session-keyed Runtime nodes survive view changes; visible panes paint independently while the active session owns input, search and commands.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin host integration boundary
entries.summary: Redeven consumes coordinated released ReDevPlugin Go/npm/Rust/machine artifacts. Product owns sessions, source review, placement, runtime builds and business adapters. Missing or unverifiable platform contracts fail without copied mechanics, sibling imports or compatibility fallback.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin Redeven adapters
entries.summary: Redeven binds authenticated sessions, source policy, business capabilities and placement to released ReDevPlugin. Platform alone owns protocol/package integrity/execution/state. Adapter faults stop at product boundary without implicit grants, copied platform state or substitute lifecycle.

entries.title: Plugin platform integration
entries.summary: Redeven mounts one released ReDevPlugin Host/HTTP namespace/client/scope. Published Supervisor runs verified Linux/Darwin runtime. Product supplies sessions, sources, placement and adapters; platform owns package/state/protocol/execution. Unproven identity fails closed.

entries.title: Plugin process sessions
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin Process Broker owns processes; Redeven supplies authenticated scope/permission/minimal environment/secrets/state/audit. Opaque handles expose bounded binary stdio, no second protocol. Overflow may lose output; close/disable/uninstall/revoke/owner teardown stops owned work.

entries.title: Plugin background entries
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns headless Worker lifecycle and durable intervals. Redeven supplies environment permission policy and presents verified status through ordinary plugin management. No hidden surface, host scheduler, replay endpoint or second Worker protocol is involved.

entries.title: Plugin package and runtime lifecycle
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin owns package inspection, installation, source identity, durable receipts, runtime readiness and retained data. Redeven supplies authenticated product policy and a single review experience for market, GitHub, HTTPS, uploaded and generated packages. Installation does not grant permissions.

entries.title: Plugin surface recovery and permissions
entries.summary: Env App owns one authenticated plugin client, shared scope and installation observer. ReDevPlugin owns inventory, Executions, Events, permissions, revocation and recovery. Panel closure/reconnect retains exact request identity and outcome; refresh never becomes another mutation or lifecycle.

entries.title: Plugin market consumption
entries.summary: Redeven consumes one complete public market representation. Official and community are display classifications, not admission privileges. Packages remain ordinary `.redevplugin` assets in GitHub Releases; every installation uses the released Host inspection and durable installation APIs.

entries.title: Container execution and operation observation
entries.summary: Every container operation binds exact engine, endpoint and resource identity. The service owns admission through execution and read-only reconciliation; UI streams observe it. Cancellation is explicit, terminal uncertainty never replays commands and transfer counters report only measured download facts.

entries.title: Container resource capability, console and usage facts
entries.summary: Native resource services own endpoint-bound execution, admission and reconciliation; the console presents typed authorized facts and drafts. Missing engines and partial volume inspections stay explicit. UI reachability, size or reference guesses never grant mutation authority or replace resource preflight.

entries.title: Container engine service management
entries.summary: One ContainerServiceController owns Docker/Podman discovery, lifecycle, configuration, preflight identity and reconciliation. Opaque IDs hide endpoints; mutation requires full RWX/Admin without elevation. Unknown owner/revision/final state fails closed, never replaying interrupted work.

entries.title: Single-administrator Web Center access
entries.summary: Center has one administrator and multiple devices. Center, Gateway and Runtime authorize independently: directory/open access never bypasses Runtime login or grants host management. Device revocation cancels all derived admissions while retaining unrelated devices and routes.

entries.title: Runtime access sessions
entries.summary: Runtime accessgate alone owns validity/revocation. Valid sessions survive tabs/refresh/disconnect; cookie names isolate protocols/ports without extra authority. Expiry/logout/security/restart needs login. Invalid/incompatible clients fail closed; MFA owns credential recovery.

entries.title: Runtime two-factor authentication
entries.summary: Runtime accessgate independently requires password then TOTP/recovery for browser/direct/Cloud sessions. Password challenges grant no app access. Native/SSH management has separate authority; missing/corrupt state fails closed and recovery blocks access until new credentials commit.

entries.title: Local UI exposure, HTTPS identity and explicit certificate changes
entries.summary: Runtime owns public listeners, saved HTTPS identity and session admission; Desktop presents explicit next-start changes. Network exposure requires concrete authority and password, while certificate trust remains a separate user action. TLS failures never downgrade or expose the private Desktop bridge.

entries.title: Permission policy and filesystem scope
entries.summary: Runtime policy is authoritative even after control-plane session authorization. Clamp grants by local permission policy and scope every file-facing feature to explicit directory roots. Product controls present that decision; they never widen permissions or infer access from paths.

entries.title: Plugin platform integration security
entries.summary: ReDevPlugin accepts authenticated host identity and source policy, never browser-claimed trust. HTTP checks auth/origin/CSRF/action; direct calls check owner/action/resource. Source identity, execution approval, update eligibility and permissions remain independent and fail closed on identity or scope mismatch.

entries.title: Verified Environment access routes
entries.summary: Desktop associates Gateway routes only through trusted attachment ID, Runtime public ID and Gateway-key matches; health is independent. Names/URLs/renderer claims grant nothing. Local/Cloud ownership stays separate; missing/unverified routes require explicit replacement.

entries.title: Host application component cache
entries.summary: Published artifactcache owns verification, locking and eviction. Desktop supplies its private directory, seven-day idle retention and 2 GB budget plus document-local transfers/UI. Devices reuse verified archives; cancellation retains completed cache. Unknown catalogs fail and cleanup cannot negate successful preparation.

entries.title: Desktop qualification lifecycle
entries.summary: Desktop supervisor owns scenario/resource/cleanup deadlines. Acceptance leaves no owned processes, bridges or fixtures; preserve production Quit and independent Runtime. Names/ports grant no stop authority. Timeout/interruption/forced cleanup/residue fails with retained manifest evidence.

entries.title: Desktop development sessions and bundles
entries.summary: Development launcher owns Desktop, local Runtime, saved Gateways and bundles. Launch exact current source and stop owned services together. Prune only verified inactive bundles, preserving user identity/data, unrelated services and recent/selected/live builds; incomplete inventory blocks pruning.

entries.title: Desktop Web Service browser window
entries.summary: Desktop owns protected target views, toolbar, navigation and cleanup over Runtime-authorized Web Service routes. Reopen reuses the same live forward; content gets no Desktop bridge. Invalid navigation rejects, while marked upstream failure offers local retry without reauthorizing or restarting the app.

entries.title: Desktop host application titlebar
entries.summary: Redeven owns the compact host toolbar; macOS capture/Xpra own commands and sessions, Desktop supplies native geometry. Window selection, picture settings and close share one titlebar. Disconnect disables unavailable actions while preserving window and recovery.

entries.title: Desktop shell theme state
entries.summary: One validated Desktop theme snapshot drives Welcome, Env App, chrome and generated documents. New/reset themes use Porcelain; valid choices survive upgrades. Selection paints before persistence, retaining acknowledged state, drafts/focus/content and Retry on failure.

entries.title: Environment library, registrations and card presentation
entries.summary: Welcome projects authoritative registration owners into a stable library. Exact Runtime/Cloud links and verified Gateway routes may share cards, without transferring lifecycle or storage authority. Explicit actions name their owner; snapshots preserve drafts, focus and pending work while late replies cannot resurrect removed records.

entries.title: Desktop interaction continuity
entries.summary: Welcome owns interaction sessions; Launcher/Runtime own business operations. Observations retain open panels, draft, focus, selection, steps and scroll. Only explicit user transitions or current completion alter visibility. Invalid authority blocks submission with recovery; closing progress never cancels work.

entries.title: Desktop Welcome navigation
entries.summary: Welcome page selection is immediate and independent of Launcher IPC or Runtime preparation. Visited pages retain state; readiness gates Flower requests, not navigation. Explicit Environment tab changes may animate cards, while refresh/return preserves headers and skips entrance replay.

entries.title: Desktop transport recovery and model-source sessions
entries.summary: A placement bridge owns one immutable recovery generation and exact Environment session. Only its owner replaces transport after validation; late callbacks are fenced. Model-source lifetime survives control reconnects without delaying Env App or persisting transport history, while terminal failure withdraws interaction authority.

entries.title: Desktop SSH runtime operations
entries.summary: Desktop uses saved SSH connection/placement for host/container Runtime. One local coordinator, operation, transport lease and temporary helper own lifecycle/recovery. Gateway/Cloud credentials grant no SSH authority; targets persist no Desktop supervisor or lifecycle lock.

entries.title: Desktop WSL runtime operations
entries.summary: Windows11x64 runs Electron, not native Local/container Runtime. Register initialized Linux x64 WSL2 targets; manage only exact distro/user Runtime. Windows owns distro lifecycle. Missing/old/uninitialized targets or broken commands/packages/Bridge need visible explicit recovery.

entries.title: Environment settings sessions, connections and presentation
entries.summary: One target-bound settings session owns connection/access drafts and immediate opening. Verified registrations govern management, never card layout or URL text. Health refresh preserves forms and geometry; saves fence older reads. Public addresses stay independent from private lifecycle credentials and current process state.

entries.title: Desktop SSH environment settings
entries.summary: SSH creation/editing share one form and registration API. Common controls precede advanced options, retained in an inspectable summary. Failures preserve drafts. Registration contracts own connections/secrets, while Environment settings owns the window, tab, draft and asynchronous recovery lifetime.

entries.title: Desktop Runtime coordination and readiness
entries.summary: One target-bound coordinator admits managed Local, WSL, SSH and container lifecycle work. Verified direct channels and current compatible Presence govern actions; Gateway/Cloud access stays separate. Conflicts retain the first operation and failed observations never prove stopped state or authorize alternate routing.

entries.title: Desktop managed Environment reinstall
entries.summary: Wipe reinstall confirms exact target/root, verifies package, attempts stop, replaces root, verifies startup and cleans old data. Unknown process or broken state cannot block filesystem recovery. Preserve-data reinstall changes managed files and rolls back failed verification.

entries.title: Desktop application updates
entries.summary: One Desktop update coordinator serves every entry. Packaged macOS uses signed architecture-specific Sparkle; Linux uses matching DEB/RPM feeds. Unsupported, development or misplaced builds offer manual recovery. Internal Windows NSIS has no production update feed.

entries.title: CodeSpace system-browser access
entries.summary: Desktop resolves trusted resource identity over Environment transport into short-lived loopback entry. Browser receives resource-bound HTTP/WS, never private bridge tokens. Runtime owns permission/editor generation; closing Environment retires routes and failed open leaves no listener.

entries.title: Native Desktop CodeSpace access
entries.summary: Desktop owns CodeSpace window/profile/loopback listener/route; Runtime owns editor generation/permissions/AccessGate. Native HTTP/WebSockets need no privileged preload. Close/revoke/stop ends connections; route or saved-port failure never substitutes transport or replays requests.

entries.title: Optional Runtime Cloud egress
entries.summary: Cloud is optional Runtime functionality. Gateway has no Cloud binding or credentials. A Runtime can explicitly select an attached Gateway as a restricted network exit; that selection changes transport, never Cloud ownership or independent access authority.

entries.title: Gateway device trust and host operations
entries.summary: Paired devices receive independent Gateway access, never accounts, roles or host-management grants. Scoped TLS bootstrap supports fresh private networks. Runtime password/MFA and Web Center administrator protection remain independent; revocation affects only the device's derived channels.

entries.title: Independent Gateway service
entries.summary: Gateway independently owns Runtime attachment/device admission/relay, working without Cloud account, cached authority or public Internet. Cloud alone owns membership/organizations/roles. Gateway device trust and Runtime environment authentication create no local user directory.

entries.title: Gateway network settings
entries.summary: Verified host admin atomically saves share endpoints/listeners/Host restrictions. Listener changes require explicit restart; live sockets persist. Empty hostname restrictions never weaken TLS/invitations/membership/Desktop policy. Invalid or failed writes preserve saved/live state.

entries.title: Gateway Desktop interactions
entries.summary: Desktop enrolls Local, SSH, WSL and container Runtimes through one app session. Management, invitation verification and consent are separate authorities; only confirmed membership completes enrollment. Observations retain drafts, failures require explicit recovery, and no Runtime URL enrollment form exists.

entries.title: Gateway access sessions
entries.summary: Desktop reaches joined Runtime over its outbound Flowersec Gateway connection; Gateway forwards to fixed application entry without dialing a Runtime URL. Desktop/Runtime terminate TLS; Runtime retains password/MFA/Host/Origin authority. Entry expiry never shortens established sessions.

entries.title: Independent Gateway qualification
entries.summary: Independent Gateway acceptance uses production handlers, host placements, real application authentication and multilingual management. Evidence qualifies only exercised device admission and revocation paths. UI/process qualification stays separate from exact-main push gates and release packaging.

entries.title: Browser Editor runtime
entries.summary: Browser Editor support is owned by the Code App app server. Codespaces are opened through Local UI `/cs/<id>/` routes or through remote `cs-*` sandbox hosts, while Desktop and Env App can prepare or update managed Browser Editor runtime versions through code workspace engine APIs.

entries.title: File preview rendering, formats and viewport
entries.summary: Redeven owns source identity, authorization and preview modes; published renderers own layout and parsing. Each page has one asynchronous owner, stale work is fenced and failures remain local/retryable. HTML stays isolated, rich formats retain original bytes and unselected widgets gain no input authority.

entries.title: File preview actions and dismissal
entries.summary: Redeven owns file actions, drafts and immediate cancellation; Floe owns titlebar, tabs and exit presence. Retained panels preserve document state through switching and close motion. Accepted dismissal fences work before releasing resources, with unsaved-change confirmation and responsive focus restoration.

entries.title: Flower companion presence, composer and motion
entries.summary: Collapsed Flower projects canonical work and connection-local editor intent through one retained textarea. Priority decides whether to show a decision, draft, status target or inspection. Shared shell motion preserves draft, selection, IME and focus; historical completion never becomes new feedback.

entries.title: Flower conversation selection and detail reads
entries.summary:
Flower acknowledges navigation before transcript work. One coordinator serves
navigation, command confirmation and reference preflight. ThreadCache owns
selection and detail; the loader owns bounded ephemeral demand.
Readiness controls reveal; elapsed time controls feedback only.

entries.title: Activity navigation restoration
entries.summary: One Redeven Activity record selects the saved target before mounting and commits navigation/recency immediately. Floe owns geometry only. Invalid targets use available built-ins or Terminal; transient inventory failure retains the target, and late restoration never overrides a newer user selection.

entries.title: Env App resource snapshots
entries.summary: Floe owns disposable cache restoration/coalescing/fencing/persistence/eviction; Redeven verifies identity/projection. Resource lists retain successful data while refresh animates only its icon. Cache grants nothing; denial clears, connectivity failure retains facts with Retry.

entries.title: Page loading, asynchronous feedback and document recovery
entries.summary: Retain successful same-resource content through refresh while initial loads occupy final geometry. Source replacement and permission loss fence retained state. Published placeholders, stable controls and asset monitoring preserve work; only explicit user reload replaces an outdated document.

entries.title: Whole-window status surfaces
entries.summary: Floe owns window layout/retry/artwork; Redeven maps actual access/connection state. Opaque neutral recovery covers retained inert workspaces without duplicate notices. Floating windows/widgets/drag exclude this material; appearance grants neither authority nor another recovery loop.

entries.title: Tessiven canvas navigation, relationships and Flower reading
entries.summary: Published Floe owns graph layout, routing and viewport paint; Tessiven supplies canonical topology and selectable details. Folding, summaries and filters change only the visible scene. Flower remains the editing/operations interface, with compact replies retaining canonical actions and conversation state.

entries.title: Runtime settings
entries.summary: Env App owns settings destinations/drafts/API adapters; Floe reusable layout/navigation. Narrow/revisited panels retain usability, drafts and scroll. APIs authorize writes, never reader UI. Failure retains input; maintenance continues through its controller after explicit consent.

entries.title: Flower extensions
entries.summary: Shared Flower retains Skills/MCP/Plugins management through typed authenticated carrier adapters. The rail entry below New chat preserves drafts and tab filters; Runtime has no duplicate Skills destination. Readers inspect, admins configure, failures retain input/Retry, and all locales supply copy.

entries.title: UI presentation transactions
entries.summary: Navigation selects synchronously, paints intent, commits target visibility, then focuses/resizes/scrolls/measures after content paint. Floe owns visual/committed value separation; Redeven applies it across heavy product surfaces without duplicating business state.

entries.title: Env App floating layer order
entries.summary: Env App assigns global bands for windows, Flower, plugins, modals and commands; interaction reorders only its band. Floe owns viewport constraints/drag geometry. Redeven saves settled bounds while preserving reachable controls, local scroll and destination interaction.

entries.title: Dialog content placement
entries.summary: Published Floe owns Dialog structure; Redeven supplies localized content/actions. Headers hold identity/controls; guidance and consequences belong in bodies, including drawers and confirmations. Missing descriptions require content fixes, not hidden text or header subtitles.

entries.title: Adaptive desktop and mobile navigation
entries.summary: Desktop and mobile remain distinct interaction modes; narrow desktop regions use temporary drawers without rewriting saved placement. Mobile panels and Flower navigation preserve business-page/editor identity and explicit focus choices. Published geometry controls safe areas without product drag or snap lifecycles.

entries.title: Git workspace generations, diffs and visual state
entries.summary: Exact client capabilities and monotonic generations fence Git inventory, diffs and filesystem decoration. Dispatched effects invalidate even on unknown outcomes; preview never grants authority. Retained inspection and theme roles preserve selection and local scrolling without treating layout as content freshness.

entries.title: Shared surface material
entries.summary: Published Floe owns material and motion. Env App/Welcome select soft-neumorphic roles while business content stays flat. Preserve input, portals, widget identity and hot interaction ownership. Resolve conflicts at the product override source without copying shadow logic or introducing another theme/dependency owner.

entries.title: Product accessibility for AI agents
entries.summary: Redeven owns accessible names/state/relationships while preserving layout, handlers, focus and inert exclusion. Floe owns reusable controls/layers. Shared defects require evidence and published fixes. Scope claims accurately: accessibility edits alone certify neither WCAG nor model performance.

entries.title: Input focus boundaries
entries.summary: Published Floe owns focus presentation; Redeven supplies layout, semantic state and explicit compound-input boundaries. Ordinary fields change border color only, preserving geometry/shadows; the persistent Flower chat composer keeps its border unchanged. Fix conflicting styles at their owner with source/browser checks; no fallback stylesheet.

entries.title: Workbench composition, input and surface lifetime
entries.summary: Published Floe owns canvas composition and generic input mechanics; Redeven supplies permission, persistence and selected-widget adapters. Explicit wheel and text-selection contracts stay separate. Lazy module delivery preserves the mounted canvas and never creates another lifecycle or eagerly initializes inactive features.

entries.title: Workbench terminal interaction
entries.summary: Floeterm terminal-go owns PTY, VT, geometry, controller epoch, semantic history and atomic Presentation. terminal-web renders one canvas/view and collects local input. Authority/renderer faults fail closed; history/search faults stay local and retryable without disconnecting output.

entries.title: Terminal fonts across client devices
entries.summary: Env App owns document-local terminal fonts. New preferences use bundled JetBrains Mono at size 12; existing IDs/sizes remain unchanged and each client resolves availability. Floeterm retains canonical cells, cursor and session grid. Font presentation cannot replace terminal authority or erase stored preferences.

entries.title: Terminal session groups
entries.summary: Runtime catalogs own groups, assignments and named views; Activity/Workbench share environment projection with local expansion/active view. Default is immutable and every session has one known group_id. Membership is independent of placement, cwd, controller and recovery.

entries.title: Plugin package review, installation and saved-data recovery
entries.summary: All plugin sources share released package inspection, exact review and durable installation. Official/community classification changes display only. Permissions remain independent explicit decisions; unknown effects reconcile from durable receipts without replay.

entries.title: File icon presentation
entries.summary: Floe owns filename recognition, SVG icons and palettes; Redeven supplies names, directory/link metadata and size. Formats retain reviewed distinctions and unknown files use the generic upstream icon. Icons confer no preview/execution/extraction authority, whose independent format and permission checks remain.

entries.title: Files context menus
entries.summary: Floe owns file-menu placement, scrolling, gestures and dismissal; Redeven supplies bounds/actions/locales. Keep menus eight CSS pixels inside Files/surface/visible viewport intersection. Invalid bounds close; never escape global layers or duplicate Workbench transforms.

entries.title: Plugin Center interaction
entries.summary: Redeven owns Plugin Center navigation; Floe owns dialogs, presence and input. Workbench uses a retained drawer and Activity the same directory page. Search/filter/selection/scroll persist. Closing management does not cancel Host execution; released ReDevPlugin owns lifecycle, permissions and surface authority.

entries.title: Plugin discovery, placement and layout continuity
entries.summary: Redeven owns navigation, pins and persisted geometry; released ReDevPlugin owns surface slots and authority. Activity and Workbench placements remain independent, lazy opening captures current context and hidden opened surfaces retain edits. Layout continuity never revives revoked authority or replays unknown writes.

entries.title: Flower turn submission, outbox and input recall
entries.summary: One immutable transport outbox captures ordinary submitted text and resources before asynchronous admission. Request identity survives receipt/live ordering and explicit recovery, while newer composer edits remain independent. Canonical confirmation retires transport state; recalling history never submits or restores attachments.

entries.title: Flower references, origin context and canonical admission
entries.summary: Connection-local chips carry authorized discovery and frozen page/thread context into explicit Send. Floret alone owns admitted ordered references. Labels and paths grant no authority; source failures retain drafts and outbox reconciliation never overwrites newer input or creates duplicate canonical records.

entries.title: Absolute filesystem directory selection
entries.summary: Floe owns picker navigation/validity/request lifetime; Redeven supplies authoritative path context/connection/locales/form. Absolute paths and root shortcuts grant no access. Failed navigation retains intent, disables confirmation and offers Retry; execution rechecks policy.

entries.title: Personal directory favorites
entries.summary: Runtime stores independent ordered favorites/revisions per authenticated namespace/endpoint/user. Env App/Desktop supply metadata to published Floe pickers and menus; existing filesystem navigation alone validates/selects paths. Favorites neither grant authority nor duplicate navigation.

entries.title: Flower working directory navigation
entries.summary: Flower owns draft/thread directory intent; Env App destination navigation. Full-page selects/browses directory, companion omits it. Menus freeze thread/path. Activity opens Files/new Terminal; Workbench creates widgets without scaling canvas or injecting existing-shell commands.

entries.title: Flower Activity companion and contextual Ask Flower placement
entries.summary: One retained Flower surface moves between authorized Activity and Workbench hosts. Published Floe owns companion geometry and presence; product adapters supply safe-area measurements and focus handoffs. Contextual Ask Flower adapts the published Floe `PromptCard`; Floe owns its complete layout, motion and viewport behavior. Placement creates neither another stream nor a second execution or editor owner.

entries.title: Flower read state
entries.summary: Redeven confirms reads per user from server version and actual local presentation. Old responses cannot restore already-cleared indicators; unseen activity stays unread. Temporary sync failures recover in background without blocking operations or inventing acknowledgements.

entries.title: Flower incremental live state
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical history/versions; Redeven authorizes one workspace stream into ThreadCache. UTF-8 growth changes only its item. Transport/window recovery preserves execution, prose and drafts; retained DOM and scoped reads keep navigation/disclosure stable without rescanning history.

entries.title: Flower timeline ordering
entries.summary: Flower renders Floret ordered facts using stable item, TurnID and RunID identities. Captured ordinary input appears immediately; only that draft is consumed. Queued inputs stay in the dock. Canonical request-key confirmation preserves mounted rows without duplicates, and summaries never author timeline detail.

entries.title: Flower turn status and process disclosure
entries.summary: Floret owns turn outcome and timing. Terminal turns fold eligible process rows once; pending controls, uncertain effects and inspected work remain visible. Explicit choices persist, user messages/finals stay mounted, and settled question/answer receipts reopen with complete content.

entries.title: Flower personal conversation preferences
entries.summary: Explicit model, directory and model-owned reasoning choices are remembered per authenticated namespace, endpoint and user. Loading/switching threads never writes defaults. New roots prefer explicit launch/draft choices, then personal memory, then configuration; existing threads and immutable turns retain confirmed settings.

entries.title: Flower model and navigation presentation
entries.summary: Flower separates Desktop/environment sources, unavailable models and first setup. Thread-owned model/reasoning choices remain authoritative. Navigation distinguishes visual intent from committed content and fences stale reads. Transient action failures use notifications; canonical failures remain in their timeline.

entries.title: Flower setup and settings
entries.summary: Shared setup/settings serve both Flower carriers. Unconfigured profiles offer setup; configured new chats offer editable starters without launching. Retained modal preserves saves/errors and makes covered chat inert without read acknowledgement; existing model/permission/recovery owns policy.

entries.title: Flower provider setup and account selection
entries.summary: Provider dialogs keep explicit access methods, keys, accounts and model selection independent. Background discovery preserves drafts and known-account UI; user selection alone starts neither OAuth nor persistence. Backend policy determines capability and errors never silently switch service or billing.

entries.title: Flower failure recovery
entries.summary: Floret owns outcomes/checkpoints/migration. Flower retains readable content and one recovery surface while drafts, queue edits, Stop/navigation remain usable. Transport uncertainty permits no replay. Readiness timeout offers refresh; deterministic migration failure remains administrative.

entries.title: Flower composer attachments
entries.summary: One Flower controller owns attachment select/paste/drop/retry/remove/preview/send. Hosts authenticate staging; Redeven owns bytes/unadmitted commands, Floret admitted history. Large text converts only after successful staging, retaining IME and source on failure.

entries.title: Flower consecutive tool sequences
entries.summary: Desktop/Env App group consecutive tools and adjacent thinking. Active groups open; following prose or canonical turn end folds eligible work, never temporary gaps. Inspection survives and answered input separates settled work. Presentation stays ephemeral over Floret facts without summaries or migrations.

entries.title: Flower activity disclosure interaction
entries.summary: Desktop and Env App render canonical Floret facts with one transcript viewport owner. Live updates cannot move pressed triggers or insert hit targets before click completion. Canceled gestures activate nothing; disposal releases gesture ownership while retained content stays inspectable.

entries.title: Flower conversation sidebar
entries.summary: Desktop and Env App share one Flower sidebar with ThreadID-owned rows and endpoint-owned pin order. Selection, running work, unread attention and pending actions remain distinct. Live summaries preserve row/menu/focus identity. Resizing and pin feedback are ephemeral presentation over the canonical ThreadCache.

entries.title: Flower inline media
entries.summary: Shared Flower renders canonical images/video/audio/screenshots/self-contained HTML through released Floe media/isolation. Redeven authorizes resources. Forbidden, missing, oversized or mismatched media yields local retryable errors without interrupting conversation.

entries.title: Flower streaming stability
entries.summary: Indexed ThreadCache and published incremental Markdown apply actor-native changes only to affected text/DOM. Preserve history, code color, copy, focus, selection and disclosure. Semantic changes stay visible; malformed updates recover through the single live-state owner without suppressing output or adding lifecycle.

entries.title: Flower progress and provisional edit presentation
entries.summary: Floret request facts drive output indicators; frozen tool schemas drive bounded provisional names/counts. Stable geometry keeps metrics readable without repeated announcements. Confirmed results replace previews, and failed edits retain only actual mutations without giving provisional paths filesystem authority.

entries.title: Markdown diagram rendering
entries.summary: Flower and file Markdown preserve authored Mermaid while consuming published Floe/Pele. External Pele renders syntax; Floe owns sanitization/scheduling/controls. Redeven binds document identity, semantic palette, locales and context without copying an alternate renderer.

entries.title: Flower code highlighting
entries.summary: Flower owns committed Markdown lifetime; Floe enhanceCodeBlock owns visible tokenization/scheduling/color. Completed labelled fences receive colors in Env App/Desktop while source stays readable/copyable. Highlighting preserves geometry, focus and selection; unavailable or excessive work leaves plain code.

entries.title: Flower message appearance
entries.summary: Shared Flower uses Floe colors for compact reading and contrasting sent-message selection. Themes change paint without disturbing DOM/geometry/selection. Queue stays quieter; forced colors use system roles. Media/cards preserve identity without empty message bubbles.

entries.title: Flower terminal activity presentation
entries.summary: Flower renders canonical Floret Activity with host task labels and safe details for every terminal operation, including writes/empty reads. Disclosure/scroll are ephemeral; no stdin/private paths/effect internals or invented lifecycle. Approval controls remain composer-owned.

entries.title: Shared interface scale
entries.summary: Published Floe owns type, controls and responsive rows; Redeven maps semantic roles without root scaling or a separate density setting. Desktop uses 13px body/control, 12px supporting and 11px captions. Coarse-pointer fields and targets retain the published touch scale.

entries.title: Flower decisions, approval presentation and secret drafts
entries.summary: Canonical Floret input and approval requests determine decision visibility and settlement. Shared row-local guards retain explicit choice/custom drafts, volatile secrets and safe operation facts. Read-only or unavailable controls remain visible with reasons; local rendering never creates permission or lifecycle.

entries.title: Flower citations
entries.summary: Floret stores assistant sources with end-exclusive Unicode code-point ranges. Flower renders titled links and removes provider markers on Copy. Only safe credential-free HTTP(S) URLs link; marker IDs imply no URL. Historical gaps stay explicit and authored bibliographies remain content.

entries.title: Flower child task navigation and detail window
entries.summary: Authorized parent inventory controls child navigation; canonical thread identity chooses portraits and task labels. The detail window reads bounded current state without selecting the parent or creating another stream. Stable capsules, dropdowns and footer preserve reading geometry through updates and failures.

entries.title: Flower parent event timeline
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical child reports/events and admission; UI owns pages/bodies/disclosure only. Reports appear in the selected parent with canonical child avatars, without receipt/admission/preservation notices. Reading wakes neither task. Every full read rechecks recipient authority and canonical fixed-range paging.

entries.title: Flower computer viewer presentation
entries.summary: Floe owns Stage geometry/launcher; Flower projects canonical status and decoded media. Viewing, moving, closing or restoring grants no target/execution authority. Interrupted/private frames retain recovery and cannot borrow unrelated images. The media contract remains the sole authorization/sampling owner.

entries.title: Flower working files and deliverables
entries.summary: Flower keeps intermediates in Runtime state and finals at the user's destination. Redeven owns bytes, filesystem policy and UI; Floret owns canonical results and identities. Files, Fork and cleanup preserve this boundary without another artifact index, transcript, upstream API or domain migration.

entries.title: Flower MCP runtime
entries.summary: Redeven configures MCP over official Go SDK stdio/Streamable HTTP sessions; Floret owns invocation/approval/effects/history/recovery. Add no competing execution or retry owner. Unknown outcomes are terminal without replay; invalid saved configuration remains unchanged.

entries.title: Flower Agent Plugins
entries.summary: Flower loads environment-scoped Agent Plugins1.0.0 Skills/MCP, separate from native .redevplugin SDK/packages/market. Redeven owns admission/distribution/configuration and Floret invocation/history. A manifest identifies a package, never grants execution or registers a market listing.

entries.title: Flower plugin catalog integration
entries.summary: Flower can consume an explicitly configured plugin directory without shipping or maintaining a default index. Runtime sources and user-managed sources use the same catalog reader and GitHub installation workflow. Catalog availability never owns installed plugin authority.

entries.title: Flower thread Goals
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical Goal, model tool, reflection and completion; Redeven authorizes and presents facts. One current Goal/thread states intent without text limits or Todo dependency. Stop/navigation/recovery remain usable; unresolved requests never imply successful mutation.

entries.title: Tessiven Flower tools and scoped Runtime operations
entries.summary: Flower maps authorized code, configuration and Runtime facts into canvas versions. Resource discovery and explicit actions reuse original registries and executors with exact bindings. Missing authority never substitutes a local route, and unknown mutations require original-operation inspection before any new attempt.

entries.title: Authorized platform model gateway
entries.summary: Redeven discovers authorized models via trusted control-channel lease/origin; Runtime never receives platform Provider keys. Floret owns execution/tools/history/recovery; platform Edge admission/binding/reservations/accounting. Routing does not transfer these ownership boundaries.

entries.title: Model directory and selection
entries.summary: Runtime owns atomic metadata. Reads/send preflight use shipped/saved snapshots; refresh never blocks configured chat. Background refresh is disclosed, opt-in and excludes OpenRouter. OpenRouter/Ollama discover on addition; manual refresh remains available.

entries.title: Model web search
entries.summary: Redeven resolves provider/model search preferences once for settings and turns; final tools drive prompt/wire. Floret v7.40.2 validates hosted events against frozen requests. Undeclared hosted execution fails because remote effects cannot safely be assumed absent.

entries.title: Local ChatGPT admission and account lifecycle
entries.summary: Authenticated local capability and verified account facts govern ChatGPT registration, renewal and requests. One local owner manages bounded sign-in and logout, independently of provider connection saves. No remote credential transfer, implicit OAuth or fallback billing changes account authority.

entries.title: Provider configuration validation
entries.summary: Redeven owns configuration, credentials and Flower readiness across every settings entrypoint and provider-bundle save. Floret's public runtime contract is unchanged. Invalid saves preserve configuration and credentials; authentication/network failures remain execution errors.

entries.title: Provider API and catalog review
entries.summary: Runtime, Web, Desktop and iOS share one authenticated catalog. Official contracts and pinned models.dev inventory require released adapters and qualified limits, replay, tools, images and reasoning. Refreshes preserve configured model selections and stored conversation identities.

entries.title: Direct image reading and tool media retention
entries.summary:
image.read inspects authorized files/snapshots. Redeven owns bytes/authorization;
Floret owns history/membership. File references stay references; results use native
images, not browsers, temporary servers or Base64 result JSON. Original snapshots
remain available after model preparation.

entries.title: AI tool runtime and canonical interaction ownership
entries.summary: Redeven supplies typed product tools, policies, effects and presentation; Floret owns invocation, irreversible intent, approvals and admitted history. Browser state cannot authorize or settle execution. Canonical terminal views control release, and persistence failure retains unresolved interactions rather than inventing success.

entries.title: Flower storage ownership and migrations
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical Agent formats; Redeven owns product facts and uploads. Supported state upgrades through stable kinds, contiguous atomic migrations and public APIs while preserving history. Unknown, future, drifted or invalid state blocks Flower without resetting data or disabling the core Runtime.

entries.title: Flower backup and recovery
entries.summary: Readiness drains generations while storage owners snapshot/migrate and Floret ends execution. Freeze Flower writes, verify collections and retain backups; restore history/settings/read-state/uploads without stopping other surfaces. Failures preserve recovery, never replay effects or roll back binaries.

entries.title: Flower historical writer acceptance
entries.summary: Immutable fixtures come from locked released Redeven writers; current tests copy and verify them. Supported history must remain readable and continue after upgrade. Preserve source/module digests and public write paths. Fixture drift or upgrade failure blocks integration; database open alone is insufficient.

entries.title: Flower attachment resources
entries.summary: Redeven owns authenticated bytes/metadata/quotas/retention; Floret turn membership. Upload once, submit opaque attachment_id, render attachment://v1 and revalidate provider resources. Paths remain private; invalid identity/claims/digest/bytes reject only the affected reference.

entries.title: AI tool permissions and dispatch
entries.summary: Redeven owns product visibility, policy, prompt and approval UI; Floret owns invocation and neutral tools. Current thread permission applies at the next boundary, while each admitted call retains its snapshot. Ordinary independent calls may authorize together; invalid authority rejects and dependent work waits.

entries.title: Computer and browser use runtime
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns targets, resources, control and script processes; Floret owns Agent lifecycle/effects/history. Prefer authorized commands for data, semantics for interaction and images for visual decisions. Missing target/permission/capability fails explicitly without selecting a substitute tab/window/device.

entries.title: Computer semantic snapshots
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime normalizes browser, macOS AX and Linux AT-SPI facts into bounded schema v2. Unsupported facts stay absent and relationships stay within the tree. Invalid observations are discarded while confirmed effects/output survive. Metadata grants no input authority and uncertain effects never replay.

entries.title: Computer script execution and semantic observations
entries.summary: One computer.exec is one Floret effect attempt. QuickJS exposes controlled ui/browser/log under ComputerUseRuntime. Same-target loops/navigation compose, but target/permission/private-input changes stop at existing interaction boundaries, preserving confirmed progress without uncertain replay.

entries.title: Computer script read and validation boundaries
entries.summary: Browser/native reads deliver the promised shape or explicit failure; absent observation never becomes empty data. Later read failure preserves confirmed input without replay. Typed document/candidate preflight invalidation with no input/preparation yields `dispatch_status:not_dispatched` and seals the call; it never enters `completed_actions`. [Scripts](computer-use-scripts.md) owns namespace/failure barriers; every read retains permission, privacy and publication checks.

entries.title: Computer source detail and continuation reads
entries.summary:
Source reads make original AX/DOM fields and descendants reachable beyond the
bounded default tree. [Read validation](computer-script-read-contract.md) owns
permissions, privacy and final publication; source detail does not bypass it or grant new target authority.

entries.title: Optional built-in browser installation
entries.summary: Runtime owns optional Chromium installation, enabled by default but downloaded only after authenticated confirmation. Disable cancels/closes/blocks prompts while retaining bytes/site data. Floret owns waiting/continuation; failed verification publishes nothing and exposes Retry/source choice.

entries.title: Built-in browser Linux system preparation
entries.summary: Installation manager owns readiness; short approved Runtime transactions prepare Linux namespaces/dependencies. Preserve sandbox/global AppArmor and admit only catalog bytes at fixed root-owned paths. Separate dependency, sandbox and unknown launch failures; failed publication preserves data.

entries.title: Browser and desktop settings
entries.summary: Both carriers share Browser and desktop settings. Runtime capabilities, thread grants and extension consent are independent. Flower discovers and selects task pages/applications through its computer tools; settings do not expose a manual target picker. Open/refresh/close grants or launches nothing; failed reads stay unknown. Floret alone owns conversation lifecycle.

entries.title: Guided personal browser connection
entries.summary: Desktop and Env App share browser connection guidance over ComputerUseRuntime and Floret interactions. Users confirm Chrome installation and initial binding; later sessions restore the same environment. This bounded observation UI owns neither execution nor another lifecycle, and verified connections are reused.

entries.title: Chrome connection diagnostics and recovery
entries.summary: Runtime owns readiness/handshakes; both carriers provide host-specific recovery. Installed Chrome/accepted launch proves neither control nor continuation. Distinguish resource/session/launch/status failures; only compatible live profiles enter Floret Respond, without browser substitution.

entries.title: Managed browsers and authorized Chrome tabs
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns connection, authorization and control for managed Chromium, explicit CDP and Chrome extension through one restricted executor. Selected-tab authority excludes siblings/devices. Disconnect, revocation, closure and uncertain effects stop work without automatic replacement.

entries.title: Semantic desktop operations and explicit control
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns desktop execution: explicit macOS app window or private Linux Xvfb/D-Bus. Semantic actions prefer native accessibility. Foreground work requires task authorization and honors Stop/takeover; OS permissions alone cannot certify unobtrusive background operation.

entries.title: Computer target selection across threads
entries.summary: ComputerUseRuntime owns discovery/selection through Flower's computer tools. Users describe work; Flower locates the page/window. Product settings expose no manual target picker or endpoint-to-picker route. Selection is working position, not authority. Stale/disconnected/occupied targets fail explicitly while retaining previous selection.

entries.title: Computer use safety pauses and user control
entries.summary: Floret owns questions, answers and continuation; Redeven owns authorized computer effects and private media. Failures remain factual and blocked capture is not a screenshot. Answers pass unchanged without granting authority or replay. Fresh safe observation precedes further input; no second recovery lifecycle exists.

entries.title: Private browser observation and input
entries.summary: Runtime owns observer-bound private pixels/input; Floret takeover/continuation. Bind observer/revision/thread/run/target; disconnect revokes and uncertainty never replays. Canonical answer starts a fresh Run/observation; private input also waits for matching decoded pixels.

entries.title: Computer use media and visual requests
entries.summary:
Redeven owns authorized screenshots; Floret owns history/preparation. Flower
shows frames inline/in Stage. Durable frames and ephemeral samples have separate
lifetimes; tool success does not prove delivery. Model encodings never replace original assets.

entries.title: Computer use product qualification
entries.summary: Qualify Computer through built renderer, Runtime, decoder and target adapter. Exact fixture effects, decoded pixels, source/artifact hashes and cleanup prove only the named target/provider scope. HTTP, metadata or model prose is insufficient; uncertain input is never replayed to produce a pass.

entries.title: Computer use provider qualification evidence
entries.summary: Historical runs support [qualification](computer-use-qualification.md) only for their declared platform, provider and build scope. Canonical results and independently observed effects establish execution. Original model, measurement and transport failures remain distinct from subsequent passing runs; no result certifies arbitrary applications.

entries.title: Computer use qualification evidence
entries.summary: Historical runs follow [the acceptance contract](computer-use-qualification.md). Worktree passes do not replace exact-main checks, certify arbitrary applications or erase failures. Retained diagnostics exclude private text and pixels. Each result keeps its original platform, source identity, acceptance boundary and unresolved limitations.

entries.title: Browser and native drag timing qualification
entries.summary:
Browser drag timing is measured from actual input events, with all model and
assertion failures retained. [Script contracts](computer-use-scripts.md) define
behavior; [qualification](computer-use-qualification.md) defines the test lane.
Browser measurements certify only the tested browser paths and durations.

entries.title: Media contention and native read qualification
entries.summary:
The October 28 qualification validates cancellable media-write admission and
native node/subtree completeness. Production uses published Floret v7.88.0;
its existing cancellable inventory and write-gate contract need no upstream
change. Browser, AX and AT-SPI share the same completeness semantics.

entries.title: Computer use paired model measurements
entries.summary: Paired production Flower/Floret/model/browser fixtures compare visual primitives with semantic scripts on the same tasks. Keep all failures and reject missing, duplicate or unmeasured samples. Headless results do not certify native desktop or Chrome focus; those require separate product qualification.

entries.title: Codex computer and browser use design evidence
entries.summary: Versioned official documentation and installed app 26.908.40834/extension 1.26.901.11451 inform command-first routing, AX/script batching and compact observations. They expose neither proprietary implementation nor universal external-window isolation. Flower Runtime remains execution and authorization authority.

entries.title: AI terminal tool runtime
entries.summary: Redeven owns PTYs and bounded output; Floret v7 owns canonical tool calls, interactions, effect attempts, results and Activity. One adapter authorizes execution once and publishes current views. Product SQL stores no parallel terminal lifecycle or effect recovery.

entries.title: Model reasoning capability, selection and transport
entries.summary: One capability catalog and canonicalizer define reasoning controls for saved threads and immutable turns. UI exposes only supported intent and writes preferences only on explicit successful edits. Provider fragments remain reasoning, automatic title policy stays independent and loading never changes choices.

entries.title: Flower prompt and rule sources
entries.summary: Every Flower run profile shares one host English base prompt defining Redeven assistant identity, visual output and local delivery. Runtime facts, tool definitions and native Floret guidance retain separate ownership and availability; product identity never replaces them.

entries.title: AI model and context runtime
entries.summary: Redeven persists model/reasoning preferences, credentials and source selection. Floret owns provider context and opaque continuation. Desktop/environment sources stay distinct; typed observations drive usage/compaction. Token input/output limits remain separate and configuration merges preserve unrelated settings.

entries.title: Model provider surface and history
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical provider history/rendering lineage; Redeven supplies model, prompt, permissions and ephemeral overlays at declared boundaries. History stays readable without restoring removed tools or rewriting facts. Surface changes create compatible lineage, never a host continuation store.

entries.title: Model request recovery
entries.summary: Floret owns retry admission, physical-request deadlines and attempt identity. Redeven supplies protocol facts through one adapter and displays the authoritative current view. Frozen input, confirmed tool exchanges and user cancellation retain their existing authority across transport recovery.

entries.title: Model request reuse
entries.summary: Floret owns reuse decisions/canonical state; Redeven runs one prepared request/Responses consumer. In-memory transport reuse requires matching next canonical state and complete input. Failure follows ordinary turn recovery; supplemental context never enables reuse.

entries.title: Context usage, measurement and compaction
entries.summary: Floret owns confirmed usage, pressure, bounded compaction and canonical installation; Redeven maps independent token, byte and image evidence. Full input and frozen attempt identity constrain measurement. Manual compaction is explicit intent, while unavailable historical evidence remains unknown.

entries.title: DeepSeek Responses
entries.summary:
Flower routes the DeepSeek provider to the published Floret v7.66.1 Responses gateway.
Floret owns `/responses` rendering, SSE parsing, reasoning, usage normalization,
function-call validation, and opaque provider history. Redeven only maps its
model DTOs and canonical dotted tool names to provider-safe aliases.

entries.title: Flower canonical thread queries
entries.summary:
Flower exposes two read-only tools for finding another readable conversation
and reading its content: `threads.query` and `threads.read`. The tool contract
is intentionally smaller than Floret's published general query API.
`threads.aggregate` is not registered or dispatched.

entries.title: Floret thread runtime integration
entries.summary: Floret v7 ThreadService alone owns active/canonical lifecycle. Redeven authorizes endpoints/resources/provider-tool effects. Send/Respond/Cancel/Retry/CompactContext return typed state before continuation. Canonical records deduplicate; drafts and execution tokens stay transient.

entries.title: Floret Redeven adapter and projection
entries.summary: Redeven authorizes ownership/resources and maps typed Floret views, updates, failures and safe Activity. Floret alone owns lifecycle, persistence, migration, cancellation and provider state. The adapter neither waits on provider work nor mirrors execution or receipts.

entries.title: Flower child runtime and parent event boundary
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical child threads, reports and parent-scoped lifecycle events. Redeven projects bounded status and complete authorized handoffs without another store or scheduler. Child input and approvals remain blocked at their own boundary; labels and historical references never transfer ownership.

entries.title: Flower thread Fork and deletion coordination
entries.summary: Floret owns canonical Fork and deletion; Redeven authorizes endpoint scope and coordinates product settings, read state and file claims. Stable explicit requests preserve exact destinations and cleanup order. Convergence uses typed canonical outcomes without a saga, compensating deletion or cross-database atomicity claim.

entries.title: Flower plugin generation
entries.summary: Flower authors applications through the released ReDevPlugin CLI/SDK and version-matched skill. Redeven owns intent, guidance, review and placement; platform owns templates/build/preview/package/execution. Floret owns tool dispatch/approvals; no copied authoring implementation.

entries.title: Redeven environment operations
entries.summary: Environment lifecycle goes through Redeven product operations, never guessed container/SSH/systemd/launchctl/process commands. Flower receives this rule from the standard redeven-environment skill; do not embed a second environment workflow into the global prompt.

entries.title: OKF bundle lifecycle
entries.summary: Redeven builds its embedded OKF bundle from curated source files under the top-level `okf/` authoring root, verifies deterministic dist outputs under `okf/dist/`, and embeds the resulting bundle into the binary used by Runtime and AI features for local retrieval.

entries.title: OKF tool suite
entries.summary: Redeven exposes the embedded OKF bundle through read-only `okf.index`, `okf.search`, and `okf.open` builtin tools. Redeven projects bounded safe results into Floret v7.26.0 structured Activity rows, and the shared Flower surface expands those rows without reading raw OKF result JSON.

entries.title: Flower managed runtime facts
entries.summary: Floret v7.47.1 owns chronological admission, semantic updates, context messages, compaction and recovery. Flower only collects/presents authorized complete facts in four partitions: execution environment, date/timezone, repository rule sources and available skills.

entries.title: Gateway v6 independent device protocol
entries.summary: Gateway v6, authority epoch 70, defines independent client-device trust and Runtime attachments. The public protocol and private host API are separate surfaces on the same service, with independently verified device access and host authority. Cloud machine management and publication are absent.

entries.title: RCPP v5 Cloud API
entries.summary: RCPP v5 separates Cloud authority from route. CloudRuntimeBinding binds Environment/Runtime/Namespace/principal/generation. One Runtime controller owns direct/Gateway enrollment, registration, heartbeat, reserve and recovery; Desktop never duplicates credential ownership.

entries.title: Self-contained installer distribution
entries.summary: Release builds macOS/Linux amd64/arm64 self-contained installers without CGO and renders entry from exact binary digests, all signed via SHA256SUMS. Receiving hosts need no Go/Cosign/Python/OpenSSL/package manager, but require shell, HTTPS downloader and SHA256 utility.

entries.title: CI and release gates
entries.summary: Focused checks precede staged pre-commit and exact-tip main admission. Dependencies, assets, locales and OKF must agree. Browser/Desktop/native/long-thread acceptance remains explicit; releases require authenticated artifacts and same-commit historical-data qualification. Windows is internal-only.

entries.title: ReDevPlugin release artifact gate
entries.summary: Consume the coordinated published ReDevPlugin release with artifacts bound to tag, source, target, digest, signer and receipt. Registry readbacks, native evidence and closed inventories establish provenance. Partial, mutable, Windows or target-mismatched inputs fail before admission.

entries.title: Plugin integration gate
entries.summary: Plugin gate checks released ReDevPlugin Host/market against Redeven authority, placement, renderer and Desktop lifecycle. Use published packages/isolated profiles; copied platform paths, implicit grants, second bridges and stale projections fail instead of fabricating integration.

entries.title: OKF release assets
entries.summary: Releases distribute OKF manifest and SHA256 verification assets alongside CLI/Desktop packages and signed SHA256SUMS. The signed aggregate remains their public integrity anchor; standalone verification files never replace authenticated release checksums or source provenance.

entries.title: Automated service-template catalog updates
entries.summary: The template repository publishes immutable recommendations. Redeven daily/manual adoption pins public Go checksums, regenerates notices/OKF and passes normal integration checks. Failure retains published main and uncertain push requires ref inspection. Adoption never upgrades installed service instances.

entries.title: Deploy and qualify standalone Web Center
entries.summary: Center binary/UI deploy independently of Runtime/Desktop. Qualification records source/artifacts, host/browser, real duration, cleanup and limits using isolated names/ports/state. Preserve existing Runtime; smoke checks certify neither eight-hour soak nor a different native browser.
