concepts.title: Flower attachment resources
concepts.summary: Redeven owns authenticated bytes/metadata/quotas/retention; Floret turn membership. Upload once, submit opaque attachment_id, render attachment://v1 and revalidate provider resources. Paths remain private; invalid identity/claims/digest/bytes reject only the affected reference.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity and provider preparation
Redeven product threadstore v1 owns generated attachment ID, authenticated user hash, private relative storage name, detected/sanitized media metadata, exact size/SHA-256, optional strict UTF-8 code-point/line counts, source/state/idempotency and retention claims. Floret ResourceRef is content-addressed; display locator is attachment://v1/<attachment-id>/<encoded-name>. Retention never authorizes canonical reads.

Admit files independently of model modalities/tools. Preserve recognized text/image/PDF types; other files, including Office and non-UTF-8 documents, keep original bytes/name as application/octet-stream. Active UTF-8 uses text/plain; pasted long text requires strict UTF-8. Queue/admission enforce owner, staging, count and byte bounds, not a model MIME allowlist.

Capabilities affect presentation only. Supported modalities receive native content; otherwise the owning user message/tool result receives a factual manifest: name, media_type, size_bytes, locator, content_included:false, content_trust:untrusted. It adds no system message, tool-selection instruction or generic failure advice. Tool definitions own access guidance; manifest implies neither extraction, tool availability nor parser installation. The model chooses tools or explains its limitation. Switching models never rejects retained attachments/images; verify canonical descriptors/digest before the same manifest fallback, preserving native rendering for capable models.

## Reads and copies
Historical reads revalidate membership and bytes. Upload/image lookup uses current-path public Floret windows (50 items, 128-byte previews), one authorized subscription and page/stable-leaf correlation; no full hydration or retention-inventory authorization. Resolved handles prove ownership/metadata only. Hash during materialization; provider/text/image consumers verify their exact snapshots and downloads verify before returning paths. Avoid prehash plus reread. Bound size/cancellation; corrupt bytes never publish a copy.

Floret v7.51.1 exposes user and confirmed tool descriptors canonically. Retention distinguishes tool media from uploads; never parse image refs as upload rows.

attachment.materialize requires current execution/canonical authorization, RWX and normal write policy. Create a unique regular scratch copy using cancellable 32 KiB streaming with exact size/SHA-256; image locators retain bounded validation. Failure deletes private staging, repeated names never overwrite edited copies, and output exposes only the work path.

## Lifetime
Cleanup removes work copies, never original inputs/images. Retained references permit rematerialization after cleanup/restart/compaction/parent deletion. Historical Fork inherits refs only through its canonical cut and separately copies current scratch/staging. Product settings/claims publish transactionally without another admitted-message map.

Files derives input/media pages from public windows with current product authorization. Last-reference inventory includes inactive paths/queued inputs but grants no read authority. External files/deliveries retain destinations and survive cleanup. Existing upload/media backup scope excludes disposable task files.

concepts.title: Flower backup and recovery
concepts.summary: Readiness drains generations while storage owners snapshot/migrate and Floret ends execution. Freeze Flower writes, verify collections and retain backups; restore history/settings/read-state/uploads without stopping other surfaces. Failures preserve recovery, never replay effects or roll back binaries.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Preserved snapshots
Ordinary startup, binary changes and transactional migrations do not create full snapshots. A damaged old snapshot cannot block healthy live data.

Abandoned task staging is removed only after any durable replacement completes and before a new generation opens; an unclosed generation prevents that path.

## Administrator recovery
Settings and the Flower maintenance action expose backup time, source build, size and protection.

Old unfinished Turns become terminal, old interactions become resolved and non-executable, and queued input remains canonical readonly `RestoredInputs`.

Diagnostics use the existing sanitized export and do not include conversations, credentials, database contents or uploaded files by default.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Only conversation-owned databases and uploaded resources participate in a restore. Environment extension configuration, including the [Agent Plugins registry and data](flower-agent-plugins.md), remains outside conversation snapshots and is preserved unchanged. Restore staging never initializes its plugin manager. Core Runtime services remain available.

concepts.title: Flower thread Goals
concepts.summary: Floret owns canonical Goal, model tool, reflection and completion; Redeven authorizes and presents facts. One current Goal/thread states intent without text limits or Todo dependency. Stop/navigation/recovery remain usable; unresolved requests never imply successful mutation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Compaction and continuation
[Manual compaction](model-context-usage-and-compaction.md#manual-compaction) defaults to explicit continue_goal intent. Retry and restart use canonical preparation and confirmed tools. Redeven forwards intent and renders state without a second execution coordinator.

## Goal ownership and execution
User and model updates enter Floret's shared journal writer with request identity and expected version. An existing unfinished Goal remains authoritative across continuation and context restoration.

Stop cancels execution and reflection; deletion only cancels future Goal checks.

## Interaction and recovery
Selecting or entering /goal opens an in-composer command chip.
The chip shares the editor's typography and first line box. Entering, typing a
single-line Goal and exiting preserve composer, footer and transcript geometry;
multiline text retains normal bounded autosizing. Native command conversion
synchronizes the editable value even when the canonical draft stays empty, so
the localized Goal placeholder appears immediately.

Each popup opening confirms detail through the existing read coordinator before showing canonical text.

A failed binding leaves the draft available for retry; no cross-thread target validation is relaxed and no attachment is uploaded twice.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Todo
Default Flower tools, capability lists and prompts omit write_todos and current Todo state. Deleting Todo later requires no change to Goal execution or interaction.

concepts.title: Flower managed runtime facts
concepts.summary: Floret v7.47.1 owns chronological admission, semantic updates, context messages, compaction and recovery. Flower only collects/presents authorized complete facts in four partitions: execution environment, date/timezone, repository rule sources and available skills.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Goal changes](flower-goals.md) use Floret-owned typed context facts, separate from the four product-collected partitions.

Skill rediscovery uses one authoritative catalog and deterministic text; disabled or newly restricted skills cannot reuse an activation cache. Loaded skill instructions remain historical model facts.

## Skill catalog and explicit reads
The automatic skill catalog contains current available names and descriptions in stable priority/name order.

Disabled, deleted, restricted, unreadable or invalid skills cannot return older instructions as current content.

Whole-request wire bytes and body tool-result bytes are reported separately by the regression tests; these are byte measurements, not tokenizer counts or production change rates.

## Snapshot lifecycle
UserInput.Context retains ordinary submitted facts and references. Automatic facts use ModelContextSnapshot, never historical free-text parsing.

No new thread, storage migration, historical text parsing, or product-owned snapshot is required.

Authorized canonical reads and the existing workspace subscription carry the same snapshot, record location, changed/removed keys and latest request use.

Subtask details use the same component and bounded detail cache.

## Presentation
One confirmed request supplies native input-token usage, visible Unicode character counts and recent cache rate as independent measurements. Missing historical values remain unavailable; visible characters never estimate or explain token differences, and no provider history is reconstructed.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Optional runtime configuration
REDEVEN_AGENT_AI_PLUGIN_CATALOGS is a runtime-process JSON array of {id, name, url}; unset/whitespace/[] means none. Example:team/Team extensions/https://catalog.example.com/plugins.json, never a default. Restart applies config. No official URL, startup fetch/search/remote switch/automatic enrollment.

Limits:16sources,1 MiB, IDs plugin-name syntax≤128characters, names nonempty single-line≤128Unicode, unique IDs/URLs. HTTPS host required; reject userinfo/query/fragment/unknown fields/malformed config explicitly. Network checks occur only when browsing through bounded public distribution.

Configured sources use configured:<id>/managed:true and memory only. User UUID/CAS sources retain independent 16 limit. Configured URLs take display precedence without deleting user records; removal reveals retained source. User APIs cannot delete configured sources. Config changes do not revise installation registry or alter snapshots/credentials/data. Desktop/Web use authenticated runtime routes; renderer-only environment has no effect.

## Directory document
flower.agent_plugin_catalog.v1 contains directory id/plugins; entry{id, optional display, source{type:github, repository, ref, path}}. IDs follow plugin-name syntax≤128; unique entry IDs. Limits 128entries/1 MiB, reject overflow rather than truncate. Empty[] valid; missing/null arrays, unsupported schema, trailing JSON/unknown top-level-entry-source fields reject. display alone allows discarded additive fields:single-line name/author≤128Unicode, description≤512. Render text only, no HTML/badges/credentials/configuration. Incompatible changes need a new schema.

Existing public-GitHub normalizer validates repository/ref/commit/path (default .). Different repository paths stay independent installs. Catalog identity/removal never changes installed identity/state.

## Browse and install boundary
Browse reads bounded JSON only, no archive/preparation/process/enablement. Install invokes the existing manual-GitHub preparation:resolve exact revision, snapshot package, validate real manifest/components. Preview uses actual metadata, not directory claims; commit binds reviewed digest/explicit selection. Listing/topic/manifest is no endorsement.

Fetch failure exposes Retry, not empty success. Unconfigured/unavailable/removed discovery cannot affect installed management/execution. [Extensions](../ui/flower-extensions.md) owns UI; [Agent Plugins](flower-agent-plugins.md) owns snapshots/permissions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Discoverable author guidance

The embedded `redeven-plugin-authoring` system skill appears in the ordinary
skill catalog. Its description distinguishes application plugin authoring from
Flower Agent Plugins and MCP configuration. It is loaded through normal skill
activation, remains user-disableable, and does not expand the global system
prompt. Its installation coordinate is projected from the imported ReDevPlugin
platform version before catalog, browse or model content is exposed; it carries
no independent version pin.

The guidance starts from the user's project and preserves its identity and data
contracts. New projects select the smallest released template that satisfies the
request. Pure Web surfaces may use declared private resources without a Worker.
Worker execution uses the published WASM toolchain and verified development
runtime. Missing platform or business capabilities remain explicit requirements.

## Released author workflow

ReDevPlugin 3.14.0 owns doctor readiness diagnostics, the shared generation,
typecheck, build, business-test and package pipeline, event-driven watching,
persistent development roots, manual update candidates, fresh session authority,
controlled connection review and runtime preparation. Flower invokes these tools
and uses their actual stage reports. It does not duplicate their validators,
watchers, lifecycle state or runtime supervisor.

Manual preview updates preserve the current frame and drafts while a candidate
builds. Applying or reloading creates a fresh frame and requires saved application
data for continuity. Failed builds preserve the last valid preview. Explicit
persistent roots survive restarts; reset is an intentional destructive action.
Configurable connections retain destination review, explicit grants and revocation.
Doctor readiness and business/package tests do not establish browser or real WASM
execution. Acceptance exercises the actual requested user journey and identifies
which boundaries were verified.

## Dedicated plugin drafts

A product draft owns one dedicated canonical Flower conversation and one opaque
platform author workspace. Ordinary conversations may be referenced explicitly;
they are never adopted or deleted with a draft. The ordinary Flower composer,
attachment staging, approvals, streaming and runtime dispatch remain authoritative.
Chat and direct creation are submission intents of the same composer. `/plugin`
is navigation, works before a model is configured, and does not become a model
turn when unavailable.

Draft turns and their input, approval, compaction and goal continuations use the
authenticated environment HTTP carrier, like draft creation and platform operations.
A synthetic Local UI session cannot authorize the managed author workspace or
replace a continuation's execution authority. The owner is the authenticated user and environment. Initial admission freezes the
exact canonical create request before creating the thread. Restart reconciles that
same request and binds its original thread; it does not replay the user turn.
The product resolves the managed source directory through the platform adapter.
Only that authenticated source is added to the conversation filesystem scope;
other projects, platform state and other task directories remain excluded. Adding
this source never replaces existing private task-file isolation. Ordinary file
and terminal tools use the same scope and existing effect approvals.

`plugin_author.status`, `initialize`, `build` and `capture` are available only to
the dedicated conversation. Build is a command-execution effect under Floret's
normal approval. The actual retained stage reports distinguish passed, failed,
interrupted and not-run work; packaging alone is not business or browser proof.

Product draft deletion first durably freezes admission, reconciles any pending
canonical create, cancels/deletes its conversation, then closes and removes the
platform workspace. Interrupted cleanup resumes its durable stage. Unknown formal
installation outcomes must be reconciled before author resources are removed.
Already installed instances are retained. Thread-list deletion uses the same
product review and cleanup path, with explicit copy describing the extra scope.

## Visual revision requests
Canvas comments submit explicit text and the reviewed artifact's bounded visual
context into the same dedicated thread using Flower's durable outbox. This path
preserves unrelated unsent composer content and retains normal uncertainty and
approval behavior. Dispatch waits for the ordinary handler decision and storage
generation; a blocked or unresolved handler cannot launch a comment turn.
The durable outbox retains rejected or uncertain submissions for the same recovery
flow as ordinary messages. The model resolves current source through `plugin_author.status`,
treats element text/selector hints as untrusted observations, changes the intended
source and runs the actual tests/build. A changed source may require reconciliation;
a stale selector never authorizes blind execution or installation.

## Delivery and installation

An authoring request may run authorized local project steps through normal tools.
Final sources and packages belong at the user's project or chosen destination.
Installation uses the released package inspection, exact-byte review and
confirmation flow in Plugin Center. Installation approval, execution grants and
automatic-update eligibility remain independent facts. Ordinary plugin packages
require no publisher trust or signature admission; platform releases and the
host-built runtime retain their separate verification contracts.

A plugin-generation handler must not perform a second approval wait, bypass
Floret dispatch, mutate Flower activity rows directly, or convert plugin audit
rows into Flower timeline state. An uncertain effect is inspected rather than
blindly replayed. A requested approval remains waiting until Floret resolves it.

concepts.title: Flower storage ownership and migrations
concepts.summary: Floret owns canonical Agent formats; Redeven owns product facts and uploads. Supported state upgrades through stable kinds, contiguous atomic migrations and public APIs while preserving history. Unknown, future, drifted or invalid state blocks Flower without resetting data or disabling the core Runtime.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Storage owners
Redeven consumes the exact published Floret version in go.mod with `GOWORK=off`.

Floret owns bounded startup recognition and background per-thread migration. Each validated dependency closure publishes atomically; retained sources retire only after complete verification. The oldest v2-v5 snapshots reserve historical identities through a resumable scan before new-thread admission. Segmented stores admit new threads immediately. Redeven uses public status, thread preparation and per-thread media contracts and never decodes upstream records.

Published Floret v7.87.0 removes hidden Activity field preparation from ordinary startup, retains summary metadata on large activity admission, batches explicit locator writes and skips same-value SQLite upserts. Its recent manifest cache is bounded, memory-only and owned upstream. No new host indexes, full-text indexes or duplicate conversation storage are introduced. First disclosure may still prepare the selected complete activity once; this is not a claim of field-granular cold preparation.

Cancellation, shutdown and execution-context settlement resolve canonical control records through Floret. The host keeps the original Stop request and does not read or reconstruct upstream conversation bodies to settle it.

A read-state failure cannot become a core Runtime constructor failure or a synthetic read record.

Redeven also owns the [Agent Plugins registry](flower-agent-plugins.md), snapshots and installation data. Its schema-1 SQLite store is separate from canonical conversation history; credential references resolve through SecretsStore schema 4. Neither owner decodes Floret records.

## Execution configuration
Product schema 11 to 12 adds bounded execution configuration to the existing
admission authority. It retains original provider/model and RunOptions for
continuations; it is not a second lifecycle table. Historical rows remain valid
with no inferred configuration. Floret owns host-work facts, final output,
notice admission, unknown recovery and continuation identity.

## Readonly checks and owner transactions
`sqliteutil` owns WAL-aware readonly preflight, integrity checks and complete SQLite snapshots for product and read-state owners. Inspection never creates missing data or runs a migration.

Required upgrade snapshots precede Floret space maintenance and all migrations, as specified by the [backup and recovery contract](flower-backup-and-recovery.md).

## Frozen historical queue conversion
The migration-only `pendinginputlegacy` package owns the complete interpretation of historical queue bytes: session identity, options, context shapes, default values, resource metadata and normalization limits.

The v4-to-v5 product transaction imports canonical pending inputs through Floret's public idempotent import API, records necessary product authority and removes retired source tables before commit. The upgrade operation contains only target build, original snapshot identity and completion; owner versions and canonical records remain the progress authority.

## Resource and authorization retention
Product upload references retain resources for every canonical thread that contains them, including ordinary forks, nested forks and restored inputs.

After activation, product recovery pages settings, retains each thread's complete descriptors and promotes eligible admitted input. Failures retain the cleanup gate while independent threads recover. Tool-media collection keeps its complete global inventory, write gate and idle constraint.

Bounded keyset maintenance and compaction stop and drain with their owning generation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Placement and authority
Runtime owns `<StateDir>/task-files/<ThreadID>/{scratch,staging}`; finals belong at the requested destination or selected project/worktree, independent of temporary cwd. Admission/provider context publish identical absolute roots. System placement overrides skills without filename heuristics or new permissions; source/tests/builds retain normal locations. Children get FLOWER_SCRATCH_DIR/FLOWER_STAGING_DIR, never FLOWER_OUTPUT_DIR; cwd/HOME/cache/TMPDIR keep normal semantics.

Private roots grant no sibling authority. Registry [filesystem policy](tool-permission-runtime.md) applies to every file/patch operation; cwd only resolves paths. Reject escaping symlinks/siblings without adding whitelists for authorized external/detached roots.

## Fork and recovery
Fork copies current scratch/staging even at historical cuts, not historical file snapshots; projects/finals remain shared. Block source admissions/cleanup, cancellably drain admitted work and reject unreaped processes. Rooted bounded copying preserves executable bits, checks identity/size/time/final tree, rejects unsupported types/external/hard links and renames complete private staging only.

Transactionally publish settings/validated canonical upload claims while retaining the source-deletion gate. Unadmitted copies stay invisible; canonical replay finishes preparation without recopying admitted edits/cleanup. Source markers support interrupted publication/context, survive cleanup and disappear on deletion. Recheck ownership before failed-copy removal.

Startup/periodic recovery scans 50 names/batch, skips in-flight gates and removes private stages/marked forks lacking settings. Explicit orphan operations share the target gate. Retry keeps canonical identity but copies afresh. Context maps ancestor suffixes, including nested forks; request inspection/repair of hardcoded paths without rewriting history. Ancestor cleanup cannot delete descendants.

## Delivery and discovery
file.present validates/hashes an authorized regular file outside application state, cancellably checking identity/size/mtime. Return path/title/MIME/size/SHA-256/mtime/endpoint and thread/turn/run IDs; never relocate originals.

Files discovers successful authorized Floret results (50 records/page,32 KiB/record), preserving Fork/restart provenance without crawling or another ledger. Available means accessible with unchanged size/mtime; history does not rehash. Changed/missing/unavailable are observations.

Default view is deliveries/uploads; Process files separates tool images/Temporary files without changing retention. One controller reads 50-item/128-byte-preview windows through empty/search results until cursor end; viewport end advances. Initial sources may parallelize, then serialize. Repeated cursors expose Retry; temporary navigation/child preview pauses discovery. No full View/retention scan.

Same-owner refresh retains equal/successful rows, focus and scroll. Thread/runtime change invalidates; close/change aborts discovery/previews/download reads and fences late replies. Partial failure keeps successful rows. Floe Dialog owns placement/focus/Tab/Escape/row restoration; close retains query/filter/scroll, folder handoff closes it. Env supplies rich renderers; Desktop supports image/PDF/text/Markdown and opaque-origin sandboxed HTML, otherwise Download.

loadTaskFile uses validated endpoints, reauthorizes each 256 KiB, rejects version/offset drift, caps previews at20 MiB and streams downloads. Desktop permits exact thread endpoints/query keys with IPC cancel. Browser Blob sinks retain their memory cost; reads never publish originals.

## Downloads and panel
Enqueue before destination selection in Shell Downloads: Env top bar, one Desktop full/companion owner. Deliveries/temp use validated chunks; uploads/images use attachment reads. Retry binds original thread/source/runtime; metadata stores no URLs/Blobs.

The manager owns progress/destination/cancel/failure/retry/completion. List/thread changes stop previews, not admitted downloads. Reopened lists consult active downloads before cleanup. Late settlement cannot revive cancellation; finalization cannot cancel. Native destinations offer Reveal/Open; identify browser handoff. Retain records until Shell exit/Clear finished, never import OS history.

Use published Floe controls/icons/tokens. Title/close in header, search/refresh in body; filters only for multiple known kinds, vanished selection resets All. No ambiguous totals, empty headings, collapsed images or manual paging. Delivered means file.present. Keep same-name image names/timestamps. Rows offer keyboard preview, origin/size, lazy thumbnails and exceptional availability; hide success badges/MIME parameters/IDs/absolute paths even in tooltips. Paths remain action inputs. Phone names wrap beside accessible download/folder/source actions.

Temporary files appears only when present, with Back/preview/confirmed cleanup; Process files has no blanket cleanup. Restore focus/scroll; active work/downloads disable cleanup. Failed pages expose Retry beside retained content. Only body scrolls in a stable responsive viewport; explicit locales and [loading continuity](../ui/page-loading-continuity.md#page-continuity) apply.

## Cleanup/deletion
List <=200 files after <=10,000 entries, disclosing truncation/lower bounds. Confirmed RWX cleanup pins Runtime-owned roots, rejects symlinks and checks opened identities; paths grant no deletion authority. Active/queued turns, interactions, admitted work and unreaped terminals block it through in-memory admissions/canonical View.

Deletion settles canonical work/stops owned terminals; force explicitly cancels. Resume from settings only after Summary confirms ErrThreadDeleted. Maintenance handles50 settings/pass with bounded waits, advances failures and retries next cycle. Clean files before product/child state; remove anchors only on success.

Cleanup preserves uploads/images. Deletion releases upload claims while canonical retention protects other queues/forks/references. Exclude finals; archival deletes nothing and has no TTL. Disclose project-local state.

concepts.title: Flower canonical thread queries
concepts.summary:
Flower exposes two read-only tools for finding another readable conversation
and reading its content: `threads.query` and `threads.read`. The tool contract
is intentionally smaller than Floret's published general query API.
`threads.aggregate` is not registered or dispatched.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Find, browse, read

- `threads.query` defaults to `object: threads`, listing recently updated
  conversations first. Optional `title` is one literal, case-insensitive title
  fragment. Optional `thread_id` selects one exact conversation.
- To browse `messages` or `tool_calls`, provide one `thread_id`. Records are
  chronological; there are no model-controlled sort keys or detailed filters.
- `limit` defaults to 50, with a maximum of 200. Continue with `next_cursor` and
  unchanged input. Pass a record's `ref` to `threads.read` for complete content,
  following its cursor until no continuation remains.
- Nested `filter`, message-body matching, argument/result matching, keywords,
  phrases, time/role/tool/status predicates, grouping and aggregation are not
  accepted by the tool schema or handler. Unsupported inputs fail explicitly.
- Reasoning, secrets and private provider state remain excluded. Tool arguments
  and confirmed results are available only through authorized content reads.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Authorization owner

Authenticated session authority supplies read permission, user, endpoint and
namespace identity. Redeven reconstructs the readable scope for every page and
read. Tool parameters and returned references never grant authority. Changed
scope invalidates frozen cursors; a new query starts under current permission.
The adapter uses published Floret public APIs and never reads Floret SQL or
reconstructs canonical records.

## Historical results and presentation

Saved query/read results remain previewable after restart and after their
original refs expire. The historical aggregate result renderer remains solely
for immutable already-saved tool exchanges; it cannot dispatch aggregation.
Private query contents are not added to Activity snapshots. The intent label
and explicitly opened, bounded result preview remain the presentation boundary.

## Storage and execution

The canonical owner stores source locators and metadata. Flower requires no
full-text index and schedules no startup or background indexing. Metadata-only
browsing requests one thread's ordered records; canonical full content is read
only as needed. Floret's retired optional indexing declarations are not a
product capability. The engine's published query API may retain compatibility
filters without exposing those filters to Flower's model tools.

concepts.summary:

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- File mode accepts file_path and optional target_id; locator mode requires a
  canonical media:v1 locator, excludes file_path/target_id, and reuses original
  bytes without reopening the source. Default behavior remains unchanged.
- Every permission mode checks image capability, CanRead, filesystem scope and
  ToolTargetPolicy. Unavailable explicit targets fail without device fallback.
- File reads and crop results retain their 10 MiB bound; Computer snapshots retain
  16 MiB. All reads are bounded to 16384 pixels per side and 32 megapixels. Tool
  guidance discloses these limits and the width/height/size_bytes result fields.
- Locator-only crop accepts integer x/y/width/height within original image pixels,
  never clips, and saves a new lossless PNG with source_crop metadata. It uses
  fresh canonical authorization. Image pixels differ from CSS action coordinates.
- image.read stores original snapshots, while every model input (including crops
  and summaries) uses [default model preparation](computer-use-media.md). Original
  locators remain available for detail crops; no durable derivative cache exists.
- Floret preserves every image in ordered summary batches; capacity failures shrink
  the same unconsumed batch. Current user images remain exact. Tokens and JSON bytes have separate
  limits; indivisible overflow fails.
- Switching to a text model preserves all images and presents verified metadata and
  locators through the [attachment manifest](flower-attachment-resources.md), without
  blocking selection or claiming that the model has seen pixels.
- toolMediaStore retains immutable images in computer/keyframes across source
  changes, Retry, restart, Fork and compaction.
- Previews check ownership/canonical membership directly. Markdown images stay unchanged.

## Maintenance and interactive writes

One in-process media gate protects writes and the complete canonical inventory
through deletion, following Floret's published retention contract. Maintenance
skips a held gate or queued writers. An interactive write cancels a running
maintenance scan and waits for that scan to settle; its own wait honors caller
cancellation. Partial or failed inventory never authorizes deletion. No second
membership ledger, detached scan, speculative unlock or input replay is used.

concepts.title: Flower MCP runtime
concepts.summary: Redeven configures MCP over official Go SDK stdio/Streamable HTTP sessions; Floret owns invocation/approval/effects/history/recovery. Add no competing execution or retry owner. Unknown outcomes are terminal without replay; invalid saved configuration remains unchanged.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Configuration and protocol
Standalone configuration lives at `<stateDir>/ai/mcp.json`, with schema version 2, one monotonic configuration revision, and server revisions for optimistic edits. Persistence failure leaves the in-memory catalog unchanged.

Catalog limits are 32 servers, 128 tools per server, 32 KiB per schema, and 4 MiB total persisted configuration.

Package-owned connections project from the [Agent Plugins registry](flower-agent-plugins.md). They use the same SDK/session and Floret invocation paths, with separate credentials and explicit discovery. They cannot be edited through standalone MCP writes.

## Standalone identity
Creation accepts an omitted local ID and display name. The runtime generates a cryptographically random lowercase ID with an mcp_ prefix, independently of the name or connection address; duplicate explicit IDs are conflicts, never replacements. Edits require the saved ID and revision. Missing IDs with a nonzero revision fail without creating another connection. Existing IDs and exact-ID Skill dependency matching remain unchanged.

For new unnamed connections, use the HTTP hostname or local executable basename, then prefer serverInfo.title followed by serverInfo.name from the existing successful initialize exchange. Automatically selected names are trimmed, limited to 120 UTF-8 bytes without splitting a character, and reject control characters. Explicit names win. Edits with an omitted name retain the saved name, and checks never rename a connection. Disabled creation uses connection-derived names without starting a command or contacting the server.

Typing or opening a form does not probe connections. Failed discovery/persistence does not create a saved identity; retry remains an explicit user action. The persisted schema and credential-preservation rules do not change.

## Presentation icons
Save and explicit Check read `serverInfo.icons` from the existing SDK initialize result. Connection-preserving disabled edits retain icons; changed connection settings clear stale discovery.

Rejected sources receive the generated identity described in [the shared UI contract](../ui/flower-extensions.md#navigation).

## Execution and dependencies
Enabled, previously discovered tools join the dynamic tool surface before the existing permission filter. Their identity binds the exact server configuration and tool schema, so a changed or disabled configuration cannot execute through an old invocation name.

Enabled, checked configuration satisfies the catalog indicator; it does not promise current network reachability or bypass approval.

## Image results
Typed ImageContent and image EmbeddedResource blobs become immutable tool-media
attachments before the text display limit. Ordered text placeholders retain each
image's attachment index, original dimensions and canonical locator. Arbitrary
strings, structured JSON and resource links never trigger image downloads.
Admission bounds each original to 10 MiB/32 megapixels and each result to 64
images/32 MiB; HTTP SSE events allow 48 MiB for Base64 and metadata. The released SDK
retains its 16 MiB stdio frame bound; transport rejection is explicit and never
authorizes replay. Provider delivery uses the shared [model policy](computer-use-media.md).
If image retention fails after CallTool returned, the result records confirmed
invocation completion and unavailable output. This does not authorize tool replay,
including when retention observes cancellation. Already retained attachments stay
paired with the completed result.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
MCP tools are conservatively mutating and open-world regardless of server annotation claims. An MCP handler cannot run directly without that proof.

Server tool errors and known connection failures remain distinct from an unknown execution outcome.

concepts.title: Context usage, measurement and compaction
concepts.summary: Floret owns confirmed usage, pressure, bounded compaction and canonical installation; Redeven maps independent token, byte and image evidence. Full input and frozen attempt identity constrain measurement. Manual compaction is explicit intent, while unavailable historical evidence remains unknown.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Usage and recovery
### Evidence and projection
Lifecycle evidence may retain frozen trigger candidates, pressure and validated replacement. Floret installs complete actor-owned context before publishing its version. Changed context bypasses text cadence; equal snapshots coalesce text in bounded queues. Redeven neither accumulates usage nor reconstructs lifecycle facts, invents budgets or infers capacity from weights.

### Independent capacity evidence
Published Floret v7.94.0 supplies optional typed request-byte and image-capacity evidence alongside
compaction decisions. Host preparation failures include exact actual/limit byte
counts; server HTTP 413 carries no guessed counts. Both can occur while the last
measured token ratio is low. The indicator retains that confirmed ratio, while
the divider explains the independent capacity cause and message-text estimate.
Cause-only events, reloads and Desktop RPC retain this distinction. Historical
records without this evidence remain unknown; no error-text inference is used.

Aggregate image evidence carries exact image counts or decoded bytes, with
preparation/response stage; counts never occupy byte or token fields. Desktop
RPC v6 reconstructs the typed upstream cause before Engine recovery; older peers
are rejected at the version handshake. During recovery
the inline divider says “Organizing image history…” in every shipped locale and
shows measured cause details. Token utilization remains independently measured.

Floret owns bounded recovery, complete ordered image-summary batching, protected
current inputs and replacement validation. A failed/cancelled summary never
installs a partial checkpoint, and completed tools are never replayed. Schema 34
migration belongs exclusively to Floret; Redeven never patches upstream records.

### Timeline
One row between short separators uses a compact surface-owned tooltip without expansion or reflow. Success labels canonical message text estimates explicitly, never as full provider-request input. Localize missing-count, running and cancelled explanations. Wrap original errors without clipping; localize the fallback only when absent.

The tooltip follows the active surface and global theme outside chat. Prefer above, or below near the top boundary. Delay pointer-exit dismissal for hovering/selection. Escape, Tab, blur and outside clicks dismiss it; the visibility owner closes it on process collapse. Retain keyboard/touch access and independent retry.

## Request measurement
Floret calculates pressure from a qualified native prefix plus the remaining frozen-input estimate, or the complete estimate when proof does not match.

Desktop RPC prepares supported provider requests on the credential-owning side and
returns the rendered estimate and fingerprint. Execution, output refits and retries
use the same frozen input. DeepSeek prepares authorized images through Floret's
credential-scoped, expiring upload owner and reuses cached uploads for repeated
preparations. The Desktop bridge does not claim native usage measurement proof
that was not transferred and validated across the RPC boundary. Floret's logical
preparation context releases Desktop handles after settlement or discard, while
single-attempt close preserves replay for as long as that context remains active.
Floret v7.107.4 verifies saved DeepSeek assistant boundaries even inside
Runtime-grouped messages when Retry follows retained reasoning with a new tool
call. Desktop forwards opaque state unchanged; confirmed effects and native
history survive restart and Fork without replaying the tool.

RPC v6 applies one-part request credit, bounded response reassembly and per-request
cancellation. Prepared handles transfer ownership only after the client acknowledges
the result; cancellation before acknowledgment releases them on Desktop. A slow consumer cannot fill another request's queue or close the
shared connection; incompatible older peers fail the version handshake.

The 90% threshold and public output reservation semantics remain upstream.

Unknown gateways, hosted execution, automatic truncation and hidden continuation do not qualify.

Output refits and transport retries preserve the same frozen input; failed or cancelled attempts never supply committed response evidence.

## Manual compaction
Pure compaction ends after install/noop; Goal continuation prepares context and uses existing Engine/current review in the same execution. Floret owns Stop/Retry/restart.

### Explicit manual intent
`POST /_redeven_proxy/api/ai/threads/{id}/context/compact` accepts `storage_generation`, `client_request_id` and optional `continue_goal`. True selects `goal_continuation` only when Floret finds an active canonical Goal during admission.

Failure and noop retain their actionable error or result.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Floret owns summary, validation, convergence and installation. Never reclassify historical `/compact` output as successful compaction. [Cache counts and latest/cumulative rates](model-request-reuse.md#cache-usage-presentation) use confirmed canonical usage, not another host store.

Floret alone checks attempt identity, commits output, persists and revalidates measurements, selects pressure and executes bounded [compaction and recovery](#usage-and-recovery). [Request reuse](model-request-reuse.md) cannot broaden native coverage proof.

Floret exclusively owns canonical compaction and Goal execution. [Usage and presentation](#usage-and-recovery) maps upstream facts; [qualification](../operations/flower-compaction-qualification.md#compaction) defines isolated runtime and provider checks.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Runtime uses `runtime/model-catalog` and resolves shipped defaults on read. Identity-only unreviewed models require configuration. Cloud uses its catalog protocol without dispatch-time discovery.

OpenAI-compatible inventories use Floret's public `ParseOpenAIModelMetadata`.
Explicit endpoint limits, modalities, tool declarations and reasoning efforts
survive atomic snapshots and restart. Field provenance separates endpoint facts
from inherited reviewed defaults, so old snapshots still refresh shipped defaults
and partial declarations override only reported fields. Full unknown wire IDs
remain intact; complete serving facts enable only explicitly selected models.
A reasoning boolean never invents effort controls; advertised Ultra remains
capability-gated. Conflicting metadata rejects the complete refresh and preserves
the previous snapshot. ChatGPT, Google, Ollama and OpenRouter retain their own
inventory contracts.

Settings retain sparse user overrides, show unknown input capabilities, expose
the usable input budget and warn when a window override exceeds the endpoint's
reported limit. Reset restores endpoint facts. Refresh never silently changes
saved selection or manual settings.

Profiles separate selection, overrides, custom definitions and default identity from metadata; visibility changes none of selection, identity, capabilities or routing.

Flower groups icon/name rows by provider: inline title/search/close, icon tiles, selection outline/check and fixed footer. Desktop: viewport-bounded 17rem width, 20rem height cap, 24px minimum rows, 10px labels and 9px provider headings. Touch: 44px targets, 16px search. Preserve search, aliases, keyboard control, refresh and management. Hide limits, image/search capabilities, quantization and alias descriptions. Unavailable rows show brief status with tooltip/accessibility reasons. Attachment feedback requires checks or attention. Long names/headings truncate with tooltips; scroll vertically.

The shared Flower UI owns provider brand rendering in Desktop and Env App. Settings, provider dialogs and model selectors use unchanged, pinned theSVG assets recorded in assets/flower_provider_icons.json; checksums and licenses are verified by the third-party notice generator. Monochrome marks use the foreground color through an alpha mask, while color marks retain their original SVG bytes. Both Kimi connection types share Kimi; the legacy chatglm type displays Z.ai; custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints use the OpenAI protocol mark without asserting endpoint ownership. No host-specific SVG paths or runtime CDN requests are used.

Both `GET /api/ai/models` modes share unfiltered `provider_catalogs` and backend `provider_defaults`: capabilities, never account availability, even before setup. Settings/drafts remain editable without usable models.

A selected platform whose catalog is unavailable shows the localized model-check failure and recovery action, never the first-use setup welcome. Preserve draft and selection; explicit model-menu refresh recovers from an authoritative directory response.

`LoadForStartup` freezes supported legacy selections before service start; no discovery wait or current-profile migration.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Tool names
Redeven owns the canonical-to-callable alias table at its provider boundary. Internal definitions, execution, history and Flower keep canonical names. When serialization changes a name, the detached tool description explicitly maps its canonical name to the callable name using that same table. OpenAI Responses/Chat, ChatGPT namespaces and DeepSeek receive this guidance before request measurement and freezing; unchanged names, including Anthropic definitions, receive none. Prompts, user content, scripts, argument schemas and canonical records are never text-rewritten. Returned stream/final calls still map back through the registered aliases; frozen retries retain identical guidance. This requires no Floret API, storage or dependency change.

## Responses
Strict OpenAI rendering makes optional object properties required but nullable.
Only adapter-added nulls are restored to omission before canonical validation;
required fields, canonical nulls and false/zero/empty values keep their meaning.
The nullable property's description retains its original guidance and explicitly
says to use null for omission. Canonical schemas and non-strict DeepSeek requests
remain unchanged. This belongs to Redeven's existing provider-schema adapter.

Hosted search includes web_search_call.action.sources for Activity URLs; Qwen keeps its tool shape. Floret7.97.0 ResponsesOutput reconciles done/terminal. Completed reasoning ciphertext wins; fill only missing/null/empty from matching terminal item. Search done bytes win when only valid action.sources differ,never merge/overwrite lists; answer annotations independent. Validate terminal-only fallback; omitted terminal retains ordered done events. Duplicate done,identity/content/arguments/status/inputs/unknown fields/missing items/byte limits remain strict.

Redeven maps opaque SDK bytes/typed errors. CompleteWithDiagnostics returns safe paths,boundary,counts/chosen authority,never query/URL/values. Localize post-response.completed validation failure with exact copyable conflict detail. Attempt epochs identify requests,not failed retries. Validation never advances history,changes retry policy or replays effects.

Floret7.92.2 PrepareResponsesHistory owns OpenAI key/compatible/Qwen/ChatGPT replay. Hosted receipts,encrypted reasoning/functions survive disabled tools/search. Confirmed incomplete Responses keep snapshots for length continuation; failed/interrupted streams install none. ChatGPT rejects incomplete; filtering never advances history. Activity is not replay state.

Estimate full native input. Only explicit API-key OpenAI responses_continuation plus Engine permission uses response-ID/suffix; others full input. Freeze request/choice through transport retry; rejected IDs cannot drop evidence. Explicit config may choose full replay. ChatGPT retains namespace/OAuth/WebSocket/published state. Historical ID-only states retain opt-in but missing bytes unrecoverable; new states store full upstream envelope. Reader removal requires future-major migration,not v7. Changed prefix discards stale IDs/suffix; Floret isolates model/account/secrets. Manual Retry/Fork keep facts/tools,clear source state.

Floret7.99.0 CommitAssistant binds full text once before ordered functions. Hosted Activity boundaries are presentation. Old split bindings stay readable at saved prefixes; remap only native-proven whitespace coordinates,save next successful commit. Preserve search/reasoning/phases; changed content/role/tool/namespace/order fails without reset/replay. ResponsesHistoryError carries safe reason,zero-based record/canonical positions,counts/allowlisted fields via history_detail/Desktop RPC. Both hosts distinguish pre-network preparation/post-response commit,show details/manual Retry,omit irrelevant setup.

Floret7.37.0 owns append-only lineage keyed provider/model/reasoning/prompt/local-hosted tools/adapter/context policy/state compatibility. Flower uses saved Activity/neutral display,never unknown JSON/arguments.

## Measurement/recovery
Floret7.26.0 EstimateRenderedRequest owns Responses/Chat/Gemini signatures/Moonshot/Anthropic. Verified models use official vocabularies; unknown explicit multilingual BPE proxy. Server rendering may differ; no host calibration/preflight. Floret7.79.0 owns [measurement](model-context-usage-and-compaction.md#request-measurement),frozen-prefix pressure/schema28; [recovery](model-request-recovery.md) owns retries/deadlines/diagnostics/current feedback.

## Anthropic
Floret7.95.0 owns HTTP/SSE,frozen cache hints,authorized attachments,signed output; Redeven maps public Gateway content/controls/usage/events,retiring SDK route. Brand selects no behavior. Engine permits<=4 ephemeral cache markers separate from opaque state. Cache-off keeps signed history; secrets clear both reuse paths.

Completed output survives continuation/restart. Retry/Fork/compaction retain facts,clear source;never invent signed thinking/convert to answer. Frozen retries resolve no attachments,use new attempt IDs. Usage separates uncached/read/write; measured input requires complete partitions and no service-transformed hosted/signed input,otherwise estimated. Failed stream preserves billing without history advance. Structured HTTP errors/exact limits remain diagnostic.

## DeepSeek temporary images
Floret7.89.1 owns Files upload/validation/expiring reuse/accounting/frozen replay. Explicit official HTTPS root(/v1 allowed) only,one-hour expiry/48MiB request. Custom stays inline/32MiB. Runtime/Desktop each bound reuse by provider identity; endpoint/credential change selects new owner. Rotation uses HMAC-SHA256/random local key,not reusable plain credential hash. Reauthorize attachments each preparation;no host file-ID persistence/migration. Explicit missing/expired ref allows one upstream re-preparation; quota/upload/media errors never enter summary loop.

concepts.title: Model reasoning capability, selection and transport

frontmatter.title: Model reasoning capability, selection and transport

concepts.summary: One capability catalog and canonicalizer define reasoning controls for saved threads and immutable turns. UI exposes only supported intent and writes preferences only on explicit successful edits. Provider fragments remain reasoning, automatic title policy stays independent and loading never changes choices.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Runtime capability
### Capability and transport
OpenAI-compatible Chat reasoning is capability-driven. Redeven reads only response fields named by that result, emits their fragments as reasoning without trimming provider whitespace, and never treats reasoning-only output as assistant body text.

Budget-only and fixed-thinking models never acquire synthetic effort names or a toggle merely because another model supports one.

### Default selection
Default asks for the model's own reasoning behavior. Thread creation, Thread
edits, and every Turn canonicalize it once, in
`config.CanonicalAIReasoningSelection`: on a model without verified reasoning
controls a budget-free Default is the omitted selection and is neither stored
nor sent. Default with a budget, Off, On, and named efforts remain explicit
intent and are rejected for such a model; personal memory keeps no reasoning
choice for it. Clients may send Default without knowing the model's capability
and must not drop or rewrite it themselves.

### Settings ownership
Thread model, reasoning and permission settings are Redeven product state. Execution authority records admission permission for historical attribution only, never as live tool authorization. The configured `current_model_id` initializes future threads only.

### Automatic titles
Published Floret v7.26.0 owns title reasoning and output limits. They never change the thread's saved reasoning choice or the main response policy.

The [live timeline contract](../ui/flower-live-timeline.md) owns canonical title status, persistence, and workspace-summary presentation.

## Selection controls
Loading, reconnecting and rendering never write reasoning preferences. Explicit new-thread Off survives shared remounts/attachment preparation; a confirmed non-reasoning model clears unsupported draft intent.

[Preferences](../ui/flower-conversation-preferences.md) own explicit full-model-identity choices and budgets. Sending/automatic normalization cannot save them; preference failure reports separately without rolling back confirmed thread settings or changing retry snapshots. One localized ordered option list serves all controls; explicit Default remains distinct.

| Capability | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean | Default, supported Off, On |
| Named efforts | Default, supported Off, declared levels only |
| Token budget | Bounded input; clearing removes override |
| Fixed thinking | Noninteractive Always on |
| Unknown thinking controls | Noninteractive Model controlled with explanation |
| No reasoning | No control |

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The same capability and selection reach direct Environment models and Desktop model-source RPC. A model rename never changes its declared control type. Existing database migration lineages remain unchanged.

This is shared Redeven UI policy, not a Floret API or a second preference store. Runtime continuation uses the [immutable Turn surface](floret-thread-runtime.md); no reasoning override is added to an input answer.

concepts.title: Model request recovery
concepts.summary: Floret owns retry admission, physical-request deadlines and attempt identity. Redeven supplies protocol facts through one adapter and displays the authoritative current view. Frozen input, confirmed tool exchanges and user cancellation retain their existing authority across transport recovery.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Published Floret v7.58.0 shares provider.RetryAdviceForError across direct and Desktop paths. Adapters supply HTTP/stream/close-code facts; Engine owns bounded replay, cancellation, attempt identity and draft retirement.

Redeven neither repairs old cancellation records nor owns a second retry loop.

Adapter-owned response checks use typed diagnostic codes and reviewed constant
messages for output conflicts or gaps, tool namespace/argument conflicts, invalid
usage and native history preparation/commit failures. Classification does not
change retry advice, cancellation, response validation or tool dispatch. Original error messages and wrapped causes are retained separately from the
sanitized summary. Published Floret v7.101.0 owns the FailureDetails contract.
The authorized original field preserves complete HTTP/SSE bytes, messages,
status and native identifiers without truncation, normalization or redaction.
Bytes remain base64 in JSON; valid UTF-8 also has a readable original_body_text
view. Partial reads retain received bytes and explicitly mark incompleteness.
Request headers, keys and prompts are not collected. Returned evidence may
contain private provider content and must be rendered as literal text.

The Responses attempt collector normalizes failures before attaching transport
facts. Its versioned envelope preserves HTTP status, request/response identifiers,
terminal event, output index when known, and Floret attempt identity through
Desktop RPC and canonical failure storage. Logs serialize numeric timings and
only the safe failure classification, excluding original evidence. Restart retains the details without
replaying the request; older envelopes remain readable. Flower shows the safe
reason with collapsed, expandable and fully copyable original evidence. Display
and copy preserve whitespace; provider text is never interpreted as markup. Missing historical evidence is not
reconstructed.

Tool repetition diagnostics use only validated Floret ToolRepetition fields:
tool name, call ID, consecutive count, limit, prior feedback and non-execution.
They share the existing expandable/copyable error detail with canonical thread,
turn and run identity. No argument values are exposed. Historical failures retain
their safe reason without invented counts or claims that recovery feedback was
sent. Localized copy preserves saved-result and explicit-retry guidance.

concepts.title: Model request reuse
concepts.summary: Floret owns reuse decisions/canonical state; Redeven runs one prepared request/Responses consumer. In-memory transport reuse requires matching next canonical state and complete input. Failure follows ordinary turn recovery; supplemental context never enables reuse.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Runtime/Desktop epoch 68 and model-source RPC v4 preserve Floret's effective request reuse policy. Adapters cannot broaden it.

Full input always owns estimates and fingerprints.

Official OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions requests use a deterministic,
URL-safe prompt cache key bounded to 64 ASCII characters. Redeven derives it
from Floret's namespace and the provider, normalized endpoint and account
identity without sending those values in plaintext. Disabled reuse and
non-official endpoints do not receive this key. A key-format change creates a
new provider cache namespace; it does not change canonical conversation state.

## Responses continuation configuration
`config.AIProvider.EffectiveResponsesContinuation` is the sole provider-level decision. Complete canonical input remains available when the ID is omitted.

No gateway-specific retry or alternative history owner is introduced.

## Cache usage presentation
The existing context tooltip shows the latest completed request and cumulative session cache hit rates. Recent counters project Floret's canonical confirmed usage directly and clear with its existing model/compaction boundaries. Historical cumulative usage is neither rewritten nor backfilled.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
HTTP and WebSocket use one Responses event consumer and send at most one generation per attempt. Unsupported upgrade, recoverable connection failure, interrupted streams, missing completion and precise pre-output stale continuation return to the Engine's existing budget and backoff.

There is no persistent transport history or second retry owner.

OpenAI request settings, continuation state, and input prefixes use SHA-256 only
as equality fingerprints for in-memory reuse decisions. These digests do not
store or verify user passwords and grant no authentication authority. Credential
rotation separately invalidates the live connection before another request.

concepts.title: OKF bundle lifecycle
concepts.summary: Redeven builds its embedded OKF bundle from curated source files under the top-level `okf/` authoring root, verifies deterministic dist outputs under `okf/dist/`, and embeds the resulting bundle into the binary used by Runtime and AI features for local retrieval.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
`build_assets.sh` invokes `build_okf_bundle.sh`, which runs `cmd/okf-bundle` against explicit source and dist roots. The builder emits the bundle, manifest and checksum deterministically. Summary, contract, boundary and complete Evidence bodies are embedded as structured sections. Explicit Evidence opening returns bounded narrative text plus structured references; default Summary opening omits them. Authored source budgets still count every section; the contract/body budget excludes observational Evidence. `okf/dist/*` is generated from source and is never an authoring surface.

## Quality gates
Report mode exposes layout, indexing, summary, evidence, duplication, lifecycle and budget issues without blocking cleanup. Strict mode fails structural and source-integrity violations, overdue reviews, and source totals above the hard cap. Final integration runs strict content quality after source integrity and before verifying the generated bundle.

## Source budget
Count Unicode characters in every source Markdown file under `okf/`, including the index and log, after CRLF-to-LF normalization; exclude `okf/dist/`. The report shows total, remaining capacity and index/concept/log usage. Exceeding 900,000 warns; strict quality accepts exactly 1,000,000 and fails above it. A per-concept `quality_exception` cannot waive this hard cap.

## Review and log lifecycle
Every concept declares `lifecycle` and `reviewed_at`: review contracts every 180 days, active measurements and operational evidence every 90 days, and retained history every 365 days. Retained history also needs a concise `retention_reason`. Report mode warns and strict mode fails on invalid or overdue metadata; expiry prompts review and never deletes a document automatically. Keep `log.md` to compact summaries from the last 30 days after durable knowledge moves into its concept.

## Index and retention
Keep categories and concept links in the index; the parser derives each retrieval summary from the concept's `# Summary`. Prefer an existing concept, preserve only decision-relevant historical conclusions and counterevidence, and remove obsolete detail from the current tree so Git history remains the recovery path.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The bundle remains auditable only while OKF Markdown concepts are the sole authoring surface, source and lifecycle budgets are enforced through the shared parser, and `okf/dist/*` stays a generated verification artifact set rather than hand-edited truth. A `quality_exception` may document a justified per-concept length exception, but it never waives the source cap or other quality checks.

concepts.summary: Redeven exposes the embedded OKF bundle through read-only `okf.index`, `okf.search`, and `okf.open` builtin tools. Redeven projects bounded safe results into Floret v7.26.0 structured Activity rows, and the shared Flower surface expands those rows without reading raw OKF result JSON.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
Runtime OKF code loads the embedded bundle once, indexes root directory sections, scores structured summaries and sections in memory, and opens a concept summary or one selected section by id or path. Internal ids, paths, and unfiltered result objects never enter that display contract. OKF activity labels and operation values come from `ToolPresentationSpec`, so the Floret projection does not own a separate OKF display vocabulary.

## Tool workflow
`okf.index` browses `okf/index.md` as a structured directory and returns summaries plus section counts. `okf.search` returns a bounded short candidate list with query-aware snippets and the best matching section id/title; title and Summary matches outrank section body matches.

Evidence narrative participates in search and the section catalog. Explicit `section: "evidence"` reads its bounded body and references; `include_evidence` on another section adds only structured references. Default opening omits evidence content.

Models should follow `okf.index -> okf.search -> okf.open Summary -> okf.open section` and must not rely on snippets for detailed contracts.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The tools return scoped Redeven repository knowledge and do not mutate OKF source or dist artifacts. They must not be used for current news, recent public events, market or pricing facts, third-party documentation, external facts, or general web facts. Source-level conclusions still require file or terminal verification after OKF navigation.

Flash and both official aliases support images, while Pro is text-only. All support off/low/high/max and a 393,216-token output ceiling. Built-in search remains ignored by the provider. |
| Qwen | Qwen3.8 Max, Flash, Omni Flash | `/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions`; existing qualified search models use Responses. Omni Flash: tools, text/image input, text output. Qwen3.7 Max/Plus output ceilings rise to 131,072. |

| Kimi Code | K3.1 Pro / Highspeed, K3 / 256K, K2.8 Preview, K2.7 Code Highspeed | Personal subscription key; native /coding/v1/responses on api.kimi.com or api.kimi.ai. Six reviewed wire IDs; no custom aliases or thinking-off fallback. |

K3.1 Pro/Highspeed launched October 23. Floret v7.83.0 qualifies Moonshot catalog, output controls and reasoning/tool replay from the same snapshot. The downstream adoption test exercises its public gateway with Redeven capabilities.

frontmatter.title: Flower child runtime and parent event boundary

concepts.summary: Floret owns canonical child threads, reports and parent-scoped lifecycle events. Redeven projects bounded status and complete authorized handoffs without another store or scheduler. Child input and approvals remain blocked at their own boundary; labels and historical references never transfer ownership.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Child runtime
The `subagents` tool supports spawn, send input, wait, list, status, inspect, close, and close all.

Its flat provider schema describes conditional fields: spawn requires task_name,
task_description and message; send_input requires target and message; close
requires target; status/inspect require target or ids; wait requires ids. The
existing action validator also runs as a pure Floret decoder before resources
and effect authorization. Published Floret v7.107.8 owns bounded model correction
and omits rejected calls from actionable Activity. Valid argument values remain
unchanged. Child scope, stale targets, storage and permission checks remain
execution-state checks, not input correction or permission to replay effects.

The model-facing result keeps child identity, task name, status, current turn, queue count, failure and interaction facts. Display timestamps, duplicated IDs and counts, and UI action flags remain outside that projection. Spawn and wait do not repeat task descriptions; list and explicit inspect retain them. A preview is omitted only when the same result carries the complete handoff.

Complete handoff bodies bypass generic output caps. Explicit event reads retain their full page contract. Bounded-wait metadata derives from the original execution result, never its compact model projection. Wait returns on child events and includes available complete reports; inspect explicitly reads reports. Tool descriptions state input and output semantics without prescribing a coordination workflow.

Parent reports, lifecycle events, bounded waiting, and the compact event panel are described in [Subagent parent events](#parent-events).

item without creating a second parent confirmation. Child requests remain
blocked at their own authority boundary. The parent model can use completed
handoffs, perform independent work or explicitly ask for a dependency decision.
Unchanged attention is neither a timeout nor new progress. Parent UI activity
continues to derive solely from its canonical lifecycle; child badges retain the
real requests. Existing persisted parent requests remain operable after restart.

### Child ownership and historical references
Forks copy conversation facts, never child ownership.

Missing targets are presented as missing rather than completed or timed out.

## Parent events
Flower enables published Floret v7.49.0 parent events.

Floret atomically records references for completion, failure, cancellation, interruption, normalized execution timeout and input/approval attention alongside their canonical source.

The browser keeps only temporary reading/disclosure state.

concepts.title: AI terminal tool runtime
concepts.summary: Redeven owns PTYs and bounded output; Floret v7 owns canonical tool calls, interactions, effect attempts, results and Activity. One adapter authorizes execution once and publishes current views. Product SQL stores no parallel terminal lifecycle or effect recovery.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
[Task-file placement](flower-task-files.md) supplies thread scratch/staging through
child-only environment variables while preserving project cwd and OS temporary
path conventions. Cleanup waits for owned terminal processes to be reaped.

PTYs use Floret execution/effect identities. `terminal.exec` waits 5 seconds when `yield_ms` is omitted or zero; positive values cap at 30 seconds. Yield returns a running process ID without stopping the command.
Its model-facing description discloses the 30-minute command lifetime, explicit
termination and Service shutdown. Cancelling the initial exec wait stops its
command; cancelling a later read preserves it. It identifies shell reads/searches as the file
and discovered-rule reading path, and discover/select/exec as the browser preview
path. These descriptions do not change process ownership or permission.

`cwd` is the preferred working-directory field; `workdir` has the same semantics. When both fields are empty, the run working directory is used; relative paths resolve from it. Two nonempty fields must resolve to the same authorized directory, including equivalent symlink paths. Neither takes precedence. A conflict retains `INVALID_PATH`, with `reason=conflicting_working_directories` and `process_started=false`; rejection precedes host-work admission and process creation.

On macOS/Linux, one exit worker observes command exit without reaping, kills its process group, retires numeric signaling, verifies no live members within 2 seconds, then reaps and drains output. The unreaped root pins its PID through cleanup. Child cleanup preserves shell exit codes; only confirmed Stop termination means cancellation. Stop, input failure, the 30-minute limit and Service shutdown share this worker. Unconfirmed cleanup reports a runtime error and retains workload admission. Settlement stops the watchdog.

Long-lived commands stay foreground under the yielded process ID. Backgrounding and `nohup` cannot transfer ownership; escaping the PTY group/session is unsupported. Independent services need a managed lifecycle; previews use the managed browser. Names, CPU use and age never establish ownership.

`terminal.read` observes output after the caller's sequence for up to 60 seconds, returning early on output/exit. An expired observation retains process ID and cursor and reports `wait_expired`/`wait_ms`; `timed_out` means command timeout. Continue with the same ID and returned `last_seq`, without sleeps or command restarts.

Normal expiry uses Floret `BoundedWait`; Floret measures handler time and owns repeat protection. Immediate, failed, canceled and early reads gain no exemption, nor do neighboring repeated effects. No extra retry counter, clock, wake or durable ledger exists.

Reads are read-only effects: cancellation preserves process and cursor, then confirms the canceled result after observation returns. Execution/input retain shell-effect uncertainty rules. `terminal.write` bounds stdin; `terminal.terminate` kills the owned group and waits for reap/output drain. Thread Stop policy governs cleanup.

Read results contain incremental output, status, cursor, wait and exit facts. Command, cwd and timing remain in canonical Activity without repeated model echoes.

Browser payloads exclude local working paths, stdin, authorization proofs, and effect internals.

Completion Activity uses a separate preview selected from whole UTF-8 output chunks
within the 8,000-byte presentation budget. The full retained chunk sequence is
sealed independently. Preview truncation and sequence watermarks describe exactly
the bytes shown; completion omits command/cwd already owned by the invocation.
A persistence failure is logged immediately with bounded execution identities
and remains an error at shutdown; it never triggers effect replay.

sections.body: No authority barriers, admission receipts, recovery handles or projection-cursor waits exist. Reads never retry settlement. Open-detail polling refreshes bytes, never canonical status or provider dispatch.

frontmatter.title: Tessiven Flower tools and scoped Runtime operations

concepts.summary: Flower maps authorized code, configuration and Runtime facts into canvas versions. Resource discovery and explicit actions reuse original registries and executors with exact bindings. Missing authority never substitutes a local route, and unknown mutations require original-operation inspection before any new attempt.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Runtime operations
Discovery starts no process/business session and path refs grant no authority. Identity/generation changes or revocation stop input.

### Official surface
- `tessiven.runtimes` / `GET /_redeven_proxy/api/tessiven/runtimes` returns independent source availability and exact target paths.
- `tessiven.runtime.inspect` / `POST .../runtimes/inspect` reads status, bounded public diagnostics, or the original Desktop operation.
- `tessiven.runtime.action` / `POST .../runtimes/actions` requests connection or one supported `start`, `stop`, `restart`, or `update` process operation.
- `tessiven.inspect/action` retain the canonical canvas version, bound instance, and resource identity checks for Managed Services and containers.

No sibling module, replacement SDK, or product lifecycle queue is introduced.

### Source authority and discovery
Desktop registers its Tessiven host through owner-authenticated private Runtime control. Web Service, CodeSpace, nested frame, unrelated-origin and worker requests cannot declare a native source.

Ambiguous references fail closed.

### Connection and business access
Explicit connect reuses saved configuration and existing connection leases.

It cannot carry claimed permission flags, an arbitrary URL, another Runtime reference, or a process-lifecycle action.

Member removal and replacement retire the transport; no local or alternate route is substituted.

### Native lifecycle handoff
Process actions use saved direct Desktop placements and the existing [Desktop lifecycle owner](../desktop/desktop-runtime-process-lifecycle.md#process-lifecycle). The model cannot choose a download URL or release version; the existing release selector owns updates and post-operation verification.

Unknown connection outcomes require checking the selected connection in its native owner rather than retrying.

## Flower document tools
- Tessiven tools read the canonical schema, list/read/validate versions, save a complete new version, inspect explicit targets, and execute one exact bound instance when the existing permission and approval checks allow it.
- Read-only inspection of a missing, non-current, or unauthorized Runtime returns structured `unavailable` state without a binding. Unknown mutation outcomes disable another mutation until the original manager has been inspected.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
### UI and compatibility
The Connected environments panel and Runtime node entry use this same service. The Runtime Dialog is part of the loaded Tessiven page; opening it must not suspend the page or show its navigation loading placeholder.

Gateway v6 application access, Tessiven DSL, and persistent database lineages retain their current shapes.

Flower and the UI call the same Tessiven service; neither writes its database directly. Explicit connection uses the original native owner; missing authority never substitutes a local target. External and unmanaged resources support inspection and explanation only.
