concepts.summary: Redeven owns product visibility, policy, prompt and approval UI; Floret owns invocation and neutral tools. Current thread permission applies at the next boundary, while each admitted call retains its snapshot. Ordinary independent calls may authorize together; invalid authority rejects and dependent work waits.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Default tools omit write_todos; historical Todo remains readable. [Goals](flower-goals.md) retains independent ownership. Registry includes read/search/file/patch/terminal/web/OKF/interaction/skills/subagents/MCP/Floret tools. Bounded typed details exclude raw/status/name-only affordances. Target media validates MIME/size/digest; never persist image bytes in tool state.

Pure conditional-input validation belongs in typed tool decoders, before resource
resolution and effect authorization. Published Floret owns bounded correction and
paired model feedback; Redeven reuses its existing [child action validator](subagent-runtime.md).
Projector failures remain contract failures. Stateful permission, storage and
business failures retain their owner classifications and never imply safe replay.

## Diagnostic ownership
Classify owner-typed/cancel/deadline/filesystem errors; unknown wording stays UNKNOWN/source text. Keywords cannot infer resource, authority, retry or replacement args. Owners resolve authorized relative/home paths. Keep patch diagnostics; removing unused suggested-fix inference proves no model-quality gain.

## File editing
Redeven patch cwd resolves relative paths only; registry owns canonical/logical write policy, including authorized external/current scratch roots. Deny readonly/sibling/ancestor/symlink escapes. Target tools retain target policy.

Resolve symlinks/new-file ancestors before authorization. Ordered canonical resource sequence rejects swapped/changed targets. Preserve submitted paths and resolve at full preflight, each commit and Move source deletion; source/destination snapshots must match. This is not an OS sandbox or elimination of all TOCTOU races.

File mutation exposes only `file.write` for complete contents and `apply_patch` for contextual single/multi-file changes, creation, deletion and moves. There is no separate literal-replacement tool or execution alias. Strict JSON/routing has no input_format/patch aliases; model name implies no freeform support. Search original source forward with anchors/EOF/ranges. Only order failures may reorder uniquely exact/nonoverlapping chunks without anchors/ranges/EOF/pure additions, using the same matcher/plan. Preserve original arguments/classifications; ambiguous chunk requests unique context, provider still requests source order.

Historical calls/results stay immutable and readable. File/patch presentations retain canonical target navigation through typed presentation facts, without restoring a removed tool's registration, routing or execution.

Pure additions append. Untouched endings remain; insertions use first ending (empty=LF); nonempty updates retain final newline. Match exact, then trailing/surrounding whitespace, then selected Unicode normalization, first permitted match. Context copies source; insertions literal, no reindent. Add/Move may replace regular files; one operation/canonical path.

Diagnostics name order/overlap/anchor/EOF/context/duplicate path with chunk/body-line/search boundary/exact source line/remedy; never choose writes. Floret validates JSON. Validate all before writing and snapshot-check each commit. Validation failure confirms no writes; commit failures preserve completed operations/unknown effects without replay permission. completed_files means whole operation. Activity retains confirmed paths/counts/full actual diff; model omits full diff and may inspect content. A Move whose destination succeeds but deletion fails reports destination create/update against its prior bytes, not completed rename. Atomicity is per-file, not patch/Move. Published ordered-resource/EffectOutcome/PatchActivity owns authorization/settlement/persistence.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Tool names are not aliases for deleted knowledge-era tools. OKF is an embedded project corpus and does not access the internet; external, current, recent, news, third-party, market, pricing, and general web facts must use direct authoritative URLs or web search discovery instead.
Search and fetch are independently configured. Published Floret fetch guidance
describes reading a known URL without assuming search is available.

Flower must not infer remote execution from thread context alone; it can only claim remote or target execution when a tool result or Redeven product command returns explicit execution provenance.

concepts.summary: One process-local Redeven controller owns AI construction/retry/publication/leases/drain/close; Floret owns durable facts. Non-AI surfaces stay usable. Requests bind one generation; failed readiness returns typed sanitized state without partial publication or Store repair.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- Startup recovers unfinished replacements, opens the Floret owner with bounded waiting, migrates product data, activates and publishes. Floret's worker prepares historical threads.
- After activation, recovery pages settings by 200, retains complete media inventories and resumes eligible admitted queues. Per-thread failure cannot starve later pages; ownership review follows. Incomplete recovery gates destructive maintenance and retries next maintenance pass. Waiters retain their own attempt's result.
- Background phases cannot regress a published generation or unmount Flower. Orphan discovery updates degraded/retry state; successful reconciliation or explicit repair clears issues. Shutdown cancels/joins generation workers before storage close.
- Explicit asynchronous retry admits one startup owner. Replacement cancels long-lived generation work, waits for idempotent lease releases, closes once, then publishes the next monotonic generation.
- Unleasable AI routes return HTTP 503 `AI_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with sanitized state. Readiness/retry/stop and admin snapshot/restore bypass service acquisition. Incomplete provider leases release supplied resources and cannot report ready.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Authority
- [Runtime execution](containers-operation-observation.md#engine-execution) owns discovery, endpoint binding, typed CLI reads and normalization; [volume usage](#volume-observations) owns reference completeness and independent usage reads.
- Strictly decode mutations and reject unknown fields. Keep uncertain outcomes explicit. Server gates `/_redeven_proxy/api/container-resources` and `container-resource-operations`; disabled controls are only presentation.
- Renderer cannot construct argv, skip admission or mutate managed resources. DTOs expose typed redacted facts, excluding environment/label values, credentials, sockets/certificates, remote URLs and Compose paths. Terminal sessions retain Write/Execute checks.
- [Console](#console) projects established targets/capabilities. Direct engine reachability proves resource readiness; host-service management state cannot replace that probe.

## Console
- Persist only resource view/key per `redeven.containers` instance. Preserve target identity even for same-name resources. Existing actions reuse their source; creation uses the sole compatible engine or asks Docker/Podman within its dialog.
- One compact header owns refresh/Operations; Workbench suppresses duplicate title. [Operation observation](containers-operation-observation.md#operation-ownership) owns progress/errors.
- Compose input is 1–8 ordered absolute YAML paths, optional absolute env-file and at most 16 profiles, represented as arrays. No retired directory-only or lazy-picker alternate path.
- One `ContainerRunDraft`/serializer feeds existing preflight/hash/operation admission. Never persist environment values/host paths in UI state. Retain draft through preflight/confirmation; clear only on success or explicit close.
- Use sortable desktop tables, fewer columns in narrow Workbench and mobile cards/full-screen details. Missing/stopped/unreachable/denied engines show detection state rather than stale inventory.
- Keep restrained typography, semantic surfaces and brief bounded feedback; published primitives own menu/dialog position, focus and presence.
- The log toolbar stays at content height; its viewer receives the remaining detail-body height, with the existing bounded gap and responsive wrapping. Sparse or empty logs must not stretch the toolbar.

## Volume observations
References include stopped containers; sizes report occupied bytes, never capacity. Failed size reads retain inventory with unavailable metrics.

### Reference completeness
Volume inventory and detail return `referenced_containers`, `used_by`, and `references_complete`. The native console renders incomplete observations as Unknown and excludes them from both In use and Unused filters. A partial Used by view may show known references together with an incomplete-inspection notice.

### Disk usage
`GET /container-resources/volume-disk-usage` is an independent, Read-only, no-store observation. Unexpected layouts fail visibly instead of being interpreted as an empty measurement.

Disk usage never authorizes cleanup or overrides the reference preflight.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
`containerengine` owns execution/redaction; `containerresource` owns admission, locks, cancellation, events and reconciliation; Web Services owns its resources. ReDevPlugin has no Containers adapter/package/client/UI role. Host administrators own engine installation and OS access.

Floe owns reusable pickers/controls/icons. Redeven owns filesystem adaptation, product state/copy/placement/navigation; `containerresource` alone owns mutation/reconciliation.

Volume usage is an observation, not a capacity, quota, free-space, billing, or cleanup contract. Redeven does not infer safety from an unavailable size or an incomplete reference scan, and it does not bypass the authoritative mutation preflight when deleting a volume.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity/execution
Discover engines independently,one service each,no inactive-context scan/fallback. Share two-second command budget per engine; health reuses selected endpoint. Resource readiness separately bounded. Desktop requires selected desktop-linux/desktop-windows or exact endpoint alias; installed plugin proves no ownership. Use docker desktop version --format json,not slow status. Resolve Podman Machine before health.

Known management/health faults retain ID/implementation/config sources/actions. Missing CLI/permission/timeout/unknown is not stopped. Start needs stopped;Stop/Restart running;save-and-restart needs known state before write,plain save remains.

Lifecycle shares two minutes across steps vs ten-second queries/two-second discovery,parent deadline/cancel honored. macOS Start uses /usr/bin/open -g -b com.docker.docker then bounded poll;Restart stops first. Other platforms/Stop use official CLI. LaunchServices allowlists identity/home/PATH/temp/shell/locale/timezone/proxy/certificates,excluding Redeven metadata,Electron/Node controls,CLI overrides,secrets. Explicit empty env stays empty;CLI/probes unchanged. Launch acceptance is not completion;reload final state under lock. Never sudo/pkexec/polkit/elevate/change groups or socket modes.

Read-gated GET /_redeven_proxy/api/container-resources/services returns modes/source IDs;one engine failure cannot hide another. Legacy state→engine,client_proxy→docker_cli.

Optional `diagnostic` separates observed discovery/management/health faults from `guidance_code` ownership advice. It contains only phase, typed code and observation time; never stderr, paths, endpoints or credentials. Permission, missing CLI, timeout, unreachable and unknown are distinct. Only a health probe can report stopped; management failure cannot establish running state. Successful refresh removes the previous diagnostic.

## Interaction
One preflight confirmation names service/localized risk/impact/action,no retyped name/second review. Client binds name,server identity/authority/request+plan hashes. Cancel creates no operation;duplicates locked. Hide hashes/raw prose;history resolves names/localized errors.

Settings warns. Header aligns square outlined Back/title independently of description;touch>=44px. Refresh retains cards,animates indicator only,errors inline. Known Desktop/unknown health retains disabled Start/guidance until revalidated. Active divider replaces controls with elapsed/cancel/secondary history;no invented percent/auto-open history. Failure offers recovery;SSE/poll completion reloads service/Runtime.

Current health leads;active work retains locks/feedback. Terminal start/restart failure on running card and stop failure on stopped card clear live feedback;unknown/config failures retain recovery. Completed/canceled remains history. Current running cannot rewrite failed restart. History separates original result/error/duration from current state;no empty error or historical live timer.

### Ask Flower
Existing cards prioritize a concise localized diagnostic over management guidance. Permission/unreachable/error states and stopped services without Start expose only the Flower icon in the existing action row, with a localized Ask Flower tooltip and accessible name. Read access and a ready resource suffice to ask; asking performs no configuration or lifecycle operation. Active operation controls retain their owner. Existing header Refresh revalidates the same cards and removes the assistance action after recovery.

The action opens the existing [contextual launcher](../ui/flower-activity-companion.md#shared-input-card) beside its button in Activity or Workbench, with one removable/previewable reference before an empty editor. No generated question, extra sidebar or setup wizard. `container_services` accepts only `text_snapshot`: a frozen allowlist of environment/service identity, observed state, available version/rootless/remote facts, capabilities, configuration source IDs, diagnostic, displayed summary, management guidance and capture time. Missing facts remain unknown. Raw configuration and secrets never enter the snapshot.

The existing current-runtime target and server admission own authority; snapshot facts never grant access or authorize elevation. Sending projects the snapshot into the existing canonical text reference/model context. The optional service response and paired Runtime-served Env App addition leave Runtime Service/placement protocols, Desktop request shapes and database schemas unchanged; no compatibility epoch changes.

concepts.title: Container execution and operation observation
concepts.summary: Every container operation binds exact engine, endpoint and resource identity. The service owns admission through execution and read-only reconciliation; UI streams observe it. Cancellation is explicit, terminal uncertainty never replays commands and transfer counters report only measured download facts.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Operation ownership
### Admission and serialization
The operation key contains engine, opaque endpoint ID, resource kind, and canonical identity.

Reusing a request ID with different hashes produces an idempotency conflict instead of a second operation.

### Execution, cancellation, and events
The service owns an operation context from queued state through reconciliation. Cancellation is an explicit API action; closing Activity, Workbench, an inspector, an event stream, or the browser never implies cancellation.

Terminal errors use a small public taxonomy for storage, registry availability, rate limiting, not-found, and access denial; the drawer maps known codes to localized guidance alongside the durable timeline. Unknown codes use a localized generic failure; codes and backend messages remain diagnostic evidence, not visible UI copy. Timeout guidance acknowledges that host work may still be in progress. Desktop service cards direct users to its native application for setup/startup recovery and expose status revalidation. Service history shows state transitions without generic execution stages or a synthetic percentage bar.

### Authoritative terminal observation
After engine execution returns, the service reloads the exact endpoint-bound resource or relevant bounded inventory.

The operation is never replayed, regardless of whether the resource appears present or absent.

### UI observation
Inventory requests and streams are fenced by source runtime, endpoint, resource view, and request generation. A superseded response cannot replace current data.

Mobile and desktop expose the same state and cancellation authority. Service lifecycle feedback stays on its card; history is secondary. Polling terminal transitions refresh authoritative service/runtime facts even when the event stream was lost. The portaled history drawer owns its responsive container and independent scrolling. Desktop uses a history sidebar; narrow drawers place a horizontal history strip above details. Rows use stable operation IDs and pressed selection; polling preserves focus and detail nodes. Details separate identity, live cancellation, duration/current health and timeline. The active final timeline step uses a pending indicator, never a completed check.

## Engine execution
Observe Docker/Podman independently without probing inactive contexts or changing global selection.

### Execution ownership
Every request binds `(engine, endpoint_id, resource kind, canonical identity)`.

Observation failures are returned as errors and must never be converted into an empty project or a successful removal.

### Image pull observation
Docker/Podman pulls retain CLI endpoint selection and credential helpers. On Unix the dedicated pull runner supplies terminal output so Docker emits transfer counters; both output streams are read continuously with bounded lines and terminal controls removed. Ordinary command/log runners keep their existing behavior. Windows retains combined pipe output and reports only counters actually supplied by its CLI. Cancellation terminates the task process group; an executed pull is never replayed as a non-streaming fallback.

Downloaded bytes sum observed compressed download counters even while another layer's size is unknown. Total bytes remain unknown until every noncached layer supplies a total. Cached layers contribute no transfer bytes; extraction counters never replace download counters, and download completion does not imply extraction completion. Repeated terminal redraws for unchanged layers are suppressed. Error classification retains bounded trailing evidence, including containerd's unresolved-reference not-found response.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
- The database is operation evidence, not a mutation queue or replay journal.
- UI inventory and SSE consumers observe service authority; they do not own lifecycle state or reconciliation.
- A runtime restart converts active work to interrupted after read-only observation; it never assumes success or retries the command.
- The full native container ownership contract is defined in [Native container resources](container-resources-capability.md#authority).

Endpoint identifiers remain internal, and current endpoint resolution precedes each operation. Unsupported engine methods fail explicitly. Public DTOs retain the native resource contract's redaction and permission rules.

concepts.title: Database schema migration ownership
concepts.summary: Each repository migrates its own opaque stores. Validate full SQLite/WAL before readiness; contiguous atomic edges preserve records. Future, drifted, wrong-kind or unsupported state remains untouched. Failure blocks only its service without upstream repair or database replacement.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Redeven-owned stores
Each SQLite store declares a stable database kind, current version, supported minimum version, ordered `n -> n+1` migrations, an existing-schema validator, and a final exact verifier.

Migration and verification failure rolls back.

Host identity upgrades use their own private journal and native verification after Registry migration; no live-engine guess or database reset substitutes for resource ownership.

## Upstream-owned stores
Floret owns canonical thread storage and its schema lifecycle through the published Runtime APIs.

Cross-database atomicity is never assumed or simulated by copying upstream lifecycle state into Redeven tables.

sections.title: Boundaries

concepts.summary: Env App adapts Floeterm PTY facts and Floe shell, focus, selection and KeepAlive. Redeven owns views/localized controls. Session-keyed Runtime nodes survive view changes; visible panes paint independently while the active session owns input, search and commands.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
File preview defaults to main surface. Chunked history remains an atomic canonical-dimension snapshot; compound controls use Floe CSS.

## Placement
Published SplitWorkspace owns splits/adaptive layouts/docking/swaps/accessible resize. Split creates backend view; subsequent placement edits update it. Named independent views have thumbnails, layout/rename/delete controls and creation above Groups.

A session owns <=one view. Selecting it activates/focuses that view, even from standalone/another view; unowned sessions appear alone. Cross-view drag atomically moves membership, leaving vacancy. Pane/sidebar close terminates named session without deleting view/collapsing geometry. Only Delete view releases members without stopping them. New views create fresh sessions.

Footer layout targets current view; row picker targets its view without activation. Preserve members, unavailable sessions, vacancies, reading order and selection. Published adaptive options deduplicate balanced rows/columns/grids/four main directions for2–32 slots; disable standalone/single-slot pickers. Geometry gallery has Adjust layout heading, accessible names/current selection/keyboard. Resolve latest target membership on apply, never stale snapshot. Add only by explicit split/drag/vacancy creation. Split uses target group and verified local cwd or group startup directory; group/cwd remain independent.

Desktop begins at pane headers with preference-controlled Workbench indicators. Footer keeps layout/search/clear/settings/create; Groups scoped creation and overlay toolbar/drawer remain. Split/attach never globally covers panes. Environment/view changes fence placement. Mobile tabs do not rewrite desktop trees. No maximize mode; Alt+Shift+Left/Right cycles.

Pane chrome uses terminal foreground/background, not ANSI blue; sidebar shell tokens. Session tiles14px, fine borders/neutral fills; headers28px. Rename preselects existing name via Floe autofocus. Idle hover pointer; dragging grabbing. Sidebar close hover/focus/touch. Previews use foreground border/background isolation/contrasting fill; no shared geometry notices.

## Projection
One environment provider atomically revision-checks affected source/destination views. Edits survive acknowledgement; conflict retains draft for explicit reload/discard. Catalog waits for shell-confirmed access/current transport. Reconnect pauses requests, retains drafts and reloads after restored access. One lifecycle resets environment/permission authority; unchanged permission retains readiness/drafts, retired connections cannot publish. Edits await readiness.

Active view is panel-local. Import unowned legacyv1 local splits once, clearing only after backend acknowledgement. Missing sessions become vacancies without pruning geometry; close persists fresh vacancy IDs and keeps even empty view selected. Each vacancy offers localized creation/exact drag target. Within-view moves leave vacancy. Local progress/errors preserve failed-close session; empty selection never chooses unrelated session. Views never restart PTYs.

concepts.summary: Env App adapts published Floe UI/runtime/protocol, FloeBrowser projection, Floeterm terminal-web and Flowersec helpers. Manifest/lock pins define the consumed release; Floe owns asset monitoring and per-view recovery, while Redeven supplies authenticated product integration.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Pins: Floe Boot/Core/Protocol v0.97.1, FloeBrowser v0.1.28, Floeterm terminal-web v0.20.0, Flowersec Core v5.11.1. Floeterm supplies Presentation/session exports. Floe Select sizes option popups to their content, bounded by the trigger width and viewport. Floe SegmentedControl owns the moving selected face, perceptible travel, production-safe CSS time units, interrupted reversal and accessible labels for compact icon-only presentation. [Asset recovery](../ui/page-loading-continuity.md#asset-recovery) uses Floe monitoring and per-view isolation.

## Mechanism

CodeSpace, Web Service and service-template catalog modules own their styles.
Vite loads feature styles with their lazy page chunks. Resource presentation
components import their shared header stylesheet; the root stylesheet does not
duplicate these imports. Every document retains the enforced 122 KiB gzip
initial CSS budget, including Desktop development builds.

Floe owns instance-based context-source capture, retained reading selection and composable PromptCard toolbar actions. Redeven supplies semantic readers and screenshot authorization.

Floe owns logical-edge anchored-panel alignment and surface clamping; Flower opts into start alignment for a stable model picker.

Floe owns loading icons, intrinsic localized label space, persistent feedback and resolved inline-media viewports; see [layout stability](../ui/page-loading-continuity.md#asynchronous-layout).

Floe owns progress-shimmer paint scheduling during drag and resize. Hosts consume
its published CSS and shared interaction marker; they do not copy its animation
implementation or suppress model output to keep input responsive.

Core supplies Host Applications' remote pointer/input controllers with render-independent bounded motion and explicit local text composition.

[Flower citations](../ui/flower-citations.md#inline-code-references) owns citation presentation and browser acceptance.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Retain Solid >=1.9.17 and matching npm/pnpm locks/overrides for Seroval >=1.6.11, Zod >=4.6.7 within major 4. Solid alone does not prove transitive fixes. Tailwind Node/Vite 4.3.3 uses the current loader hook. ESLint 10 retains explicit ESLint 9 recommended policy with compatible Solid lint; Desktop tests use ESM extensions. Reviewed Electron/esbuild lifecycle allowlists match pnpm; deny other hooks.

FloeBrowser 0.1.28 bundles host/viewer/media collector at projection protocol 26; retain integrity manifest and verified licenses. Pin @rrweb/utils, rrdom, rrweb and rrweb-snapshot 2.1.7 alongside recorder/replay/types. 2.2.0 fails dynamic-frame input/projection and cannot replace that closed helper graph.

Redeven owns shell presets, permissions, credentials, path authority and placement. Upstream owns Floe tokens, browser DOM/media, Flowersec framing/recovery/RPC and Floeterm parsing/input/history/arbitration/geometry/Presentation/cursor/graphics/rendering. These reviewed coordinates do not waive other LGPL guards.

concepts.title: Env App session event transport
concepts.summary: One Floe HTTP proxy runtime serves each Env App session and all built-in/plugin logical event streams. Features cannot consume parallel native HTTP/1.1 slots, retarget upstream identity or create another transport. Session replacement cancels observations; stopping observation never cancels business work.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## One session and one request path
Product subscriptions call the Shell-bound session event reader. Floe Webapp's acquisition lifecycle opens a logical HTTP stream on the current Flowersec session and parses SSE with its shared bounded parser.

Session multiplexing removes those event requests from the browser HTTP pool; changing request priority alone cannot do so.

## Authority and resource lifetime
Local session issuance declares only Env App API and plugin API paths plus the plugin CSRF and expected-management-revision headers. Remote issuers must declare the same plugin request authority and upload cap in their signed scope.

Product code must not reset a successful response while its bytes are still being consumed.

## Observation and recovery
Flower maintains one workspace stream; thread selection never reconnects it.

Its transport and cancellation regression coverage remain intact.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: An observer cannot choose another upstream, session identity or native HTTP transport. Ending an observation does not cancel the feature's background business operation.

concepts.title: Flower startup and recovery presentation
concepts.summary: Both carriers project one readiness owner and typed Stop/Retry, retaining drafts/navigation. Close failure needs restart; contradictory facts are nonretryable. Initial content admits workspace, then refresh/reconnect preserves mounted state without another availability controller.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- Activity, Workbench and Settings share readiness. After Runtime readiness, retain Flower loading until the first authoritative list page or selected detail is applied. Confirmed empty lists admit; empty partial-ready envelopes do not. Remaining pages load progressively. Embedded conversations wait only for their own detail.
- Before admission, hide welcome suggestions, composer and stale reconnect banners. Initial retries retain loading; terminal failure stops the indicator and offers localized Retry/access/version/capacity guidance. Readiness HTTP begins only after the secure session connects; disconnect/relock cancels its owner. Connected slow readiness requests retain loading until response or explicit owner cancellation. Access revocation is consumed from protocol snapshots, so unrelated unlock UI changes cannot reapply an old failure. No raw diagnostics/error card or extra UI timer/controller.
- A collapsed Activity companion presents runtime preparation/failure and initial conversation loading/failure as one bounded status button, including the 24-pixel Terminal footer. Pointer or keyboard activation opens details without retrying or stopping work. Expanded details retain close, progress and explicit recovery actions. Readiness never auto-expands the companion; compact presentation derives from the existing shell phase and readiness owner.
- After admission, refresh/reconnect preserves selection, transcript, drafts and navigation with existing notices. [Message continuity](../ui/flower-live-timeline.md) also retains prose during growth/completion; body locators cannot restart loading.
- Historical preparation leaves the operational generation mounted. Thread-local loading/failure retains New chat/navigation; only oldest snapshot stores may wait for their identity scan before new-thread admission.
- Unconfirmed/failed/revoked permissions block mutations until renewed. Show completed/total counts only for known totals.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Readiness is process-local availability, never Agent lifecycle. [Generation ownership](ai-readiness-lifecycle.md) and [complete-set recovery](../ai/flower-backup-and-recovery.md) remain authoritative.

- `git.getCapabilities` advertises revisioned pages, path/directory status and stash-section diff. `git.listWorkspacePathStatuses` accepts bounded known paths and returns rows or directory counts without descendant arrays.

- Linked-worktree previews expose summaries. Exclude the root Git control entry only after verifying type, applicable exact content, canonical target and filesystem identity against the resolved Git directory.

concepts.title: Flowersec transport for graphical windows
concepts.summary: Flowersec owns encrypted multiplexed transport/backpressure; Redeven resources/authorization/routes. Graphical state, tickets, input, clipboard/audio/pixels/disconnect use native proxy; static acquisition stays authenticated browser traffic. No missing-authority or raw HTTP/WS bypass.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Env App resource-management requests, including the forward touch immediately before opening a graphical window, use its active Flowersec session HTTP carrier. Window creation must not reintroduce a raw HTTP step between session admission and the resource-scoped viewer connection. Missing session transport fails closed.

## One session boundary for every backend
The viewer's `WindowTransport` maps product paths into the published `flowersec-proxy/http1` and `flowersec-proxy/ws` stream APIs.

The product's native application attachment keeps a bounded event queue.

Generic Code App injection must not install a second transport on these marked graphical documents.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
[Web Center](web-environment-center.md) viewers use this same scoped acquisition/spend contract. Verified child origin and parent credentials come from the trusted proxy; raw graphical bypass stays forbidden. Backend-advertised media/input availability remains authoritative.

## Resource authority
Acquisition requires read, write and execute permissions and an active resource owned by the authenticated user. Its exact spend target identifies the window kind, environment, port-forward application and forward ID; launcher, Runtime and application origins must all match.

A view-only session keeps the full access requirement.

## Recovery and browser capability
Carrier failure clears the cached proxy runtime.

HTTPS or a trustworthy local origin is still required where the browser restricts those APIs; product code does not mark an insecure network origin as trustworthy.

concepts.title: Host application lifecycle and Linux instance recovery

frontmatter.title: Host application lifecycle and Linux instance recovery

concepts.summary: Viewing, sharing, closing windows and ending processes remain distinct across platforms. Ordinary controls preserve save/cancel; only confirmed Force quit bypasses saving. Linux instances survive clients and Runtime only while verified user, kernel generation and private display identity remain intact.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Cross-platform behavior
| Operation | macOS | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Close outer Desktop window / browser popup | Release this client lease; app survives | Same |
| Network loss, reload, second viewer | Reconnect same live app; stale input is revoked | Same |
| Release this client lease | End this capture/route; other clients and app survive | End this proxy/route; other clients and app survive |
| No window for more than 40 seconds | Waiting, with native menu/reopen | Waiting, reconnect same process without relaunch |
| Close last window | Viewer closes; app decides whether its process exits | Same |
| Cancel normal close/quit | Preserve application and save dialog | Same; ordinary control is Close all windows |
| Explicit Force quit in library | Confirm loss warning; exact AppKit instance | Confirm loss warning; exact owned backend and descendants |
| Orderly Runtime shutdown or process exit | Native app remains discoverable | Private display survives; new Runtime verifies/reconnects it |
| Running list | Regular apps in the logged-in OS session | Caller-owned Redeven instances, including detached/windowless apps |
| Host reboot / display server destruction / OS cleanup | No survival guarantee | Same; Runtime cgroup cleanup may also end its virtual display |

### Accepted operations and visible state
Quit and force-quit requests are asynchronous. The Host Applications surface must close the confirmation dialog after acceptance and show a per-application pending state until the authoritative running snapshot confirms the target instance is gone.

The first Force quit action only enters that state; only its final confirmation sends the destructive host request.

## Linux recovery
- Instance records bind opaque ID, authorized owner, metadata, boot/PID/start, component identity and private backend endpoint. Reusable window IDs never grant authority.
- Upstream supervises GIO/descendant/sandbox lifetime. Preparation, launcher failure, app exit, windows and first pixels are separate facts. Xpra retains published readiness/final-window/audio-disable behavior.
- Browser profiles are stable private directories per owner/catalog app. Observed process-tree exit before first window fails launch even with zero status; live processes may keep waiting.
- Linux ordinary control is Close all windows, respecting save/cancel. Explicit force quit never follows close, disconnect, cancellation or uncertain response automatically. Acceptance is not exit proof; remove running rows only after kernel confirmation.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Linux cannot generically request AppKit-style application quit or reopen, nor adopt an arbitrary process on another display. macOS requires its real logged-in graphical session and explicit capture/input permissions. Neither backend can preserve an application after its OS or display environment has been destroyed.

Reconnect cannot restore destroyed display/OS processes or change ownership policy. Surviving-instance recovery never substitutes a replacement launch.

concepts.title: Host application keyboard, pointer and composition

frontmatter.title: Host application keyboard, pointer and composition

concepts.summary: Published Floe controllers own keyboard, composition and pointer gestures; product adapters bind them to painted window generations. Clients own IME and hosts deliver confirmed keys/Unicode. Cancellation releases held input without replay, while qualification distinguishes generated events from real applications/devices.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Keyboard and composition
- Embed published remote-input/CSS. Each backend has one copy/cut/paste handler, excluding duplicate IME submission. Flush pending pointer output before keys/text/clipboard.
- Native Linux uses authenticated published helper transport without another gesture/composition owner. Browser/OS owns clipboard normalization; confirmed Unicode stays byte-exact.
- Upstream owns retained Xpra capability, private environment, commit-only XIM, toolkit adapters, prepared client and scheduler. Historical preparation version alone cannot reject a viewer, replace modules or kill processes.
- macOS advertises `input_version: 1` and never switches global input source. Same-window recapture may retain focus but rejects input until decoded replacement pixels.

## Pointer gestures
### Gestures and event ownership
A touch begins pending, without a remote button press.

Both motion paths use the same target authority, microtask coalescing, explicit flush and cancellation; platform bindings must not install another raw-event listener.

Leaving the document does cancel.

### Scroll and lifecycle
A finger moving up or left reveals content below or to the right.

The Linux native adapter submits fractional CSS-pixel deltas directly; its gesture release callback has no remainder and never releases keyboard input.

Each viewer owns its controller, feedback and transient remainder independently.

### Acceptance boundary
[Validation](../operations/host-application-validation.md#historical-distributioninput) distinguishes generated browser events from actual native application receipts and physical mobile devices. Device emulation cannot qualify a real soft keyboard or pinch.

A gesture cannot cross painted-window or connection generations. Reopening a viewer cannot upgrade the still-running application's pointer protocol.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Viewer state
Use [Flowersec window transport](graphical-window-transport.md) for graphical state/picture/input. Reserve browser tab in initiating click, retain app identity through admission and use host launch deduplication for retry; closing pending tab cannot kill uncertain admission. Browser loading has no Desktop chrome/Node dependency. Pre-window launcher exit fails; a live slow process has no window timeout. Terminal records are bounded memory, lost on Runtime restart; expired routes reopen from library. Only confirmed final-window/app closure dismisses established viewing; empty inventory/transport loss proves no exit.

## Display and native streams
Published compositor owns Wayland/Xwayland geometry,resize and bounded family/popups; Xpra uses selected v20/v21 client. Native chrome moves/maximizes/minimizes primary window. Missing paint/close request/transport proves no closure. Request source density for Clarity; quality/HTTPS cannot recover absent detail. [Certificates](../security/local-ui-network-exposure.md#certificates) owns trust: viewer never creates/trusts certs,changes protocol,restarts Runtime or downgrades TLS.

Modes Automatic/Clarity first/Motion first/Save data persist through reload; same selection,locale/theme never reconnect. [Performance](../operations/host-application-performance.md) owns budgets. Published native library owns capture/regions/encoding/composition/cursor normalization. Retain complete cursor PNG/alpha/bounds/hotspot: longest<=24CSSpx,never enlarge small images. New shares use current resources without changing app identity; macOS keeps client system cursor. Only composed current pixels authorize input/ACK.

## Resources and compatibility
Floe owns immutable documents/assets/digests/capabilities; pin one per authorized Xpra share. New combined Linux sessions use native canvas/frame/input/cursor. Xpra pre-client inherits viewer's Flowersec constructor and fails without it. Retiring share revokes its snapshot lookup only.

Compatible viewers reconnect; missing/corrupt/unsupported resources fail preparation/Retry. Protocol<2 retains logical density with explanation. Unsupported input/pointer disables controls while preserving pictures/local UI; authenticated incompatible loaded modules need save/quit/reopen, never hot swap. Transient focus/context follows normal recovery. Quality changes use current authenticated attachment and cannot choose codec/binary/capture executable/install. Native component/decoder must share published SDK; no product codec/parser.

Resource origins must name active authorized share,never CodeSpace/unrelated/expired/unknown origins; no old application-HTTP-tree fallback. [Application authority](host-applications.md) owns admission/termination and [input](host-application-input.md) owns delivery. Geometry/resource notices grant no exit or first-pixel evidence.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Catalog
Catalog and session listing require read permission. Ownership comes from authorized session metadata, never a request-provided user ID.

Terminal sharing records remain bounded to forty-eight per Runtime lifetime.

Host Applications is available in Activity navigation and the Workbench launcher. A separate Force quit confirmation explicitly warns that unsaved work is lost; it never follows cancellation automatically.

Application inventory loading uses matching horizontal skeleton cards and respects reduced motion.

## Platforms
### Immutable launch plan
GIO resolves the authorized desktop entry. A sandbox launcher requiring metadata fails clearly when metadata is absent; a custom wrapper is not proof that the underlying package is supported.

The [preparation owner](#preparation) selects complete components.

### Private graphics and host services
Each instance owns unique private display/socket, authorization, runtime and bus resources.

It never exposes the whole desktop bus or arbitrary process management.

Support claims require real package and desktop evidence, as recorded in the [validation owner](../operations/host-application-validation.md#retained-xpraplatform-matrix).

### macOS initialization
The [native macOS contract](macos-host-applications.md) owns local launch, remote single-window capture, input, and graceful lifecycle. macOS 13 or newer uses the packaged `redeven-computer-host` helper.

A Mac without a graphical login cannot create a private headless AppKit session. Native AppKit applications do not become X11 applications by installing XQuartz, and Xpra desktop shadowing is not this implementation.

## Preparation
- `go.mod` owns exact dependency/toolchain versions. Never combine partial managed/system installations. [Applications](#catalog) owns environment restoration, private displays and dependencies.
- Status, explicit transfer-plan inspection and observation require Read. Upstream serializes writers with a private-root lease and owns scoped cancellation/idempotent chunks. [Desktop cache](../desktop/host-application-component-cache.md) owns cross-device reuse, seven-day/2GB policy and separate progress.
- Preparation names the selected app. Session refresh cannot reuse stale unavailable state or suppress its one pending opening. [macOS](macos-host-applications.md) owns helper/local launch/explicit capture-input permission and requires graphical login.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:

Returned icons remain bounded PNG data URIs.

Audio, microphone, webcam, printing and remote notification forwarding remain excluded.

Capability probes, not distribution names, determine Linux readiness. Missing support components block opening until preparation succeeds. macOS requires its native graphical session and permissions; Linux virtual-display assumptions cannot substitute for them.

Preparation never installs user applications. Closing a pending viewer withdraws automatic opening; unqualified staged bytes never activate.

## Independent execution
Host launches in its own session and process group. The foreground start contract remains: templates must not double-fork, background the application, or retain a permanent wrapper.

This is not a resident service supervisor or another binary.

## Native identity and recovery
The `host:v3` identity binds service ID, launch nonce, PID, and a digest of native facts:

New identities never use formatted dates, timezone, command text, or `kern.boottime`.

An old process's inherited output descriptors cannot be replaced externally; independent output handling takes effect on its next explicit restart.

## Opening and presentation
Host supplies verified native launch identity and executes only the applied authorized hooks through the common [managed opening contract](managed-web-service-opening.md). The driver stores only launch facts and after-start hook completion, never executable snapshots or a second entrance cache. Context cancellation and explicit shutdown enter the same serialized close path. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Discovery and input
AppKit discovers standard directories, running bundle paths and explicit absolute .app paths. Canonical path defines identity; localized metadata/system icons provide presentation. Launch locally through trusted Desktop Local or capture remote selected windows with host-application protocol2, separate from Computer Use. Verify returned bundle path/process and reuse single-instance windows.

Remote input shares the real foreground session: activate/raise the bound window, verify foreground/focused AX window/pointer hit ownership before injection. Local focus during recapture grants no remote authority; pre-frame composition never becomes authorized by waiting.

## Helper
One lazy Manager-owned Swift process serves Runtime catalog/app/desktop channels, not one persistent helper per app. Empty inventory leaves it idle until Runtime closes, retaining ScreenCaptureKit identity. Released FloeNativeDesktop owns capture/native desktop input; separate binary media pipe and bounded per-channel queues avoid control serialization. Each response queue holds128 messages for supported result bursts. Authorization, input and frame credit stay independent; suspending one capture cannot affect another. Helper failure ends sharing, never apps; later explicit open may recover under native validation. Shutdown preserves unsaved applications.

## Management
AppKit's Running applications includes regular processes launched outside Redeven and windowless apps. Requests bind selected bundle plus opaque canonical path/PID/launch-time generations. Explicit graceful quit cannot force-kill/retarget. Acceptance is not exit evidence; stale/unavailable targets keep sharing and actionable error. Failed viewer admission never rolls back host sessions from stale catalog state.

## Windows
Native registry distinguishes present, unknown and confirmed-empty AX inventories. Live processes wait indefinitely for first shareable window; no first-window deadline. Client release during waiting ends the lease normally, not launch failure. Confirmed destruction alone starts last-window grace. Capture availability never defines lifetime: AX identity can survive surface replacement while input generation renews and retired callbacks are fenced. Launch/helper failures stay failures; missing pixels cannot turn confirmed process exit into launch failure.

Terminal reasons remain exact: application_exited=bound process exit, windows_closed=last shared window closure, sharing_stopped=detachment. Neither closing windows nor sharing claims quit. Runtime shutdown releases capture/route/input, preserving applications; new Runtime discovers them through OS, but sharing needs explicit open. [Lifecycle acceptance](../operations/host-application-validation.md#input-cursor-and-lifecycle-acceptance) separates recovery evidence from compatibility limits.

## Menus
Only explicit inspection reads the bound app's AX menu; never on launch/first frame. Structurally remove leading Apple/system/cross-app branches before issuing handles, independent of title/language. Literal app name is first exposed group, no replacement system menu/warning. Empty/filtered/truncated containers never become executable leaves. Handles bind app and capture/wait generation; only enabled current leaves with verified ancestry execute. Removed/relocated/excluded/disabled/nonleaf/stale handles fail without pressing or disturbing app/capture. AX cannot describe every command's effect; local launch leaves OS menu unchanged.

## Picture
Native helper validates bounds and captures at min(viewer DPR,native window density,longest-edge limit). Settings never resize app. Preferences/stats preserve process/permission/input identity. Browser H.264 WebCodecs software capability may receive VideoToolbox hardware output; encoder unavailability uses declared JPEG, decoder failure explicitly renegotiates image transport. Unchanged resize retains credit; ack only decoded current-generation frames. Runtime logs connection-to-first-frame/generation; browser logs first-decoded duration. Limits such as60 FPS are ceilings, not achieved guarantees; latency/capture/encoding/decode/network constrain delivery. Capture failure keeps session recovery policy.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Requires actual graphical login, macOS13+ helper and explicit capture/input permissions; no private headless AppKit, VM/container/X11/XQuartz substitute. Protected/custom controls, separate-process dialogs and unusual window ownership need qualification. Build compatibility does not certify every OS/Intel/app. Viewer closure and quit remain separate authorities.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reporter and persisted detail
ManagedOperationProgressDetail schema v2 alone owns detail. Duplicate command IDs get deterministic suffixes. Failed uninstall retains records/output for [reviewed recovery](service-management-recovery.md#management-recovery).

## Service-row interaction
Page state keys disclosure by operation_id, never component/service-object identity. Rejected submissions retain local safe failure without backend operation or observed-state change. Compact status opens explicitly; failure labels/notices survive settlement and dismissal. Reduced motion removes animation, not readable completion hold.

## Install admission and handoff
Final install immediately closes the template drawer, clears collection filters and shows a request-owned row at the service's append position. This row is presentation only, never a fabricated ServiceView or persistent cache entry. A raw CreateResult binds its reviewed service ID to the real operation; slow collection refresh cannot hide operation details, cancellation or terminal outcome. Full ServiceView handoff preserves expansion and transfers focus only when the replaced row owned it. No management drawer or service window opens automatically.

Explicit rejection offers fresh review with non-secret inputs; secrets clear with the drawer. Ambiguous transport outcomes offer read-only request-ID receipt lookup, never blind POST replay. A missing receipt proves no rejection. Accepted work uses existing lifecycle retry, not new creation. Identity/permission generations fence late results; reopening a drawer cannot cancel work or let an earlier review overwrite it.

## Execution panel
Published Floe planes, ink, LinearProgress, StableText and presence compose a connected rail and fixed-height panel. Narrow rail reveals its current step without scrolling the page. Open details show commands/output immediately in one scrolling transcript; no secondary disclosure. Logs/transfer/stage changes preserve neighboring geometry and existing output nodes. Preserve canonical interleaved output order; follow only while already at the end.

Restrained transitions retain progress identity. Reduced motion is static. Open is natively disabled during operations with its ordinary icon and keyboard/touch/hover action-stage tooltip.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Release discovery
- Schema-v2 `ReleaseCandidate` carries source/version/time/channel, trust, compatibility, immutable identity, verification/selectability and installed relation. Verification cannot reorder visible rows. Cancellation changes no state; failed checks retain stale last success without blocking actions or toasts.
- Host npm declares exact default, HTTPS registry, executable, optional Secret token and non-secret environment. Tokens exist only in requests/task-owned `0600` npm files, never persistent state, argv, logs, hooks or plaintext cache keys. Compatibility/stopped-state checks remain backend-owned.
- Single-container OCI discovers its repository; Compose has no single release identity. Consume cursors only after successful pages. After a failed recommendation check, disable install until verified selection or closing the template flow.
- `managed_service_update_v2` is the sole old/target/phase journal; failure restores verified prior release/binding. [Version interaction](#version-interaction) owns selection, notices, stop guidance and handoff.

## Install release validation
Admission reads a verified, unexpired candidate locally and persists its exact identity. The background operation refreshes Registry metadata before runtime effects; changed/unavailable releases fail the accepted operation. npm verifies exact version, SHA-512 integrity and Node compatibility, enriches missing default integrity once and resolves the final runtime digest before launch. OCI validates tag plus pinned platform digest; explicitly reviewed digest-only verification persists `digest_verified` in ReleaseIdentity so a missing tag cannot silently change that choice on retry/restart. Later recommendations never retarget a saved install.

## Version interaction
- Installed version opens the drawer; never auto-select the first result. Keep service/current-version header, restored candidates during refresh and one scrolling viewport. Notices stay below the list without shifting prior rows; footer links to outstanding confirmation.
- Downgrades/unknown ordering follow Manager stopped-state requirements. [Operation progress](managed-service-operation-progress.md) owns completion/failure/cleanup without drawer polling or another lifecycle.
- Browser qualification visually reviews light/dark wide/narrow screenshots with notices, stop guidance, preparation/rejection and long translations; screenshots supplement assertions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Sources and launch identity
TemplateSpec 7 accepts exactly one entrance source: a fixed endpoint path, the supported Host opening hook, or `startup_url.line_prefix`. Container and Compose never acquire permission to run Host scripts.

Missing or rotated output and an absent verified record require an explicitly chosen restart to produce a new entrance.

## One preparation owner
`open-session` observes the applied instance, prepares its entrance through one common owner, checks endpoint availability, and revalidates generation, applied identity, Forward and management state before handoff.

List and inspection never prepare an entrance or execute opening hooks.

Changed business scripts and settings still require their normal lifecycle review.

## Browser outcome and recovery
`ready` means the entrance is ready for browser handoff.

Trusted IPC accepts only bounded replies from that same live main frame.

Per-service progress follows [Web Services interface](web-services-interface.md).

`scripts/qualify_managed_web_opening.sh` is the dedicated real-service lane. A failed Electron runtime preflight is an explicit environment failure; qualification cannot alter macOS trust or sign dependencies.

Explicit Import from GitHub/Check updates acquires templates only,never app packages/npm/images. Request-scoped private credentials,no git/background updates/lifecycle effects. Uncertain commit never deletes possibly active directory; retry receipts/startup cleanup resolve complete unclaimed directories. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- Load published redeven-service-templates before Registry/Manager. Recommendations default new installs; explicit compatible releases override and later catalogs never change installed identity. Failed creation removes only verified new containers, preserving data/workspace for review.
- RuntimeBinding v2/SHA-256 binds Host paths, Container name or Compose project/root. [Opening](managed-web-service-opening.md) separates entrance failure from health.
- ServiceView actions/status/primary action own presentation; old errors cannot disable healthy instances. [Recovery](service-management-recovery.md#management-recovery) owns explicit actions.
- portforward_registry_v2 schema 6 preserves v1 lineage: template/configuration/release/binding/digest, workspace/resources, desired/observed state, protected Forward/artifact/failures; no template snapshots/revisions/duplicate deployment. Schema 2 added ordinary-forward paths; managed open-session follows [session policy](web-service-browser-sessions.md#browser-sessions).

## Install admission
Preflight and Create inspect local template/input, notice, family, workspace and reviewed-plan contracts only. Create atomically persists service/forward/operation and returns 202 without Registry requests or Docker probes under the request lock. The operation begins at `release_validation`, verifies its persisted exact selection, then performs `environment_check` and runtime work. Failure/cancellation remains queryable before any workspace or runtime creation. GET `managed-web-services/install-requests/{request_id}` requires lifecycle permissions, is uncached and returns the durable receipt or null without executing work.

## Host release application
Update installs/verifies, resolves final installed metadata into one digest, replaces the process and health-checks before commit. Launch/journal/registry share the final digest; enriched trust creates no false pending changes. Originally stopped services return to stopped after verification. Failure retains rollback/recovery.

## Image pull feedback
Container pulls publish the executed command and ordered output through the existing operation reporter, including success, failure and cancellation. The reporter owns redaction and the 400-line/128-KiB output bound. Transfer rate derives from observed downloaded bytes over a short time window, retains the previous sample across sparse updates and decays when subsequent observations show no download. Layer completion is independent of byte progress.

concepts.title: Plugin background entries
concepts.summary: ReDevPlugin owns headless Worker lifecycle and durable intervals. Redeven supplies environment permission policy and presents verified status through ordinary plugin management. No hidden surface, host scheduler, replay endpoint or second Worker protocol is involved.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
A plugin may declare runtime_start, on_demand or interval. The first two use the platform background manager: starts are idempotent, scoped to the installed instance and environment, and independent of visible Activity or Workbench surfaces. Interval requires background.method.v1 and background.interval.v1, an explicit method and parameters, an environment-scoped job Worker, synchronous execution, no confirmation or preflight, a 1,000–86,400,000 ms period, and a 1–300,000 ms execution budget not exceeding the period.

The platform persists and claims each due invocation before dispatch. One instance runs at most one interval invocation; separate plugins remain independent. The first run waits one period, then each next run follows completion plus the period. Missed periods coalesce. Restart preserves completed plans; an unfinished claim becomes unknown and is never replayed. A later period is new work, not proof of the earlier result. Disable, uninstall, package replacement and revocation fence and cancel exact current work. Host close drains execution before closing state. ReDevPlugin owns contiguous control-store migration and unknown-outcome handling.

Redeven's background policy snapshots the validated runtime LocalMax intersected with the Env App application cap, then applies the existing method-effect rules. It does not depend on an online session, borrow a user's cached authority, or apply a per-user override to an environment-owned job. Admin and unknown effects are denied. The platform separately verifies owner, installed package trust, current grants, revisions, runtime admission and the durable claim. This policy grants no filesystem, process, secret or network resource: adapters requiring a live user session continue to reject background access. Selected-file and connection approvals retain their existing lifetime and owner rules.

An explicit install/enable action authorizes the declared environment lifecycle through the ordinary product review and platform APIs. Permission removal blocks future dispatch without changing the user's enabled intent. The existing disable action stops work. No separate scheduling switch is introduced.

sections.title: Presentation
sections.body: Installation review shows the localized cadence for interval entries. Method identity, exact period and execution budget remain inside existing expandable technical details. Installed details consume the authoritative background_interval projection: scheduled, running, stopped or blocked, with next-run time only while scheduled. A prior failed or unknown result remains visible without a retry button that could replay effects. A previous background diagnostic cannot override current interval status; separate process diagnostics remain available. Refresh uses the existing owner-scoped inventory path.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The platform owns durable plans, claims, authorization fencing, dispatch, cancellation, recovery and schema migration. Redeven owns only its product policy, localized review/status, and existing management controls. Business protocol state remains application-owned. See [Plugin platform integration](plugin-platform-integration.md), [Plugin process sessions](plugin-process-sessions.md), and [ReDevPlugin boundary](redevplugin-boundary.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- Startup reads the validated local cache without waiting for the market. Refresh uses ordered pages, one generation, complete inspection-derived previews, and atomic last-known-good replacement. No client capability headers, compatibility variants, per-plugin latest fan-out, or incomplete-entry fallback exists.
- Discovery uses the `redevplugin` GitHub topic plus rechecks of already indexed repository identities. A fixed-commit `.redevplugin/index.json` selects ordinary packages in independent `<release-key>-v{version}` namespaces. No developer registration, plugin signatures, publisher trust, declaration approval, or separate third-party client path is required.
- GitHub publishers are generated as `github.repo.<numeric-repository-id>` and plugins as `<publisher-id>.<slug>`. Authors choose only the slug. The released author CLI resolves the real source before building; the market and Host independently check that source. Forks receive distinct IDs; rename/transfer retains the same repository identity. Local/upload/direct-URL declarations never acquire GitHub provenance.
- Ingest uses the released verifier and rechecks repository, release, tag commit, asset identity and bytes. Reject cross-repository plugin-ID takeover and same-version replacement. Failed scans retain the last valid projection. Market schema 11 retires old non-derived current listings while preserving ingest/audit history; it never renames package bytes or creates aliases.
- Market retains one release per plugin/channel and bounded verified presentation/icons. It never proxies packages or grants lifecycle authority. Unavailable listings constrain discovery without revoking installations.
- Inspection matches publisher/plugin/version, package/security/contract hashes and repository/release/asset identities. Both classifications share review and commit.
- Installed presentation and permission requirements come from the installed package and Host-verified contracts. Newer market metadata cannot replace installed declarations or authorization facts.

## Network behavior

Market and package requests use the product network adapter, current environment/system proxy policy, and OS DNS/VPN routing. Startup stays cache-only. Singleflight, bounded backoff, jitter, cancellation, and generation reconciliation avoid request storms. Network failures cannot remove installed state or block ordinary Runtime startup. The service closes only transports it owns.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ownership and isolation
Every session binds plugin instance, user scope, environment scope, plugin invocation/session, and client key. Start requests contain an executable and argv array; ReDevPlugin never parses an implicit shell command string.

Secret references are resolved by the Host adapter and values do not cross the UI, error, audit, or diagnostic projections.

For one owner and client key, ReDevPlugin reuses only a field-equal launch request. It snapshots argument and environment collections before starting; later caller mutations cannot redefine an in-flight or running launch. Changed launch fields return a launch-conflict error. Redeven delegates this decision to the platform.

## Streams and lifecycle
The first contract supports non-PTY stdin, stdout, and stderr only. Each output stream has an independent cursor and bounded ring buffer.

The platform removes the session after close and prevents access after owner revocation.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ownership
Upstream owns validation/hash/source identity, inspection/registry, permission/confirmation, tokens/assets, sandbox/bridge, settings/intents, Executions/Events, storage/network/secrets, supervision/IPC/WASM, quotas/revocation, control state and releases/contracts. One coordinated release; frontend cannot downgrade independently. Manifests/dependency tests own pins; bootstrap retains bounded credentials before readiness. [Packages](redevplugin-package-lifecycle.md) owns admission/cache, [adapters](redevplugin-redeven-adapters.md) product modules/display.

## Availability
Plugin readiness cannot block Runtime/ordinary sessions. Market/package/runtime/storage/init failure stays local; retain files/terminal/Notes/Workbench. PLUGIN_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE executes nothing; rejected writes report not_committed. Localize faults; unreadable inventory is not empty, auto-failure never global interruption. Init budget10s; cancel fences results/closes integration. Error/panic unwinds construction without hiding host cancellation.

Channel auth is separate: failed/panicked binding grants nothing and cannot close host channel. Request panic releases admission; HTTP contains failure. Incompatible opaque state stays unchanged, never reauthorized.

## Network/history
ReDevPlugin3.12.0 separates routing/package verification/execution. Single-hop host transports honor explicit proxy,current macOS proxy/PAC,OS DNS/VPN for market/package/release. Synthetic/private addresses alone are not denial. Upstream validates URL/redirect/origin/size/cancel/hash; downloads grant nothing.

Granted HTTPS hostname connectors without private-prefix binding use released transport factory. Platform checks target/method/grant/revision,pools/quotas/revocation. Private prefixes,literal addresses/other protocols keep address-bound policy. Resolve configuration at request time; faults local.

Current admission requires Web v9. Existing retained records and data remain upstream-owned; no host compatibility parser, VNode renderer, invented declaration or package rewrite is introduced. Unknown or corrupt state stays unchanged and locally unavailable.

Platform owns Web admission/package modules/sandbox/bootstrap/bridge. Product allocates origins/mounts handlers; no DOM translation/VNode renderer/ambient parent credentials.

## Runtime build ownership
Product prepares complete Rust/C/archiver/link tools before exact published-source builds; [target build tooling](../operations/redevplugin-cross-build.md) owns pinned Zig, early real probes, cache identity, cancellation and Desktop package acceptance. Upstream runtime semantics and containment stay unchanged.

## Runtime performance boundary
Released 3.15 uses one Wasmtime actor/job path with fresh invocation state, bounded in-process compiled-module reuse, finite fuel and signed deadlines. Immutable manifest caching never replaces current permission or revocation checks. Product supplies fixed toolchain, runtime signing and placement policy; it does not add an executor, authorization cache or compatibility fallback. Cold module preparation remains separate from warm execution latency.

## Pure Web communication
Pure Web applications use native browser rendering and the released sandbox,
not a Worker forwarding layer. The default author template declares no unused
methods or intents; resource templates retain their own declared actions.
No registered Surface methods means no receiver polling. Removing the final
method drains already claimed calls and cancellation before stopping the receiver.
Opening, authority renewal, resource access and business calls remain separate
traffic. Zero receiver requests is not a zero-network or product latency claim.
Each simultaneous container owns a distinct slot, frame and origin. Product
qualification exercises private resources, sibling closure and fresh authority
through the published SDK and actual product routes.

## Authoring/execution
Platform owns config/manifest validation,bindings,build/test/package,diagnostics/watch,persistent preview,manual update candidates,connection review,verified dev runtime. Redeven version-derived skill invokes released CLI. Product owns intent/placement/review/install approval and build/signature/SBOM/publication proof; authoring grants no permissions.

Embedded creation uses the published `authoring.WorkspaceStore` and isolated
`authoring.Environment`; the product retains only opaque workspace, artifact,
inspection, installation-request and installed-instance references. Platform owns
source initialization, immutable artifacts, durable build reports, isolated Host
state, preview application and exact-byte inspection. Durable inspected installs
own idempotent request recovery and committed/unknown/not-committed outcomes.
Redeven must never turn a failed status read into absence or replay an uncertain
installation under a new request identity. Preview state and formal installation
have separate stores and grants. Deleting author resources preserves installed
plugins. Host-local source access is scoped to the authenticated draft and normal
Flower effect approval; it does not authorize plugin execution.

Preview refresh preserves selected actions and JSON drafts; pending work remains
single-flight. Unknown outcomes require explicit review and never replay.
Readiness resolves project-relative tools from the project directory. These
behaviors belong to the released author CLI; Redeven only provides its
version-derived instructions.

3.13.0 owns manifest actions/direct Surface KV/SQLite/files/settings without Worker forwarding. Dedicated-origin binary/WebSocket handler requires exact handshake; Host checks session ceilings/scope/grants/quotas/revoke. Product mounts/presents,never new endpoints/manifest interpretation. SDK conflict/unknown cannot replay; coalesced watches are not logs.

Private files1→chunked2 migration stays upstream, separate from control/author schemas. Snapshots/recovery opaque; no copied SQL/rewrite.3.12.2 retains ordinary packaging/SDK. Trusted parent query/event/cancel binds current surface gateway/plugin; pass exact scope via authenticated transport/released handler. Stale/malformed cannot broaden to management; plugin-origin direct calls denied.

Host enforces read/write ceilings/read-only effects before process operations. SQLite authorizes compiled SQL,excludes host paths,bounds values/complexity/concurrency. Product maps sessions/process adapters only; no new manifest/data flags.

## Visual review boundary
Opt-in context menus are a released ReDevPlugin surface capability. Bootstrap
collects bounded target hints and normalized viewport geometry; the SDK validates
current source/port, frame, handle, sequence and limits. Product owns canvas
annotations, artifact binding, comment text and Flower submission. No parent DOM
inspection, injected application bridge, permission grant or alternate dispatcher
is introduced. Visual metadata is untrusted model context, never authority.

## Open distribution
Ordinary plugins require no signature, publisher trust, registration or manual directory admission. Official/community is display-only. Released platform helpers own GitHub repository-derived identity; product validates market evidence using those helpers and delegates independent source inspection to Host. Authors supply a slug, never publisher registration or signature evidence. Local/upload identities do not confer GitHub provenance. All sources use inspection, exact consent, durable receipts and independent permissions. Product update scheduling uses the current authenticated session and upstream automatic-eligibility rules; it adds no host install state machine. Signed platform releases, product runtime identity and signed runtime leases remain separate platform/product protections.

Redeven supplies authenticated product policy and a single review experience for market, GitHub, HTTPS, uploaded and generated packages. Installation does not grant permissions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Inspection and installation

The Host validates ordinary package structure, hashes, manifest, capability contracts and source policy. Plugin signatures, publisher trust, signed release references, and official-only admission do not participate. GitHub repositories may expose several plugins through `.redevplugin/index.json`; the user selects a plugin before inspection. A package URL or upload uses the same inspection contract.

Review binds exact inspected bytes, intended instance/revision, owner and session. Submission uses one request ID and the released durable `StartInspectedInstall` API. A lost response queries that same request; it never invents a replacement operation. The Shell restores owner-scoped receipts, including first-install failures with no inventory row. Closing Plugin Center does not stop observation; changing the authenticated owner cancels and clears it.

Execution status and mutation outcome are distinct. A committed outcome requires inventory reconciliation even if final execution reports failure. Unknown outcomes stay read-only. A definite failure requires a fresh review; the UI never silently erases retained data, grants access, or retries uncertain effects. Installation enables the plugin while missing grants remain separate action-level authorization boundaries.

## Updates

Manual checks inspect the installed original source. GitHub provenance uses immutable repository identity, not a mutable owner/name or a market replacement. Source changes require explicit consent. Older versions use the separate downgrade lifecycle; same-version changed bytes are rejected. A market disappearance does not change installed authority.

Automatic updates are an explicit per-installation preference, off by default. While an authorized session is active, Redeven checks enabled installations after a bounded delay and at bounded intervals. It uses the same original-source inspection and durable installation path, only when the Host reports automatic eligibility: a higher version, same source and unchanged security declarations. New capabilities require manual review. Uploaded packages have no automatic remote source. No synthetic session, unattended host scheduler, or new product persistence entity is introduced.

Before automatic submission, owner-scoped durable receipts are reconciled. Pending or unknown operations prevent replay; a previous failed attempt at the same candidate requires review. Surface shutdown and inventory reconciliation use the existing placement coordinator. Neither automatic nor manual update grants permissions or overrides user-disabled state.

## Retained data and downgrade

The released Host owns target-filtered retained-data discovery, exact inspection, one-shot recovery and read-only reconciliation. Recovery binds owner, publisher/plugin, data shape, generation, management revision and active fingerprint. Atomic generation swaps preserve prior data and do not restore grants, secrets or enabled state. Discovery/inspection/status require Read; commit requires Write; disable requires Admin.

Declared data conversion runs in isolated bounded generations. Failure/cancellation preserves old bytes; committed/unknown outcomes reconcile without replay. Downgrade restores the exact historical package's retained generation. Redeven never copies opaque data, interprets converter code, or implements platform-store migrations.

Review shows concise saved-data impact and expandable verified differences. Permission grants remain independent explicit choices. No duplicate install wizard, dispatcher, package parser, or destructive retry path exists.

## Admission and ownership
`/_redeven_proxy/api/remote-desktop` is independent from application launch. Every session and forward belongs to the authenticated user; renderer-supplied identity never authorizes a route.

The same policy fences new admission under the manager lock, so an HTTP request authorized before revocation cannot recreate the removed desktop.
