macOS uses the exact remote Swift package in the existing Runtime helper.

The canonical official Alpine source remains the final fallback; every download still checks the expected size and SHA-256 before atomic cache publication, and a failed archive download can move to the next trusted source.

Capability normalization also applies to a retried connection after accepting or declining takeover, so a removed display cannot return through the stored request.

## Media and office interaction
Control and media travel through separate Flowersec native proxy streams bound to the same product attachment. Cancellation retires the selection and releases held keys; lock-screen input cannot use that text path.

Native session and frame authority remain governed by this concept.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- Use the shared monitor/pointer mark, distinguishable at Dock/header sizes across themes/high contrast. Keep diagnostic/retry after failure; cancellation stops only selected setup without reloading.
- SSH preparation, operation-bound challenge, progress and desktop opening stay in the same dialog. [SSH deployment](remote-desktop-ssh-deployment.md) owns admin scope/credential lifetime; opening the launcher changes no OS permission.
- Closing the launcher dialog through its close button, Escape or backdrop dismisses the view without canceling SSH preparation. The launcher retains one operation and progress subscription; its entry reports preparation, required input or the observed outcome, and reopening restores that state. Explicit Cancel still stops preparation and reports rollback. Dismissal clears typed credentials and withdraws automatic viewer opening; completed preparation offers an explicit connection action. Password and interruption challenges retain their existing deadline and require user response. Pending viewer creation is still released on dismissal, and environment navigation, launcher disposal or Desktop window closure still cancels its owned work.
- SSH host preparation presents observed checking, component, service and verification stages. The Desktop bridge forwards the published component media substate (`checking`, `downloading`, `receiving`, `verifying`, `installing`, `validating`, `ready`) only while the deployment stage is `preparing_media`; older byte-only reports remain valid. Component byte progress appears only during an observed transfer with a real total and received count. Integrity checking, unpacking, validation and packaging use one calm indeterminate Floe progress cue, so a completed download never masquerades as completed preparation. Avoid simultaneous spinners, shimmer and sweeping effects; static current-step emphasis and observed detail communicate stage changes. Interrupted or rollback states never imply completion.
- Preparation keeps a compact viewport-bounded content area while observed detail text and transfer metrics change. The seven-step list scrolls independently within a 128px maximum height, yields space to wrapped status copy, and keeps the active step visible without moving keyboard focus. Compact markers center digits and checks; the section heading needs no decorative activity dot. Status copy uses its natural line count with a small gap above the progress bar instead of reserving empty text rows; the dialog footer remains stable across preparation updates. The current detail is announced through a single atomic status region, the progress wrapper owns the accessible progressbar semantics, and the visual Floe primitive is decorative. Reduced-motion and forced-colors preferences disable decorative motion while retaining a visible state boundary.
- Authorization starts with one brief administrator-access sentence and a collapsed native permission disclosure. Full service scope and SSH setup details remain available on demand; the authorization selector and next action stay prominent. Authorization, password and result content use their natural height with an 18px gap before the actions. Constrained viewports scroll only the middle content area while retaining the host, steps and footer, including when permission details expand. Password focus reveals the field; stage-heading focus preserves the scroll position.
- Initial content is target/readiness/connect. Admin/display selectors retain native keyboard behavior/labels; decorative chevrons sit 12px inside the field with separate text padding and no pointer interception.
- Disabling approval reuse requests confirmation on future connections without revoking OS grants. Status refresh cannot erase connection failure.

- Only the owning root/main frame of an RWX-authorized SSH environment uses typed deployment IPC. Sensitive admin streams retain no stdout/stderr diagnostics.
- The upstream manager owns ensure/stop/uninstall and supported migrations. Unknown/future/unverifiable ownership remains unchanged. Service readiness, Runtime admission and capture readiness are separate; absent scanout cannot invalidate admitted policy.
- During component preparation, the published manager state is carried through Desktop as an optional, allowlisted `media_state` field. It is accepted only with the `preparing_media` deployment stage; byte totals remain optional and are shown only when measured. States after byte transfer describe verification, installation, validation and packaging work and therefore remain indeterminate until the manager reports readiness.
- Deployment progress separates SSH session startup, host inspection, service package creation, Runtime package preparation, per-file upload, desktop component preparation, service changes and Runtime verification. Runtime downloads and SSH uploads publish measured byte counts when available; upload file identities and transfer direction are allowlisted, and progress is throttled. Unknown totals and local verification/build work stay indeterminate; no percentage or time estimate is inferred.
- Before upload, one SSH batch checks the requested service, graphics worker, license and Runtime bytes against trusted package SHA-256 digests. The SSH identity owns a bounded four-file cache at `$HOME/.cache/redeven/desktop-transfer-v1`; entries are read-only and atomically replaced. Each hit is copied into a private transaction directory and its actual bytes are hashed there. Missing, changed, corrupt or unsafe entries are uploaded individually. Symlinked or untrusted cache directories fail closed. Inspection and publication each have a 30-second bound and accept cancellation; the UI reports inspection without fabricated byte progress or empty metrics.
- Cache reuse is a transport optimization, never proof of installation or authorization. Every connection still runs manager ownership and integrity checks, administrator authorization, actual Runtime admission, challenge/commit and rollback. Transactions clean their staging copies; fixed cache names do not accumulate prior versions.
- A kernel-authenticated root manager holds maintenance ownership. Unknown attachment counts on older services require confirmation. Stage cleanup is independently bounded; transport loss is not rollback proof.
- Linux login-screen capability failures preserve published, redacted reason codes across the native service, Runtime status and launcher. Stale compositor binaries after an OS update (`LOGIN_SESSION_STALE_RUNTIME`) and changed, missing, ambiguous, seat or TTY identities are host-action states with refresh guidance; unsupported desktops remain unsupported. The launcher never falls back to Portal or opens a connection while capture or input authority is unavailable.
- [Launcher](remote-desktop-launcher.md) projects one operation; operation/challenge IDs reject stale replies. Input release, takeover, viewer routing and local Portal/macOS retain their owning contracts.

concepts.title: Remote desktop viewer interaction
concepts.summary: Published input/playback and session contracts own current-frame authority. Separate cursors permit immediate movement; embedded cursors hide local pointer. Recovery keeps controls usable; disconnect stops media/input with confirmed removal or Retry. Frozen pixels never imply connection.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Lock-screen input
When a lock-screen frame is painted and acknowledged in control mode, the viewer
arms physical-only unlock input automatically. Paint and acknowledgement may
arrive in either order; both paths attempt arming, and subsequent acknowledgements
must not steal focus. The host lock screen remains unobscured, and a rate-limited
interaction explains the wait instead of claiming that authentication failed.
Opening a panel, losing the socket, changing generation or mode, and every
unpainted transition revoke the armed target. Backend frame, generation, control
owner and physical-input checks remain mandatory for every unlock event.

## Input and clipboard
The published Floe input and pointer controllers own client composition, physical keys, pointer gestures and release. Mouse and drag movement retains only the latest pending position, bounded to 120 submissions per second.

This desktop-only policy does not apply to host application windows, which use their own upstream cursor contract.

## Toolbar and window
Desktop opens an isolated owned window; browsers open a separate viewer. Ended sessions explain how to start a new connection from the launcher and never expose an ineffective Reconnect action.

The toolbar contains desktop-session controls only; it does not show a file-browser shortcut.

Explicit Disconnect closes that device; an enabled sound toggle must never hide a closed audio context after reconnect.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: The [connection launcher](remote-desktop-launcher.md) owns target identity, readiness, preparation, grant-reuse settings and launch feedback. The [session contract](remote-desktop.md) owns authorization, capture generations and native authority; viewer controls cannot substitute for painted control authority.

concepts.summary: Opaque single-spend control/data artifacts bind each Lease to a digest-global tombstone. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Before any remote data or control artifact can be spent, its Lease callback creates and fsyncs one no-overwrite ledger tombstone keyed only by the artifact's SHA-256 digest. Product channel, generation, sequence, and wrapper labels cannot create a second burn identity for the same opaque artifact.

A legacy local `Direct` config has no matching Portal-side durable sequence authority, so Redeven erases it into a revoked digest tombstone and requires relinking instead of importing it as usable capacity.

concepts.title: Runtime Service snapshot
concepts.summary: Typed Runtime snapshots expose protocol/version, compatibility epoch, capabilities, readiness and workload identity to Desktop/Local UI. Gateway attachment is optional routing, never a prerequisite for independent access or authenticated host lifecycle management.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Runtime publishes its own service protocol and independent component version. Desktop manages Runtime lifecycle through its verified target-host connection, placement bridge and lifecycle coordinator. Gateway manages neither Runtime processes nor their lifecycle admission.

Runtime snapshot fields and generated wire schemas change together; an unknown response key must not turn a healthy Runtime into a reconnect loop.

Compatibility epoch 35 requires both Desktop and Runtime to understand explicit reasoning `on` alongside the existing default, off, effort, and budget choices. Earlier clients reject `on`; ordinary epoch admission prevents a mixed pair from accepting a Flower or Desktop model-source request it cannot interpret. See the [reasoning selection contract](../ai/model-reasoning-runtime.md#selection-controls) for model capability and control semantics.

Epoch 59 pairs Runtime authorization requests with the shared Desktop and Env App OpenAI account picker. A saved registry requires an account selection or explicit new-registration intent; old Desktop clients must update before Flower access. Registration semantics belong to the [ChatGPT account lifecycle](../ai/chatgpt-account-lifecycle.md#account-lifecycle).

Epoch 65 requires the model directory's backend-owned default_fetch_source field in provider search policies. See [model web search](../ai/model-web-search.md).

Epoch 67 requires complete changed pin metadata in Flower pin confirmations. New pins append to the endpoint's existing order; Desktop and Runtime must agree on the changed ranks and revisions before a confirmation is accepted. See [sidebar pin ordering](../ui/flower-thread-sidebar.md).

Epoch 71 requires truthful per-attachment Gateway connection phases and a collection-only owner status API. Durable joining/joined/removal state is separate from live controller observations. A stopped Runtime cannot report a connected attachment. The shared projection, strict Desktop admission and independent Gateway epoch are defined by [Gateway interactions](../gateway/gateway-desktop-interactions.md).

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Portal control-channel fences protect Provider authorization. Gateway attachment versions fence only their corresponding attachment and transport authority. The Runtime Service has no hidden v1 lifecycle-owner fallback and does not require a Gateway endpoint, pairing, or operation store to start.

concepts.summary: Monitor owns one CPU/memory/network/process snapshot for page and Workbench. All OS-marked loopback interfaces are excluded from the shared network counters/rates. ## Sampling and presentation
The service refreshes system metrics every two seconds and process metrics every ten seconds.

Totals are not a persisted usage ledger and are not reset to zero when Redeven starts.

## Network accounting
Each sample reads interface metadata through Go's `net.Interfaces()` and individual byte counters through the published gopsutil per-interface API.

Interface topology changes retain the existing aggregate-counter rate behavior rather than introducing a second rate algorithm.

Existing client request errors retain their Retry action, subsequent polling, and cleanup on unmount.

concepts.title: Runtime terminal lifecycle
concepts.summary: Floeterm owns PTY/Ghostty VT, geometry/controller epoch, input encoding, history/reset and atomic Presentation. Redeven maps permission/session metadata/placement. Browser consumes bounded semantic streams without parsing bytes or introducing a second terminal state machine.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
The runtime wraps `termgo.NewManager` so one terminal-go `SessionActor` owns each PTY, native Ghostty VT, canonical geometry, controller epoch, input encoding, semantic history, clear/reset, and atomic Presentation.

Overflow fixtures may exceed the 8 MiB ring-buffer cap; they must recover the retained tail, preserve the stable renderer geometry after focus, and accept subsequent PTY input.

## Terminal startup and warmup
Env App hydrates one terminal session catalog after protocol connection, environment readiness, and process permission. The catalog owns canonical session metadata, notification convergence, connection epoch, permission clearing, stale-on-disconnect state, and bounded early latest values.

Diagnostics retain aggregate phase and field-presence facts only and never record session identifiers, paths, remote identity, commands, or terminal content.

## Native history budgets
Runtime persists `terminal_history_retention` with nullable `max_lines`/`max_bytes` safe nonnegative integers and applies those defaults before terminal readiness. Published terminal-go owns validation, native limit application, pruning, snapshot invalidation and atomic Presentation. Defaults affect only subsequently created sessions; existing sessions are never silently reconfigured.

`/_redeven_proxy/api/terminal/history-retention` is the product settings adapter: GET reads defaults or an authorized session; admin-only PUT persists and activates defaults; POST applies explicit limits to a session using its connection ID and transport generation. Session application reuses shell/container permission and ownership checks, is principal-bound, does not transfer controller ownership, and rejects stale attachments. Limits preserve process, live screen, geometry and content epoch, while invalidating historical snapshots through the upstream history epoch. No local implementation of terminal retention or RPC retry is introduced.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Terminal lifecycle depends on the published Floeterm and Flowersec interfaces. Redeven must not parse terminal bytes, keep another history, replay raw output, add browser VT/WASM fallbacks, or introduce a second attachment or controller owner. History and diagnostics remain observational and never become admission limits.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Published Flowersec owns Transportv3 connection/session/RPC/streams; Floeterm owns terminal lifecycle. Pins: terminal-go v0.20.0 and Flowersec Go v5.12.0. Env App and Desktop consume Flowersec TypeScript v5.12.0. Each Env App shares one current protocol session; switching thread/Activity/Workbench/terminal/file cannot reconnect it. Register complete AI inventory in direct/remote profiles before session freeze; declared methods cannot become router404. Stop is one RPC lifecycle command,no fallback.

Published WebSocketHTTPServerOptions.ApplicationHandler composes Gateway HTTP/Runtime on one TLS endpoint; egress.HTTPSProxy supplies explicit Cloud routing. [Web Center](web-environment-center.md) uses published controller/pinned RuntimeTLS/in-process Connector without new wire/replay. Desktop SSH placementHTTP2 remains separate. [Terminal](runtime-terminal-lifecycle.md) owns framing/history/attachment/warmup.

Env App adapts published artifact sources to exact origin/environment across HTTPS,explicit HTTP,Cloud/private loopback,requiring matching Service Worker control. Reconnect uses discriminated source contract. Map Portal uppercase codes to Floe HTTP classifier; emit canonical Flowersec codes retaining terminal/retryable/Retry-After authority. Desktop generation/revision fences stale updates. One immutable diagnostic view,no business-request replay.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Upstream owns acquisition/retry/framing/connection replacement; product selects profile/maps authorization. No prose classifiers,fallback URLs,second controller,TLS/private provenance bypass or background session renewal. Published interfaces must stay aligned for multiplexing,liveness,bounded RPC,admission,terminal Presentation/history/controller ownership. Diagnostics/session counts never reject creation,close PTY or pause sessions. Desktop bridge observations are not a second transport.

concepts.title: Service management recovery and resource ownership

frontmatter.title: Service management recovery and resource ownership

concepts.summary: Registry owns transactions, allocations and identities; fresh backend facts govern recovery and deletion. Names, cached reachability and uncertain legacy resources grant no destructive authority. Retain data by default, preserve unavailable facts and require reviewed ownership/consent before execution.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Management recovery
### Facts and actions
`ServiceFacts` separates presence, ownership, runtime state, inspection completeness, resource references, and check time.

Frontend code never substitutes Retry or Restart for unavailable Start.

A failed Host maintenance hook may be bypassed only through an administrator's reviewed plan, and only for verified resources.

### Review and execution
`GET /managed-web-services/{id}/inspection` requires read permission, is non-cacheable, and uses the same factual backend projection as the list.

Existing unrelated lifecycle transactions cannot be overwritten by recovery.

Instance-scoped allocation and legacy resource boundaries are owned by [Service resource ownership](#resource-ownership).

### Uninstall transaction
Uninstall uses `runtime_manifest_json`, the existing operation coordinator, and the existing event stream.

A resource recreated under the same name cannot acquire the previous deletion authorization.

Detachment remains available while it is unresolved.

### Management archives and access
Registry version 4 adds `active`, `detached`, and `uninstalled`. Only active records participate in template uniqueness and must own an authorized Forward.

Names, ports, or cached reachability never prove ownership.

## Resource ownership
### Instance allocation
New Host bindings use `instances/<service-id>/data`.

Creation must return the expected service, resource, and generation labels plus native identity.

Template permissions remain unchanged: unsupported external Compose capabilities are still rejected by template policy.

### Observation and deletion
Container ownership uses exact native ID, standard managed name, and service label.

Unknown ownership is shown honestly. Reference metadata exposes selected container identity, state, ports, and owning service identifiers; arbitrary engine labels and injected secrets never become public inventory fields.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The contiguous `portforward_registry_v2` 3-to-4 migration preserves bindings, configuration, private-file references, operation history, and existing resource locations. Failed migration rolls back completely; unknown versions and structural drift remain read-only failures. Desktop/Runtime compatibility epoch 15 covers these management contracts.

Existing volume names and directories are not renamed, moved, or recreated during schema upgrade. Uninstall defaults to retaining data and workspace, and cannot remove another container to satisfy a cleanup request. The [management recovery contract](#management-recovery) owns confirmation, journal resumption, archive navigation, and explicit preservation.

concepts.title: Tessiven immutable canvases, DSL and display compatibility

frontmatter.title: Tessiven immutable canvases, DSL and display compatibility

concepts.summary: Runtime owns immutable canvas YAML and contiguous version migration; clients render a frozen data-only display contract. Reads preserve historical bytes, digests and revisions while writes create current validated snapshots. Display projection never grants resource authority or rewrites topology.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Canvas storage
- A canvas document contains stable IDs for Runtime nodes, visual groups, business services, instances, external resources, relations, and evidence.
- Every service has at least one instance on an existing node. A missing placement fails validate/save at the service ID with a source location.
- A service kind describes its primary responsibility independently of its product name, instance role or deployment format. The [DSL versioning contract](#dsl-versions) owns version selection, read projections and write upgrades.

The `tessiven_canvas_library` SQLite lineage starts at schema v1. Canvas identities, archive state, immutable YAML versions, and idempotent request results remain intact.

A fresh v2 library and an upgraded v1 library must both reopen successfully.

## DSL versions
The contiguous v1→v1.0.0→v1.1.0 chain changes version only and retains legacy layout. New canvases use v1.1.0; invalid/unknown/failed migration remains unchanged for explicit repair. Reads preserve YAML/digest/revision; writes create current snapshots.

### Version Identities And Releases
DSL identities use stable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` strings, for example `v1.2.3`.

Paths must be unique, acyclic and complete, with source validation, target validation and semantic checks. Do not introduce a schema-only registry entry without its executable migration and fixtures.

### Read Compatibility
Validation selects the exact source schema, applies the explicit upgrade chain, and validates the current shape and cross-object contracts. Returned `document` is canonical current data.

The [canvas contract](#canvas-storage) owns those semantic rules.

Native rendering uses the independently frozen [canvas presentation contract](#display-projection), not the current DSL identity. Every DSL release must verify its explicit mapping to the oldest supported display contract without rewriting source or granting resource authority.

Ordinary edits valid in the original schema continue to upgrade automatically; no historical YAML is rewritten.

## Display projection
Unsupported source remains viewable/exportable without guessed topology; integrity failure forbids export.

### Read And Negotiation
Under `/_redeven_proxy/api/tessiven`, `GET /presentation-contract` returns `formats` and `capabilities`. Unknown well-formed capabilities are ignored rather than treated as authority.

The initial optional `group_layouts` capability enables authored group packing; without it automatic layout preserves the same memberships and relationships.

### Compatibility And Authority
The frozen schema is independent of the DSL registry. Existing display meanings must not change in place.

Resource requests continue to read the original version, check exact bindings and enforce current permissions.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The local Runtime owns the SQLite canvas library and immutable version documents. Canvas references never authorize resource actions; the [Flower and operations contract](../ai/tessiven-runtime-operations.md#flower-document-tools) owns that boundary. Tessiven does not deploy services, discover targets in the background, or synchronize libraries between devices.

### New Snapshots And Failure Boundary
Creation, imports, full save and exact edits write the current DSL. Existing history is never bulk-rewritten.

The [canvas storage contract](#canvas-storage) continues to own atomic startup database upgrades independently.

One normalized snapshot drives graph, object selection, compact summaries, details and Flower references. Native bridges receive display data and revision identity, never historical YAML, credentials or downloaded renderer code.

Removing a supported display format requires an explicit client compatibility-window decision; a DSL release cannot remove it incidentally.

concepts.title: Independent Web Environment Center
concepts.summary: Desktop combines an environment center with its existing local Runtime lifecycle. Web Center deploys independently; Runtime never requires Center or Desktop to start. Both hosts share Contracts/Core/Controller/UI. Web Center has one administrator, with no registration, users, roles, organizations or user ACL service.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Shared behavior and host ownership
Shared desktop/src/envcenter owns routes/search/filter/recovery/order/cancellation/Gateway lists. Desktop adapter calls existing lifecycle/windows; Web calls Center HTTP/browser tabs. Shared code imports neither Electron/Node filesystem nor Web auth. Desktop never contacts Center or changes Welcome/navigation/preparation/shutdown. Config/secrets do not sync. cmd/center-contracts generates exact DTO/TS/schema bounds.

Labels/hostnames grant no trust. Revisions/sequences fence observations; late completion cannot navigate canceled pending tabs or cancel open route owners. Refresh reads authority, not new intent.

## Server entry
Portal, Env and each child use distinct HTTPS origins under one registrable domain/port with matching TLS. Bookmarks are direct. Clipboard denial/absence retains descriptor/manual localized selection; announce success only after actual write.

Center pairs as access-only Gateway after fingerprint confirmation. Runtime independently persists consent through redeven web-binding apply --stdin --yes, binding RuntimeID/origin/clientSPKI/scope/revision. Published Flowersec mutually authenticated TLS1.3 pins signed Runtime service; no inbound app TCP listener.

Operations bind device/route. Browser nonce/exact origins/bounded redemption/single-use code complete handoff; response-loss same-request retry recovers one outcome. Host-only cookies never replace Runtime password/MFA. Logout/security/source/route revocation cancels derived admissions/streams.

## Runtime and child applications
webbinding owns consent, webconnector pinned TLS, environmentcenter admin/directory/proxy. Deployment requires separate stateless Connector via Unix socket with exact peer UID before credentials. Worker holds admitted route credentials only; Center retains admin/factors/master key. Direct adapter is test-only, never deployment fallback.

Control connection owns worker lease; Center loss/logout/revocation closes all streams. Connector restart loses leases; next request requires fresh valid admission. Never replay business HTTP. Systemd/Compose use distinct unprivileged identities; Connector cannot read Center state/TLS keys. IPC preserves bounded permission/capacity/compatibility/offline codes; Runtime payloads cannot invent worker errors. Published controller retries only explicit transient Gateway admission conflicts; invalid/denied/revoked proofs terminate.

Services/editor/graphical viewers use resource origins; trusted proxy retains parent credentials. Editor pins running instance. Graphical access requires scoped Flowersec. Child framing follows authenticated Runtime policy for editor workers; Portal denies framing.

## Plugin application origins
Authenticated parent operations prepare/revoke origins under shared pending/active capacity. Duplicate pending origin is busy; failed/canceled probes release reservation. DELETE fences pending work so late probes cannot revive/replace generations. Each child binds parent route/Runtime admission and cannot call management APIs. Gateway certificates/CONNECT enforce exact namespace/target. Desktop credentials attach only to trusted parent frame.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Center is trusted with plaintext application traffic. This is not browser-to-Runtime encryption against Center. Forwarded headers, loopback, SSH tunnels and browser-supplied headers cannot create management authority.

Web v1 does not implement Desktop SSH/WSL/local preparation, Cloud aggregation or local account/model delegation. Existing Desktop capabilities retain their owners. Remote terminal/files/Git/monitoring/container/Flower and graphical capabilities retain ordinary Runtime permissions and platform conditions.

concepts.title: Web service browser routing and authorization

frontmatter.title: Web service browser routing and authorization

concepts.summary: Registry access mode selects protected unified proxy or Desktop loopback; current Environment/forward authority governs every handoff. Browser cookies, Electron credentials and service authentication stay separate. Reject stale routes without direct-target fallback or durable substitute sessions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Browser sessions
- Backend normalization accepts `3000`, `:3000` and absolute/scheme-less HTTP(S) with exact `localhost`, numeric `127.0.0.0/8` or `::1`. Renderer checks are feedback only.
- Browser Local UI unified access uses `/pf/<forward_id>/...`; remote sessions use authorized `pf-<forward_id>` origin and one-time entry. [Loopback access](#desktop-loopback) and [Desktop windows](../desktop/web-service-browser-window.md) own Desktop presentation.
- [Operation progress](managed-service-operation-progress.md) owns per-service feedback. Managed services open through their verified `open-session` result.

## System browser authorization
- Only private-bridge-header admission can mint entries. Memory-only entries cap at 128; remove expired then evict oldest. Loopback HTTP cookies intentionally omit Secure and contain independent random session authority.
- One session per bridge authority/forward expires after 12 hours or shutdown. Memory-only sessions cap at 256 with the same cleanup policy.
- Existing root-mounted forwarding preserves root-relative resources, app-owned `/pf/*`, same-protocol/port redirects, queries, fragments and WebSockets. No new routing rule is added.
- Desktop derives relative paths only from that exact private origin. Local compatibility disables browser handoff and cannot switch mode.

## Desktop loopback
- Persisted `port_forwards.access_mode` alone selects mode. System browsers cannot receive Electron credentials, private `pf-*` substitutions or newly minted unified sessions.
- Bind only `127.0.0.1:0`. Native/placement bridges use canonical numeric-loopback plus exact `/pf/<forward_id>/`; remote routes retain their authorized `pf-*` authority. Keep streaming/oversized replies streaming, not buffered for optional rewriting.
- Each gateway has an independent random credential. [Managed opening](managed-web-service-opening.md) owns explicit reprepare; failed authentication cannot change mode or dial directly.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
[Web Center](web-environment-center.md) opens services/editor on resource-specific sibling origins. Parent Runtime credentials stay in the server; child browsers cannot invoke Env APIs. Editor admission pins its running instance and authenticated Runtime frame policy permits its same-origin worker iframe.

Temporary forwards are memory-only until Save; expired/unknown identities cannot be recreated from request fields. Browser-only Env App retains its popup route; no direct-target fallback or device heuristic changes registry authority.

The cookie admits one proxy origin, never Local UI, Provider/Gateway, Flowersec artifacts or other Desktop credentials. No public fallback, `/pf/<id>` conversion, durable session or alternate proxy is allowed; IPC/startup-report contracts remain unchanged.

Compatibility origin is not direct access, RBI, public listening, Local UI login or application authentication. Random credentials block ambient browser use but do not make loopback a cross-user security boundary.

concepts.summary: Activity/Workbench share service list/drawer: identity, state, action, facts. Retain narrow/localized/large-text usability. Historical failure never replaces current state; failed checks preserve facts and authorized recovery. Resource cache grants no lifecycle or route authority.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Collection
Centered header/launcher/toolbar/list. Rows have 64px minimum, not fixed height. Bounded status isolates async feedback under [layout stability](../ui/page-loading-continuity.md#asynchronous-layout); narrow/localized text wraps.

## Opening restrictions
Unavailable Open retains its ordinary icon and native disabled state. Focusable wrapper exposes reason on keyboard/touch/hover; active work names action/stage. When backend offers executable Start, it is primary within existing permissions.

## Review and focus
One drawer shows conclusion, compact resources and recommended actions. New known inventory may replace old inspection; unknown preserves facts. Older/unknown targets retain stop-first then explicit update. Originally stopped services remain stopped after update.

## Templates and versions
Template categories use published Floe Tabs with paired selection colors, roving keyboard focus and a labelled panel. Product styles never override tab ink. Template lists use compact rounded rows with source groups; the wider detail pane keeps deployment facts, runtime details and actions together. Dropdown wrappers own the sole focus target and disabled state.

Host template previews show identity, source/preview state and the version, access mode and disk requirement needed to choose a deployment. A closed keyboard-operable technical disclosure retains revision, paths, endpoint and lifecycle facts; installation steps and commands are never expanded by default. Available host templates omit redundant success explanations; installed or unavailable reasons stay visible. Switching templates resets disclosure state, and desktop actions remain fixed while technical details scroll. Narrow host previews give Deploy a full-width primary row and pair secondary actions below it. The catalog title and category controls replace introductory instructions.

Both template and installed-service versions use the same bounded directory/detail workspace. Rows emphasize version and state; the selected detail owns trust, source, platform and expandable artifact identity. Current releases retain useful provenance. Narrow layouts stack independently scrollable panes, while request feedback and submission remain outside the list. Refresh and verification preserve selection, focus, scroll and footer geometry. Confirmation, stop-first and update authorization remain unchanged. Selection motion is brief and local; reduced motion removes travel.

## Installation feedback
The installation drawer uses a bounded compact form: service identity and environment, one selected version with its change action, then a complete wrapping workspace path with its folder action. Avoid repeated version facts, nested recommendation cards and default explanatory paragraphs. Optional deployment facts and access mode live in a closed disclosure whose summary shows the selected mode. Published Floe button radios retain native keyboard selection. Custom workspace warnings, release advisories and required template acknowledgements remain outside that disclosure; consent still gates review and installation. The footer has one primary review/install action, a template-list return and the drawer's existing close control; narrow layouts give the primary action its own full-width row. Successful review adds a short status without repeating the plan.

Final install returns immediately to the active collection with an appended submission row and accessible status focus, while admission runs independently. The accepted operation supplies version validation, environment checks and deployment progress even before a full list response. Search/archive filters cannot hide the new submission. Status explicitly opens execution details; completion does not force another drawer. Rejected requests support safe fresh review, uncertain responses support receipt lookup, and accepted failures use existing service recovery. See [operation progress](managed-service-operation-progress.md#install-admission-and-handoff).

## Execution feedback
Execution details keep one bounded command/output viewport. Downloaded bytes remain visible when the total is unknown; unknown totals keep the byte bar indeterminate. Speed is shown once measured bytes are available, while fully cached pulls show zero transfer. Layer counts remain separate. New output does not expand the panel or move a reader away from earlier lines.

sections.body:
The renderer maps existing backend status and capabilities to short localized labels and semantic icons.

Specific entrance errors remain readable; failed Open never prevents another attempt.

The shell retains only collection and loading-presentation styles; management and version-review styles load with the product page rather than the initial document graph.

concepts.summary: Desktop resolves trusted resource identity over Environment transport into short-lived loopback entry. Browser receives resource-bound HTTP/WS, never private bridge tokens. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Resource intent and route ownership
After starting the selected CodeSpace, Env App submits `mode: browser` and its CodeSpace ID through the same root-frame-only IPC used for built-in editor windows.

The system browser never receives a private Local UI `/cs/<id>` URL, an environment credential, or a raw gateway header.

## One-time entry and browser session
Only main can mint an entry from the gateway object.

Runtime and editor traffic never carries the browser cookie; upstream responses cannot set the reserved cookie name.

An OS-open failure closes the newly acquired gateway and route.

No upstream package, public listener, SSH forwarding process, editor injection, or Web Service authorization change is required.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identity, tools and acquisition
`scripts/dev_desktop.sh` freezes HEAD/tracked/nonignored inputs, including authored OKF/builders/Go embeds, and rejects drift. Generated OKF/ignored assets are outputs. Reuse requires identical source/dependencies/tools/target/settings and verified Desktop/immutable Runtime; missing/corrupt/incomplete output rebuilds, never launches old bytes. --rebuild forces; REDEVEN_AGENT_FORCE_INSTALL=1 reinstalls three JS packages once. Manifests choose pnpm/npm/locks; only pinned Rust preparation may install tools.

Read Rust pin from scripts/redevplugin_build_toolchain.json, shared with Runtime preparation, never a shell assignment. Capture pin/installed compiler identities without auto-installing; cache misses prepare absent tools. Invalid pins name configuration; drift invalidates preparation.

Resolve physical checkout before profile/service ownership/building so aliases share one owner and execute CLI preparation. Resolve parent aliases for dependency boundaries: package-local links may survive managed-worktree aliases; external links/symlinked roots remain forbidden. Toolchain CLI uses Node main-module identity.

macOS infers enabled static HTTP/HTTPS proxies once unless explicit HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY (either case, even empty) or REDEVEN_DEV_SYSTEM_PROXY=0. Preserve NO_PROXY or add loopback exclusions; PAC/SOCKS-only needs explicit policy. Preserve credentials/TLS/integrity and remove only inferred environment before launch.

Official Node downloads retry three times with1/2s backoff for transport or HTTP408/429/500/502/503/504. Permanent HTTP/certificate failures stop. Retain URL/policy and CONNECT/origin/byte diagnostics. Resume owned partials only; require fresh official checksum for cache, verify complete bytes and delete failures.

Cargo reuse requires exact freshly staged locked public crates and regenerated digest/execution/consumption evidence. Complete cache works offline; missing data requires acquisition. Corruption/compiler failures cannot substitute paths. Isolate releases and rebuild whole product on source change; no component/watch mode.

## Bundle
Include Runtime/plugin runtime/standalone Computer Node/released SDKs/UI without first-launch download. Chromium remains optional [confirmed installation](../ai/computer-use-browser-installation.md). Main is pure JS/inline CSS; native SDK/updater retain boundaries, frontend trees build-only. Electron Builder admits main/four preloads/full renderer licenses/workers/fonts/Wasm; reject tests/maps/demos/extra ASAR entries and>80MiB including unpacked modules. Report Runtime/Electron separately.

Computer retains released layout/licenses/platform binary, excludes maps and checks manifest.upstream.json inventory. macOS verifies pre-signing plus signatures/unsigned Mach-O, normalizing only signature-dependent __LINKEDIT allocation. Derive signed record before sealing; reject unsigned-byte/manifest/executable drift. Linux manifest unchanged. Qualify relocated helpers/utilities offline without source/global Node, audit Electron cache/archive and report components/largest files; compare equal inputs with installed/compressed bytes distinct.

## Scheduling/lifecycle
Overlap Desktop compilation/Runtime preparation; assets-Go/plugins/Computer own outputs. Env typecheck/bundle share checkout lock; Go waits embeds and publication requires complete unchanged inputs. Three dependency workers preserve serial digest/order. Failure/cancel retains errors and stops owned descendants. Dev skips notice freshness; staged/main enforce it and releases run after assets.

Reuse compatible intact Gateways; drift never auto-upgrades. Owner repairs corrupt/missing packages; explicit Update selects a build. Dirty source is in cache key; changes retire generation, missing key creates session cache; archive owner validates. Read-only startup/cleanup locates schema5 by connection_id, supported old schemas by legacy gateway_id until migration; never trust_profile.gateway_id/change records/cleanup-ledger gatewayID for paths. Unknown/invalid schemas fail without substitution.

Dev gzip1/Brotli4 preserves decoded bytes; release uses maximum compression; profile belongs to identity. Exclude other worktrees/native cache from Gateway copies. Record dependency/verification/Desktop/Runtime/Gateway durations. Rebuilt/reused launch acceptance needs saved local Gateway,exact Runtime commit and verified cleanup; empty profile timing is insufficient. Exit/signals/failure stop owned services only. Electron resolver emits only path to stdout, diagnostics stderr, propagates failure and rechecks executable after build.

## Credentials/retention
Unpackaged dev uses AES-256-GCM with random retained0600 profile key, protecting plaintext rather than same-user access. Other modes use system storage without constructor probes. Explicit legacy Keychain recovery never reads preferences/secrets automatically; migrate files atomically, retaining credentials/Retry/Quit on failure. Corrupt keys cannot reset accounts/Runtime/Keychain.

Publish complete <development-state-root>/desktop/bundles/<manifest-sha256>. Keep newest three plus selected/reused/live; bound verified inactive count, not bytes or active/unverified growth.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Runtime state identity
Each Runtime state directory owns an immutable Ed25519 seed in `access-identity.key`. Invalid or symlinked existing material fails closed and is never replaced.

Existing TLS, Gateway trust and Runtime authentication remain authoritative.

## Observation and grouping
Main-process observations bind an entry ID to its configured connection and verified identity.

Runtime membership summaries use the Gateway pairing fingerprint: SHA-256 of the canonical, trimmed Ed25519 SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM, encoded as unpadded base64url with `SHA256:`.

Existing registrations, Gateway member and Cloud binding authority remain in their respective stores.

## Explicit default and one-time opening
The existing main Open button uses the saved default. Implicit defaults use stable registration / first-observation order, never probe completion order or a newly rebuilt Gateway catalog timestamp.

[Gateway access sessions](../gateway/gateway-access-sessions.md) owns transport isolation and same-route session reuse.

## Membership discovery and migration
Members are discovered from the signed v6 directory and matched to trusted Runtime membership summaries.

Runtime attachment requires local consent and never adds Cloud enrollment delegation. Existing unsupported state is rejected unchanged. Optional Cloud binding and explicit transport route remain independent.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Desktop shares host-neutral environment contracts, projection/controller and Gateway list UI with [Web Center](../architecture/web-environment-center.md). Existing lifecycle/window owners and user interactions remain authoritative; no Center login/service dependency is introduced.

This contract owns display association and route selection. Proof observation never upgrades those permissions.

[Gateway Desktop interactions](../gateway/gateway-desktop-interactions.md) owns the explicit environment connection, invitation and confirmation steps and the independent management, invitation and local consent boundaries; recovery reuses the original Runtime lifecycle owner.

frontmatter.title: Environment library, registrations and card presentation

concepts.summary: Welcome projects authoritative registration owners into a stable library. Exact Runtime/Cloud links and verified Gateway routes may share cards, without transferring lifecycle or storage authority. Explicit actions name their owner; snapshots preserve drafts, focus and pending work while late replies cannot resurrect removed records.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Library
- Show the Environment title, description and search/refresh/create actions. Keep counts on category filters and Runtime/window states on cards; show current snapshot issues below the description without reserving an empty row.
- Pair Local/SSH/WSL with Cloud only when linked Runtime ID, Cloud origin, Cloud ID and ENV ID agree. Access-point origin is routing metadata. Current health outranks old window reports; retained display grants no control.
- Search/equivalent snapshots preserve selection; source defaults apply once. Trusted Gateway summaries show name, endpoints, attachment identity/phase and selected egress dependency. One member needs no selector; refresh cannot restore retired selections or confirmation substitute missing members. Preserve menu order/capability checks.
- Cloud uses one section per signed-in account and a shared grid. Offer Refresh normally/after sync failure, Sign in again after expiry. Either owner pin puts the group in Pinned; controls change only the active owner and explain the other pin.

## Registration ownership
Each action names Local, Runtime target, saved URL or Gateway-member storage ownership. Desktop serializes writes, publishes committed snapshots immediately and fences late probe/Open replies so removed records cannot return.

- Create/edit/rename/pin/remove use explicit `EnvironmentRegistrationRef`, never renderer kind or placement inference. First WSL registration fills an empty default; explicit selection replaces it; deletion clears it atomically.
- The one-time retired SSH-catalog migration matches destination, port and normalized root, transfers credentials/settings, preserves Runtime Target names and removes duplicate built-in Local projections without touching remote targets. Remove decoder/journal only when the supported catalog minimum excludes that schema.
- Every Launcher Operation declares `active_progress_surface`: `open`, `runtime_lifecycle`, `reinstall` or `gateway`. Main/renderer title, details and cancellation consume it without another timeline.

## Card presentation
- Cards retain one opaque theme-derived plane and a quiet, stable contour. Connected cards carry a restrained success tint; fine-pointer hover gently shifts the same plane without removing the tint, swapping gradients, adding shadows or moving controls. Shared Floe color timing reverses from the painted state; reduced motion settles immediately and touch never latches hover.
- Use **Open window** for unopened environments and **Show window** to focus existing sessions, preserving readiness, authority, lifecycle and session ownership. Use Environment/environment window/Redeven in settings, progress, recovery and titles; Env App is internal. Every shipped catalog translates the copy.
- Card controls stay single-line; long progress actions wrap. Four creation entries form an equal-column 2x2 grid. Copy log/Close share Floe outline treatment, widths and row height without translation overflow.
- Center primary content excluding the menu toggle; idle reserves no icon space. Submission shows loader/shimmer, accessible busy state and blocks repeat clicks; completion restores centered text. Keep geometry and icon-label grouping stable.
- Batch refresh owns the header until the batch settles. Each card refresh follows its own probe/request and stops independently. Observation never makes primary actions pending; card actions cannot release batch ownership, nor batch completion clear card actions.
- Runtime/Cloud/paired Gateway tabs occupy the standalone badge slot. Cloud auth/sync failure cannot disable Runtime actions. [Center navigation](desktop-welcome-navigation.md) preserves layout and never restarts on snapshots.

## Platform presentation
Last-known facts survive disconnect/restart until replaced; unknown OS never blocks Runtime or changes geometry, selection or focus.

- Trusted `runtime_platform`/optional `runtime_linux_distribution` arrive through startup/attach, health, management status and bridge hello. Only exact distribution ID selects its bundled mark, never `ID_LIKE`, names, Desktop identity, WSL labels or image names. Unknown Linux uses Tux; unknown platforms a device mark.
- Main persists `runtime_platform_facts` in existing UI state by environment kind/stable identity. Renderer storage cannot write it or make remembered facts health/access authority.
- Reserve a nonshrinking 1rem title slot, .875rem original-color OS mark and truncated single-line name. No tint/mask/grayscale. Localize accessibility copy, not brand names.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Desktop owns registration metadata: edits/removal cannot delete Runtime/Gateway/WSL/remote resources or change policy. Recovery diagnostics are transient, not persistence or management authority. Platform display grants no access, lifecycle or plugin capability; [readiness](desktop-runtime-process-lifecycle.md#readiness) owns admission.

[Interaction continuity](desktop-interaction-continuity.md) owns drafts, authority, visibility and stale responses; [SSH settings](desktop-ssh-environment-settings.md) owns fields and [WSL operations](desktop-wsl-runtime-operations.md) discovery/lifecycle.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Settings session
- Local opens Access & security without a connection editor. Access management uses existing WSL authority only after exact-distribution discovery confirms it is running; opening/loading never starts stopped distros. Distinguish current password constraints from saved next-start configuration.
- Each opening owns committed connection baseline/draft and lazy access baseline/draft. Health refresh preserves running summary, connection nodes, expanded listeners, address filters, selection, scroll and QR panels; never reload access/certificate/security configuration.
- Save invalidates older reads. Late failure from a closed opening becomes a notification, never an error in the next editor. Access opens current-connection/browser/sign-in/HTTPS tasks; recovery-pending protection must be restored before changing it.

## Presentation
- Cap the panel at 50rem by 44.375rem and viewport/titlebar; only viewport resize changes the cap. Tabs/loading/disclosures cannot recenter it or move actions. Use one Current connection card with aligned, selectable, wrapping text/diagnostics/paths/addresses.
- Browser scope, sign-in and certificate tasks share rows, meaningful icons and published outline controls with borders/hover/focus. Preserve specialized QR/recovery-code geometry. Removal drafts cannot look committed; review never shows passwords. Separate footer feedback/actions. Floe owns focus trapping, nested Escape, restoration, variants and forced colors.
- SSH destination fills the adjacent control column in creation/settings. Loading/cached-host failure uses its trailing inset, preserving width/draft/focus; idle indicators take no external column or input clicks.
- Access steps place equal flexible connectors after non-final labels; narrow layouts stack aligned badges without horizontal connectors. Floe owns modal presence and 200ms tab underline; retained exit never blanks the panel.

## Connection facts
Observations preserve host/container namespaces; failures prove no exit. Explicit Stop clears addresses. Presentation never chooses transport.

- Name the selected Environment before addresses. Never substitute SSH aliases for URL hosts or rely on WSL localhost forwarding. Address count cannot resize settings/move the footer.
- Internal browser access aligns label with one expandable scope/count summary, stacking narrowly. Avoid duplicate scope paragraphs/disclosure labels. Preserve expansion on refresh and show total/filtered counts; environment-only addresses have no browser/copy/share actions.
- Gateway cards retain explicit URL/local/SSH/container transport without Runtime lifecycle authority. Display, clipboard and QR exclude tokens/private loopback credentials.
- Public addresses are independent of private management. Saved bind/protocol/port/password/certificate changes apply next start; drafts cannot synthesize current URLs. Failed writes preserve password verifier and report failure.

concepts.title: Desktop interaction continuity
concepts.summary: Welcome owns interaction sessions; Launcher/Runtime own business operations. Observations retain open panels, draft, focus, selection, steps and scroll. Only explicit user transitions or current completion alter visibility. Invalid authority blocks submission with recovery; closing progress never cancels work.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Ownership and observations
Each interaction field has one owner: the existing library overlay, guidance, lifecycle disclosure, Gateway foreground action or settings opening. Retained cards supply presentation only; submission reads current authoritative data.

Addresses no longer shareable still lose QR disclosure under the connection-security contract.

Before the first asynchronous submission, one synchronous transition records the attempt, closes its menu and opens its operation surface. Duplicate activation cannot submit twice.

Deferred initial focus never overrides a user-selected menu item.

The interaction-continuity package command runs required state and real component suites, including the production snapshot subscription and observer. The cached commit group runs affected staged sources; bounded integration checks affected base-to-tip paths.

Synthetic composition verifies DOM continuity; it does not prove physical operating-system IME behavior.

## Native edit context menus
Desktop-owned BrowserWindows attach a localized native edit menu for unhandled Chromium context requests. Editable surfaces expose Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste and Select all with Chromium edit flags; reading selections expose Copy. Native roles preserve the originating frame, selection, undo stack and the existing paste event path (including Flower attachment handling). No renderer clipboard-read bridge is introduced. Renderer-owned menus prevent the native fallback, so conversation/file/terminal menus remain authoritative. Navigation and window close dismiss pending native menus. Browser-hosted editors retain their browser-native menu.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
## Layers, exit and recovery
Published presence and overlay ownership provide one exit and input-routing lifecycle.

Failure, permission loss, cancellation failure and missing progress retain an exit or recovery action. Closing never infers cancellation.

concepts.title: Desktop Runtime coordination and readiness
concepts.summary: One target-bound coordinator admits managed Local, WSL, SSH and container lifecycle work. Verified direct channels and current compatible Presence govern actions; Gateway/Cloud access stays separate. Conflicts retain the first operation and failed observations never prove stopped state or authorize alternate routing.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Process lifecycle
### Ownership
Keys combine host authority, exact container engine/id and normalized Runtime root. Native Local keys use the actual canonical state directory, resolving symlinks without equating parent and child. [Scoped Runtime operations](../ai/tessiven-runtime-operations.md#runtime-operations) recheck source/target authority before this coordinator admits a handoff.

### Execution
- Start reuses one verified healthy Runtime. Stop succeeds on empty inventory and verifies termination.
- Restart stops the observed Runtime, starts the installed binary and verifies readiness.
- Update prepares/verifies its package before modification, starts even a previously stopped Runtime and verifies it.
- Refresh observes directly without mutation. Reinstall follows [its recovery contract](desktop-reinstall-operations.md).

The current binary supplies temporary exact inventory and best-effort stop. Builds, downloads, archive preparation, upload and extraction belong to package progress, never process discovery. Desktop exit/update retires WSL Bridges without stopping WSL Runtime.

### Actions
Direct targets retain lifecycle and Provider Connect/Disconnect actions in every diagnosis. Conflicting actions stay visible but disabled, naming the active operation. Access-only targets offer Open/Connect/refresh-access without lifecycle or management fallback.

## Readiness
### Direct readiness
Native Local Environment is available on macOS/Linux; Windows uses registered WSL Environments. A newly published listener without final status remains pending within the startup deadline. Desktop update warns that Desktop and Local Runtime restart and interrupt Local sessions; Later changes nothing.

WSL, SSH and container observations use the saved channel. Unknown/failed health offers Refresh with its real diagnostic. Pending refresh retains prior diagnosis/startup age but withdraws live Presence; completion replaces it. Main retains credential-free `observed_runtime_control_status` until probe failure or management-configuration change. Gateway failure affects only that route.

A completed probe preserves missing-control diagnostics even when it publishes no Presence. Unknown or unauthenticated status must not become an observed stopped Runtime. Missing diagnostics may guide recovery but never grant live management capability; only current Presence can do so.

Direct lifecycle actions remain available in every diagnosis. Failed nested recovery names the actual operation and retains structured diagnostics; raw stderr appears only in technical details.

### Access and Flower
[Verified access routes](desktop-environment-access.md) owns association/defaults. Gateway directory presence, membership and application probing are distinct; failure never changes routes or starts Runtime recovery.

[Runtime Flower access](../../desktop/src/shared/runtimeFlowerAccess.ts) checks actual protocol/epoch for commands, subscriptions, frames and attachments. Desktop restart does not prove Runtime changed. Welcome admits Flower only with compatible openable Runtime and AI `ready`/`degraded`; transitional states show preparation with a return action, while missing/blocked/unavailable facts cannot admit requests.

## Bridge boundary
- [Process lifecycle](#process-lifecycle) owns coordination and exact-target actions; [readiness](#readiness) owns compatible admission.
- [SSH](desktop-ssh-runtime-operations.md), [WSL](desktop-wsl-runtime-operations.md) and [reinstall](desktop-reinstall-operations.md) define direct execution. [Transport recovery](desktop-transport-recovery.md#transport-recovery) owns bridge generations and disposal.
- [Session/model source](desktop-transport-recovery.md#model-source-sessions) owns target routes, model-process lifetime and session invalidation. Private bridge tokens never move between partitions or attach to public origins.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Runtime owns business services and proxy sessions. User-supplied systemd, Docker or Kubernetes supervision is outside Desktop coordination.

Only Desktop chooses managed Runtime recovery. Optional platform display fields cannot change readiness or compatibility admission.

Runtime control is Desktop coordination, not a general network API or plugin grant. [ReDevPlugin](../architecture/redevplugin-boundary.md) retains its separate execution and capability boundary.

concepts.title: Desktop SSH runtime operations
concepts.summary: Desktop uses saved SSH connection/placement for host/container Runtime. One local coordinator, operation, transport lease and temporary helper own lifecycle/recovery. Gateway/Cloud credentials grant no SSH authority; targets persist no Desktop supervisor or lifecycle lock.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Authentication and transport
Keys bind normalized destination/port, authentication, SSH executable and credential scope. Preserve failure without substitution/replay. macOS/Linux use ControlMaster; Windows bounded native OpenSSH plus one child/private Bridge, never WSL/ControlMaster. Cancel only owned children.

Omitted passwords reuse exact private scope; explicit changes reject during leases and never cross scopes. Without password, explicit connections try configured keys/agent in batch mode even for password registrations; passive status may defer. Never send empty retries. Start/Restart/Update carry transient credentials through access/certificate checks, preparation and verification without saving; observations reject passwords.

Connect Timeout bounds probe/inventory/readiness; startup/packages have distinct deadlines. Windows x64 askpass accepts password/passphrase, rejects host-key prompts, writes only private stdout and preserves OpenSSH trust. Missing helper fails; no secrets in args/files/logs. Bounded includes exclude wildcard/negated picker aliases, not explicit destinations. Save exact root/container engine+ID separately from label.

## Execution
One operation reuses transport and probes platform once. Only inventory/stop prepares the small helper; Start/Stop never build full bundles. Update verifies before mutation with visible acquisition/upload/build. Use public dependencies and install Desktop deps before Env assets.

Archive bounds: 256 MiB compressed/512 MiB expanded including Runtime/Computer/signed plugins, enforced before writes and parsed once. Upload progress has its own stall deadline; command timeout resumes after final write. Stall/cancel/loss stops owned command; pipe bytes prove no receipt. Password prompts have no upload deadline.

Private slots: runtime/managed/bin/executables 0700, stamps/evidence 0600 independent of umask. Failed normalization preserves live slot; upstream owns executable admission. Host targets require confirmed user/root, containers exact saved identity. Start/Restart/Update/Reinstall may start container; Stop never does and accepts empty inventory. Signal only verified scope; retain before/after. Wipe-reinstall may tolerate helper inventory/stop failure only when direct access can isolate root.

Remote snippets perform bounded probe/stage/inventory/stop/install/start/verify/isolate/cleanup. Desktop owns order/deadlines/cancel/progress/retry; no target lock/heartbeat/supervisor.

## Progress and results
Use generated signed GitHub latest/download/redeven-install.sh with selected tag, no Portal duplicate. One Launcher Operation measures actual upload/download/acquisition bytes. Parse complete Downloading Redeven: N% records; stderr diagnostics, stdout stage path. Companion output cannot reset Runtime progress. No additional parser/process/poll.

100% transfer proves no activation/readiness. Freeze measured progress on failure/cancel. Acquisition/staging/upload/unpack are preparation; only activation changes live slot. Create operation before first SSH command. Distinguish connection/engine/preparation/command/readiness errors with technical stderr. Empty successful report stays pending to deadline; nonzero read is command failure, valid blocked report Runtime failure, only nonempty malformed report invalid. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Transport recovery
### Recovery presentation
Recovery uses an unboxed layout within the existing shell, with generous whitespace, semantic theme colors, standard buttons, and fine separators around the authoritative countdown or active phase.

A 30-second stalled-app timeout shows an actionable failure instead of an endless loading surface.

Each established bridge owns one immutable transport-recovery snapshot with a monotonic `generation` and `revision`, the real `waiting`, `connecting`, `paused`, `ready`, or `failed` phase, completed attempt count, known retry and recovery timestamps, a structured failure, and explicitly allowed actions.

Lifecycle generation fencing cancels matching Opens so a late response cannot recreate the old session.

## Model-source sessions
- Every `DesktopSessionContextSnapshot` carries `target_route`: Local publishes declared `local_host`/`remote_desktop`; SSH, Gateway and External Local UI publish `remote_desktop`.
- Compaction is a Runtime thread action. Desktop and Env App share canonical timeline/read-state updates rather than inventing transcript messages.
- One Responses transport manager survives control reconnects. Idempotent `ai.thread.transport.release` releases only memory; Floret owns canonical deletion. Exact v4 transport events reject incompatible peers.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Transport recovery IPC is a narrow current-session capability. The separate Desktop Restart handoff exposes only the current window's bounded user-authored state to its fresh session, never ports, tokens, other Environment snapshots, Runtime handles, or launcher operations. Terminal transport failure may preserve the renderer window for diagnosis and navigation, but every previously loaded Runtime surface remains non-interactive until a fresh session is explicitly opened.

Welcome Flower and Tessiven share compatibility/AI readiness. Returning to preparation disposes stale initialization while parent `ComposerDraftStore` retains drafts. Plugin workers/sandboxes receive no runtime-control endpoint/token; resource access uses released ReDevPlugin brokers and registered adapters.

concepts.title: Desktop Welcome navigation
concepts.summary: Welcome page selection is immediate and independent of Launcher IPC or Runtime preparation. Visited pages retain state; readiness gates Flower requests, not navigation. Explicit Environment tab changes may animate cards, while refresh/return preserves headers and skips entrance replay.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- Header, logo, sidebar and contextual actions select locally. Health/progress/snapshot updates cannot override navigation. Main captures navigation after asynchronous reads so stale destinations cannot publish newer revisions.
- Selecting Environments, Redeven Cloud or Gateways renders immediately. Hiding/disposing cancels motion; return does not replay it. [Environment library](desktop-environment-library.md#library) retains card/state ownership.
- Environments and Flower mount on first visit and remain mounted until disposal. Filesystem invalidation uses environment ID, Runtime start identity and session key, never health/probe timestamps.

- Gateway management is an in-shell detail page. Returning to All Gateways restores list search, filter, scroll and focus. [Gateway Desktop interactions](../gateway/gateway-desktop-interactions.md) owns its sections, enrollment dialogs and recovery behavior; global navigation preserves the retained management context.

## Popup and dropdown ownership

Welcome consumes published Floe presence and menu/tooltip CSS. Each surface has one presence owner; closing immediately revokes pointer/keyboard input and accessibility exposure, freezes its measured placement, and retains the DOM through the CSS exit. Reopening reverses the same panel and preserves drafts/selection. Only the inner surface transforms; placement reads untransformed layout dimensions. Resolved collision direction and the anchor point determine motion origin. Reduced motion uses Floe's immediate recipe.

| Welcome entry points | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Environment split actions | `DesktopAnchoredOverlaySurface` |
| Runtime/Gateway progress, recovery, Cloud account/connection details, SSH loading details and directory help | `DesktopActionPopover` through the same surface |
| Hover details and help | `DesktopPopover` / `DesktopTooltip`; tooltip uses the shorter Floe recipe |
| Connection details and retained QR disclosure | `EndpointsPopover` through the same surface; QR expansion stays an internal disclosure |
| Appearance picker | `DesktopThemePicker` through the same surface |
| Language, container, official Cloud provider and SSH destination options | `DesktopAnchoredListbox` |
| Saved Gateway/address pickers and Gateway object/connection actions | Published `Dropdown` |
| Gateway member/leave target, Cloud route and SSH bootstrap strategy | Published `Select`, including native form state and accessible listbox semantics |
| Embedded Flower model, permission, reasoning, thread switcher, subagent, goal, composer overflow/reference/command and context/compaction details | Existing Flower adapters consuming shared Floe presence |
| Embedded Flower settings, extensions and browser connection selectors | Published `Select` / `Dropdown` |
| Embedded Flower tool capability, Kimi endpoint and computer frame rate | Published `Select`; frame-rate input stays isolated from window dragging |
| File preview encoding/worksheet selectors and find/info/cell details | Published `Select` and a retained shared-presence preview panel |
| Compaction detail tooltip | Shared tooltip presence; text remains selectable while open |
| Embedded Flower thread/transcript context menus | `FlowerContextMenu`; callers retain the current presentation through the shared exit |
| Command palette, feedback disclosure, dialogs and drawers, working-directory picker | Published Floe components retain their own presence and focus lifecycle |
| Contextual Ask Flower | Published content-sized `PromptCard`, including placement, input, focus and entrance/exit motion |

Action popovers opt into published Floe `observeDialogHeight`; their content clip adds no second fill, border or shadow. The outer rounded surface owns material and height, while top placement anchors its bottom edge so expansion preserves the trigger gap without scaling text. Geometry observes the inner clip, below the height owner, to avoid ResizeObserver feedback. Closing during resize freezes the painted height through exit; reduced motion commits the natural size immediately.

An Environment split action retains one primary button and one anchor across admission, progress, recovery and completion. Localized transient labels use `StableText`; Floe's slow color tokens ease the inverse fill and foreground together. Tooltip availability cannot remount the control, and its existing action authority and progress disclosure behavior remain unchanged.

Do not put these components inside open-only `Show` blocks; that would destroy their exit. Product observations may update content but never reopen a dismissed operation surface or release a newly reopened session. Selection and confirmation authority remain with their existing feature owners. Selects use the published popup contract. Ask Flower supplies product content and admission to the published `PromptCard`; Floe owns its compact appearance, input response, file-selection controls, model menu and motion. Desktop supplies the existing model directory and attachment transport. Changing the model affects the current request without writing global preferences; unknown-admission retry reuses the captured model and staged files.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Discovery and registration
The main process publishes one immutable platform-capability snapshot. Renderer surfaces consume it and never infer the host operating system.

UI recovery copy may show Microsoft WSL commands for the user to run.

## Linux Runtime lifecycle
WSL and SSH host operations consume the same managed-Linux probe, uploaded install, atomic activation, startup report, inventory, exact stop, and verification scripts.

Runtime installs under the Linux user's home-backed `~/.redeven`, never under `/mnt`, and does not require `systemd`.

Only the Environment Stop action stops it.

## Private Bridge and failure behavior
`desktop-bridge` remains a foreground `wsl.exe` child carrying the shared `redeven-desktop-placement-h2/1` HTTP/2 session over private standard input and output.

Multiple registered distributions have independent target ids, processes, Bridges, update state, and lifecycle coordinator keys.

## Package and update boundary
The Windows Desktop bundle uses `managed_wsl_archive` and contains one verified `redeven_linux_amd64.tar.gz`; it must not contain or execute `redeven.exe`.

Public Windows assets remain forbidden until Authenticode signing, signed NSIS update metadata, signing receipts, and a real signed n-1 to n update are enabled together.

The shared toolbar and picture-preset presentation do not own backend state. macOS retains native menu, window-generation, frame credit and capture-quality semantics.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
When the trusted Desktop Shell bridge is present, Env App requests a semantic Web Service window instead of creating a renderer popup. The address field always projects the protected route back onto the user's original service origin and current application path; it must not expose Runtime listener ports, private hostnames, `/pf/<id>` prefixes, forward identities, boot routes, entry tickets, or other transport details.

[Managed opening](../architecture/managed-web-service-opening.md) owns the response and first-navigation boundary.

A Runtime-rejected reserved path keeps HTTP 404 and carries
`X-Redeven-Proxy-Error: port-forward-reserved-path`. The browser presentation
replaces only a marked main-document response with a localized, scriptless
explanation using published Floe window-status assets. The initial view shows a
short title without a primary action. A native, initially collapsed View details disclosure
reveals the reason, original service address with its current path, query and
fragment, and Copy address. It does not suggest retries or direct access. The toolbar
remains the sole address editor. Copy uses the host-projected address and acknowledges
completion in place. Only the exact current host document can request this action.
Theme/language refresh retains the explanation; navigating
to another address restores ordinary browsing. System-browser opening is disabled
on this page because the same protected route would reject it again.

Runtime strips its proxy-error header from application responses. Unmarked
application 404s and marked subresource responses never replace the document.
Env UI/API isolation and the saved access mode remain unchanged. This does not
add nested Env access or an automatic loopback fallback.

The semantic forward-window request optionally selects `presentation: application`. The same forward admission, isolated partition, request routing, window reuse, and teardown remain authoritative.

The [application titlebar contract](host-application-titlebar.md) owns control layout, backend command routing and recovery presentation.

Electron qualification checks that the compound address boundary has no visible
outline by asserting `outline-style: none`, alongside stable border width and
focus contrast across every published theme. Chromium may report a nonzero
computed outline width even when that outline is disabled.

Desktop isolation is a B-level browsing surface over Redeven's existing authorized route; it is not Remote Browser Isolation and does not claim a general-purpose browser security boundary. Redeven must not label a same-page iframe as complete isolated browsing, copy a reusable RBI implementation into this repository, or bypass the published-dependency policy to obtain one.

System-browser authorization and the persisted access-mode decision remain owned by the session contract; a window cannot create a new route or broaden a forward identity.
