concepts.title: Gateway access sessions
concepts.summary: Desktop reaches joined Runtime over its outbound Flowersec Gateway connection; Gateway forwards to fixed application entry without dialing a Runtime URL. Desktop/Runtime terminate TLS; Runtime retains password/MFA/Host/Origin authority. Entry expiry never shortens established sessions.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Reverse application streams
After local consent, Runtime redeems its invitation with its own identity and initiates a persistent Flowersec session to the unified public TLS endpoint. Gateway opens a reverse ByteStream on that Runtime's connection and relays both streams with bounded buffers and cancellation.

TLS, WebSocket, streaming responses and secure cookies retain their original semantics.

## Application and management separation
A reverse stream enters the original public Runtime handler. It never acquires a trusted Desktop management marker.

The catalog alone does not authorize service or Runtime process operations.

## Limits and revocation
The shared budget admits at most 32 business connections per member and 1,024 in total, including pending opens. One member exceeding a limit cannot consume another member's allocation.

Revoking a client closes its live streams and fences its pending artifacts. Other clients and the Runtime attachment stay connected. Reauthorization uses a fresh key, so previous artifacts never regain admission. These effects use published Flowersec session cancellation and relay primitives.

Cloud authorization never closes independent Gateway streams. Local egress cancellation is scoped separately by [Optional Runtime Cloud egress](gateway-cloud-access.md).

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Gateway owns reverse-stream admission and bounded forwarding only. No path in this contract grants Gateway a Runtime lifecycle command, arbitrary egress, or a second direct-access transport.

concepts.summary: Paired devices receive independent Gateway access, never accounts, roles or host-management grants. Scoped TLS bootstrap supports fresh private networks. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Invitations
Host-issued Runtime invitations require Runtime authentication and explicit consent. Client packages are rdgc1/purpose redeven-gateway-client/version1: one-use secret, exact Gateway ID/key, scoped CA and expiry. Parsers reject cross-purpose use, unknown fields, malformed trust and expiry.

Verify HTTPS using only that CA, then signed Gateway identity before persisting device trust. Never disable TLS or install global CAs. Packages expire after ten minutes; consumption admits no second device. Identical original completion may recover response loss. Desktop/Center retain CA in independent records; display names authenticate nothing. Revocation closes that device's channels without affecting another client/Cloud user.

## Private management
Local/SSH/container adapters verify credentials over the private host socket; public URLs expose device access only. Gateway derives capabilities, never caller-selected/persisted device roles. manage_attachments covers invitations/removal; manage_network covers endpoints/listeners/Host restrictions/egress/reevaluation. Issuance/listing/revocation/receipts require current host proof. Both management capabilities exist together only on that verified request. Removing a Desktop registration preserves remote service/data.

All public device keys are listed/revocable, including host-paired keys. Historical host_managed grants no exemption. Trust schema4 atomically migrates1–3 before readiness, preserving identity/access/revocations; unsupported state stays unchanged.

Private management uses host proof independently of device signatures, but a supplied signature must verify. Signed identity retains requested binding audience for exact connection pinning. Applications/service identity require admitted device keys even over private socket. Self-revocation preserves private management/recovery; refresh cannot pair again. Explicit reauthorization creates a fresh key; challenges/old receipts cannot revive revoked keys.

## Mutation recovery
X-Redeven-Operation-ID binds private mutations. A bounded mode-0600 host-only journal persists intent before effect, response afterward. Same ID/body returns saved result; route/body changes conflict. POST /gateway/v6/operations/query reads the original over the private channel. Retain <=1024 operations/24h. Issuance receipts may contain short-lived packages; never expose journal data in diagnostics/public replies. Expiry grants no replay.

Interrupted effect-before-receipt yields OPERATION_RESULT_UNKNOWN without replay. Desktop stores ID privately and queries after response loss. Confirmed failure clears pending state; unknown/expired stays fenced with inspectable ID. Explicit review acknowledgement clears only the verified Gateway's recovery fence. CLI supports --operation-id and operations query --operation-id, exposing ID on failure. Join/rotation/Cloud route/enrollment keep their domain receipts; refresh cannot authorize/resubmit consent.

concepts.title: Optional Runtime Cloud egress
concepts.summary: Cloud is optional Runtime functionality. Gateway has no Cloud binding or credentials. A Runtime can explicitly select an attached Gateway as a restricted network exit; that selection changes transport, never Cloud ownership or independent access authority.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Independent enrollment
Runtime owns one Cloud association, owner-issued setup authorization and its existing Flowersec connection controller. Gateway attachment consent cannot authorize Cloud registration. Attachment lookup uses an explicit Gateway identity, or the sole attachment when unambiguous; a selected Cloud route never supplies a default attachment for general lookup or removal. Runtime may select a Gateway route before initial Cloud enrollment, using route/association revision zero; enrollment verifies the actual Cloud target when it becomes known.

Route operations retain an operation ID, expected revisions, target fingerprint, confirmation and queryable result. Changing an attachment, certificate, route or Cloud identity invalidates previous consent. An unknown result queries the original operation. A canceled committed operation remains committed.

## Local egress
New Gateways deny egress with an empty destination list. Host administrators configure exact canonical host:port destinations and per-attachment inherit/allow/deny overrides. Wildcards, URLs, paths, duplicate or malformed authorities are rejected. Executable policy uses attachment.admit, access.open and egress.open; no Cloud approval is consulted.

Admission requires the current Runtime attachment certificate, current local policy and unexpired credentials. The published Flowersec HTTPSProxy carries inner HTTPS without exporting Runtime Cloud keys. Public product policy rejects private resolved destinations; the isolated acceptance harness explicitly opts into its private fixture network. No unrestricted proxy or global proxy environment mutation is introduced.

Disabled egress closes only egress reservations. Independent reverse application streams remain available. Removing an attachment closes all streams depending on that attachment. Credential expiry and stale timers cannot restore withdrawn policy. Policy snapshots copy destination lists so callers cannot widen authority by mutating them.

The catalog's effective_egress_allowed is a policy decision, not a reachability result. It combines the active attachment, inherit/allow/deny and the hook decision for the current policy revision. Egress admission requires an active eligible attachment, its current unexpired client certificate and an allowed destination. The authenticated CONNECT request is independent of the reverse application connection: a disconnected reverse channel does not withdraw egress authority, while attachment removal, certificate replacement and policy revocation do. Only a completed route preflight proves the tested destination was reachable at that time. Empty destinations disable forwarding even when policy permission is true.

Reevaluate egress policy uses manage_network, applies only the selected attachment version and committed policy, and runs no application-health or Cloud-registration test. Unsaved editor changes remain drafts. Access.open hooks continue to evaluate individual sessions; this action does not reevaluate that domain.

## No fallback or cross-path revocation

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Authority ownership
Gateway owns its stable identity, paired client keys, Runtime attachments, local network policy and active transports. Runtime explicitly consents to each attachment and owns its application TLS identity, environment password/MFA, sessions and host execution restrictions. Gateway administration grants no Runtime lifecycle or application authority. Desktop and Web Center provide the environment directory and opening experience; Gateway catalogs only describe attached Runtimes. The authorized platform model gateway is a separate Cloud AI endpoint, not this service. Device access, host administration and Runtime application authorization are independently verified. Desktop and Web Center hold their own client identities; saved host coordinates and client observations confer no management authority.

Gateway has no Cloud machine registration, Namespace assignment, management renewal, delegated Runtime publication or Cloud command receiver. Runtime may independently enroll with Cloud. Gateway failure affects only traffic using that Gateway.

## Public and private endpoints
One advertised HTTPS origin serves client pairing/identity/catalog/application admission, Runtime invitation exchange/enrollment/mTLS attachment, and optional restricted egress. All advertised origins prove one stable Gateway identity. Host restrictions apply before protocol admission. The public handler never mounts management or operation-query routes.

The native Gateway packages support Linux and macOS. Administration uses a temporary private directory (0700), Unix socket (0600), and private host credential. SSH/container bridges reach that same host socket. A loopback TCP address or request header is not host proof. Windows Desktop manages remote/container Gateways; this change does not introduce a native Windows Gateway package or named-pipe implementation.

## State and lifecycle
Gateway state schema 6 owns local attachments and policy; authority epoch 70 owns the independent Gateway wire break. Unsupported attachment state and retired cloud-access.json fail before creating identities or rewriting data. Desktop saved-connection schema 5 migrates its local locator to connection_id while retaining the independently pinned gateway_id and device credentials.

Trust schema 4 removes historical host classification while preserving every device identity and revocation. Attachment schema 6 and saved-connection schema 5 do not change. Runtime epoch 71 owns its new observation response; it does not advance Gateway epoch 70.

Explicit host maintenance is independent of client-device admission and prior service observations. Update and ordinary reinstall replace only the managed package, preserving configuration, identity and client access. Unsupported state still fails unchanged; reinstall is never an implicit schema migration.

Host-only configuration-reset requires an explicit existing state root, --confirm, a stopped service and valid existing private trust file. It archives Gateway-owned attachment, network/policy-hook, retired Cloud and host-operation configuration under a private configuration-history/reset-* directory, retaining device identity and revocations. Unsafe paths fail before moving files. A durable reset marker fences startup and repeat reset during interrupted file moves. Ordinary move failures roll back; uncertain failures retain the marker/archive for host inspection, never automatic replay. Reset requires reconnecting Runtimes and configuring network policy. Desktop exposes it as a separately confirmed reinstall option, prepares and verifies the package before reset, then starts and reconnects through host management. No public endpoint can invoke it.

Saving, refresh, pairing and attachment management never implicitly start a stopped service. Removing a Desktop connection does not remove remote attachments or stop its service. Release/build metadata is diagnostic; unrelated Runtime releases do not change Gateway authority.

concepts.title: Flower explicit long-thread qualification
concepts.summary: Complete conversations and responsive interaction are required. Run fixed-budget long-thread checks explicitly for acceptance/investigation, outside commit/integration/CI gates. sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Execution and evidence
Run `node scripts/check_flower_long_thread.mjs --fast` for focused regressions; omit the flag for sustained/browser qualification. Use frozen published Desktop/Env dependencies and visible composited Electron with production background-throttling policy. This explicit acceptance suite stays outside commit, integration and CI gates.

Record source/tree cleanliness, tools, dependencies, metrics and supervised cleanup. Product/dependency changes invalidate timing. Policy-only changes may cite unchanged-product evidence with its original source identity. Nonzero/interrupted runs, missing tests/tools/metrics or cleanup failure fail qualification. Preserve the 110 ms/21 commits/s negative regression and profile-exclusion test; no threshold/workload override or waiver.

## Correctness
Fast checks cover indexed records, bounded queues/windows, turn/disclosure identity, keyed disposal, local thinking, structural versus mutable dependencies, sealed bodies and incremental Markdown in Desktop's browser-conditioned Solid/jsdom configuration. Each sequence entry has one mounted owner: classify once, update live fields/first-prose boundaries and dispose removed owners. Read one token snapshot; retained entries must not grow dependencies. Reuse immutable partition/row identities, restored titles and admission-only visibility. Regressions include 2,400-row subscription/identity bounds, 600 retained rows, real browser arrival/DOM placement, plain/reactive cache ownership and user-only prompt history.

Per-group observers update changed blockers and dispose removed groups; a 600-group case rejects historical refolding. Body growth cannot advance restoration provenance. Root/child history scans preserve fresh motion. Correct anchors after synchronous completion render and before paint. Every-frame cold-history checks span preview/pending/large-Markdown completion during live generation and native upward wheel input: unintended drift <=1 CSS px, no owner loss, blank frames, duplicate items or malformed cells. Structural batches publish membership once after records are ready; coverage/immutable turn facts add no per-field observers. Cover reconnect, selection, input, approval and terminal state.

The sustained fixture uses real Service, published Floret and fake providers to create 500 canonical turns, 1,000 messages and 1,000 tools and verify all admitted content. No paid provider, user state, raw DB writes or product fallback. Independently produce mixed text/reasoning/Markdown at 80 updates/s, one tool/60 updates, initial 32 KiB body and >=600 seconds in one active turn. Shorter or accelerated fixtures cannot qualify it.

Export canonical terminal outcome/failure before waiting for UI completion; both canonical and observed completion must succeed. Through real history/disclosure controls, compare every generated prose/reasoning item and exact code blocks with canonical content/full Markdown. Reveal parents before children in reading mode, opening only each item's owning sequence; never force hidden clicks or disclosure state. Preserve drafts/focus/selection through drag. Synthetic floating output does not qualify terminal emulation. Responsive timing with a failed terminal fails.

Allow preparation, ten-minute output and complete inspection within the supervised fixture lifetime. A 1,200-row regression forbids geometry reads for preserved/appended baselines and verifies exact interior-gap height after removal. Actual folding protects focus/selection/inspection. Consume published Floret v7.103.1 linear active-path reads and same-read reuse without reconstructing journals or extending completion deadlines.

## History
Published Floret v7.106.1 supplies bounded transaction-local reads, validated ancestry locators and physical body batching. Preserve two-stage navigation, exact membership, budgets and scroll ownership; no new database layout/cache.

Run `scripts/qualify_flower_thread_open.mjs --fixture=<isolated-fixture.json> --output=<evidence.json> --history-scroll-steps=80` with `TestServerFlowerHistoryScrollQualification` for real HTTP decoding and native bidirectional scrolling. A separate `--visual-frames` run captures timestamped compositor JPEGs and section geometry, rejecting visible sections with forced-hidden content. Native automatic skipping must keep newly exposed sections paintable before delayed observers. Inspect frames for flashes, gaps, clipping and overlap. Capture cannot combine with profiling/tracing/opening-time thresholds and is not latency evidence. Retain canceled body/parent-event requests separately from HTTP/sync errors.

`--stability-seconds=1800` (maximum 3600) checks the same visible paragraph/table/code anchor every frame, rejects loading/error/owner-loss frames and compares collected heap plus DOM/document/listener counts. Retain reports. This settled-reading check complements, never replaces, the fixed 600-second/80 Hz active workload.

## Responsiveness
Sample idle/early/late/repeat on the same visible production UI with two PersistentFloatingWindows, >=12 monotonic seconds each. Assert both drafts throughout. Cancellation, release, blur or hidden document invalidates a sample. A nonfocusable Electron host uses the primary work-area origin and pointer isolation before showing, retaining composition, CDP input, DOM focus and interruption checks without native keyboard input.

Read counters before press. One CDP session sends press/move/release with no intervening backend calls. An independent 60 Hz producer cannot await dispatch. Require >=55 offered events/s, >=45 position commits/s and >=80% idle cadence. Budgets remain: drag P95 <=75 ms and work-minus-idle <=25 ms; >=95% prose markers with P95 <=250 ms; frame P95 <=25 ms; reactive P95 <=12 ms/max 50 ms; no main-thread task >=100 ms.

Pair complete MOUSE_DRAGGED async spans by process/identity/scope to compositor presentation; report coalesced/unpresented separately and require >=30 presented/s. Healthy rAF is not input proof. No profiling/screencast during timing or universal/photon claim.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Desktop supervises fixture/build/Electron/state/profile/ports and verifies cleanup. Keep source/lock/host-bound metrics and traces outside Git. The Go fixture exports private exclusive-create configuration/canonical evidence through an owner-selected directory handle; accept only finite nonnegative safe-integer HTTP counters, never response bodies/unknown fields. Dirty samples certify no commit. Seed complete canonical results once without reducing coverage.

Optimize stable inputs, keyed subscriptions, linear membership and bounded offscreen layout with reading/focus/selection pins. Retain DOM/disclosure through active growth: containment, not virtualization. Visit entries once per structural change; preserve partition keys through prepend/growth/completion and full order/history/drafts/choices. No throttling, suppressed output, extra lifecycle or shorter fixtures.

Floe owns floating mechanics; Redeven owns projection. During shared drag/resize, published shimmer pauses decorative paint without resetting identity/phase. One Flower gesture observer settles title/disclosure motion, keeps new titles readable, makes tool icons/activity static and removes optional tail-follow easing. Existing scroll ownership remains. Release/cancel/blur restores accessibility preferences; old arrivals never replay. Expanded reasoning shares this policy, normal reading stays smooth and content/terminal state remains live. Browser checks cover those transitions and preview drafts/selection; workloads/budgets stay fixed.

## Reproducible measurements
Compare baseline and candidate on the same host, browser version, source size and workload.

An SSH tunnel changes transport overhead and must be recorded.

| Metric | Definition and controlled viewer acceptance budget |
| --- | --- |
| Input to presented pixels | DOM key event through remote application to changed canvas pixels on the next animation frame; nearest-rank P95 of 20 samples below 150 ms in every mode |
| Input during motion | The same 20-sample measurement while document scroll continues; P95 below 250 ms, including Save data cadence |
| Presented FPS | At most one changed-canvas presentation per animation frame; Motion first at least 25 FPS during document scroll |
| Received payload | All incoming WebSocket data bytes, including JSON; excludes WebSocket/TLS/SSH framing and network retransmissions |
| Idle bandwidth | Below 0.25 Mb/s after settling; a fully unchanged document should send zero image bytes |
| Document-motion bandwidth | Below 5 Mb/s for Automatic/Clarity/Save data and 15 Mb/s for Motion first at the recorded source size |
| Decode work | No more than two current-target frames plus one retired decode; no reconnect on a picture change |
| First frame | Navigation to first decoded canvas presentation; excludes browser-process launch before the viewer attaches |

## Published-module product results
A sandboxed Chrome 153 client on Ubuntu passed all v0.21.0 viewer budgets over loopback, isolating capture, forwarding, decoding and presentation from networking:

| Application | Automatic Mb/s | Motion-first FPS | Static-input P95 across modes | Scrolling-input P95 across modes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chrome | 2.14 | 27.0 | 46–65 ms | 129–237 ms |
| Firefox | 4.37 | 37.4 | 65–81 ms | 99–231 ms |

## Input, cursor and lifecycle acceptance
Require independent app receipts/exact saved bytes, not dispatch/DOM focus. REDEVEN_TEST_DESKTOP_COMPONENT_STATE selects task-owned published combined resources. Missing CJK/emoji fonts neither invalidate exact strings nor qualify visible glyphs. TestInstalledDesktopApplicationTransport covers input/save, invalid clipboard with canceled dependent input, recreated manager/same helper, read-only rejection of unknown records and indefinite live first-window wait beyond40s.

Native0.22.19/Floe0.86.0 maps keys to Linux seat, confirms Unicode for other layouts and orders clipboard before paste. Never paste stale selection,replay text or release composition after scroll. macOS retains native authority; shared canvas extraction needs first-frame/toolbar/reconnect/stale-target tests and real fixture input. OS pointer appearance needs physical observation; page screenshots/decoded-image checks cannot prove it. Synthetic touch/composition cannot certify OS candidates/soft keyboard/physical pinch.

Lifecycle fixtures independently verify:
- Existing single-instance Mac reuse and survival after lease release;48s first-window wait without relaunch. Picker counts/literal titles preserve focus; cancel close/quit preserves app/pixels/sharing/retry.
- Unreadable/replaced surfaces never expire into closure; confirmed last-window closes established viewers. Linux dialog-only apps show native-size decoded dialogs.
- Stale quit rejects whole set before termination; unknown retains error/no inferred exit/retry. Read-only lists cannot quit/detach.
- Reload/network preserves process, suspends input/capture and frees buffers before same-session/current-credential reconnect. Successor revokes prior input/releases held keys/suspends capture.
- Distinct permission/lock recovery. Helper failure is sharing failure, not app exit: retire route/credential/buffers/helper before terminal publication; fence late callbacks and retain unknown pages.
- Unknown foreground/window rejects without replay/retargeting; missing decoder negotiates same-process images.

Toolbar: fixed bar/resizable content,320/390/1000px popovers, keyboard menus, separate close/confirmed quit, late dismissal/no replay. Native quit covers visible/windowless apps,cancel/stale generations. Run three-engine pointer/appearance via `pnpm --dir internal/envapp/ui_src test:host-application-browser`. Actual system grants remain explicit; save-dialog cancellation never permits force exit. [Platform behavior](../architecture/host-application-behavior.md) owns OS differences.

Runtime/companion deployment records its commit/helper/readiness separately from upstream release. concepts.title: ReDevPlugin target build toolchain
concepts.summary: Redeven prepares target C compilation and archiving alongside Rust before building the exact published ReDevPlugin source crate. macOS builds Linux static PIE with pinned Zig and the existing Rust LLD wrapper. This is product packaging ownership; it introduces no alternate plugin executor or upstream source dependency.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
`scripts/redevplugin_build_toolchain.json` pins Rust 1.98.0, Zig 0.16.0, official archive checksums and build-input files. The unified preparer selects the actual builder and requested target, prepares Rust, downloads Zig only when missing with HTTPS/checksum/bounded retries, then compiles C, archives it, links it into a Rust program and validates the resulting executable. Darwin native uses Apple tools; Linux native uses its C compiler and static libraries. A failed probe prevents costly package compilation.

macOS maps Linux amd64/arm64 to x86_64/aarch64 musl. Target-specific cc-rs CC/AR settings use private wrappers; the CC wrapper removes only the exact Rust triple injected by cc-rs, supplies Zig's target, PIC and disables Zig's implicit undefined-behavior instrumentation. Rust LLD remains responsible for static PIE; existing ELF architecture, interpreter and dynamic dependency rejection stay authoritative. No ambient target GCC or installed PATH Zig is assumed.

Desktop preflights before copying source or building UI/Go. Staging independently invokes the same owner. Development Cargo identity binds exact published crate digest, compiler versions, Zig archive/binary, target flags, wrapper and validation inputs. Desktop package-cache v2 binds host, target, input inventory, release manifest and source identity; older disposable entries rebuild. `REDEVEN_REDEVPLUGIN_TOOLCHAIN_CACHE` selects an absolute tool cache; `REDEVEN_TOOLCHAIN_OFFLINE=1` requires cached tools. Rust's narrower offline setting remains available.

Release-cache pruning recognizes only the namespaces generated by the release-source cache-key owner. It never descends into sibling toolchain, Cargo, source-package, plugin-manifest or unknown cache namespaces, in either startup or package-preparation mode. Toolchain preparation owns its temporary download, extraction and probe directories and removes them on completion or cancellation. This prevents another package request from unlinking an active Zig download or compiler input; disabling release temporary-file cleanup alone does not provide that protection.

Preparation distinguishes unavailable tools/cache, network acquisition, source compilation and artifact validation. Shipped locales provide the concise summaries; diagnostics retain original output. Compiler errors never trigger a network retry. Cancellation/timeout terminates the task-owned command group, escalates after two seconds, waits for close and cleans temporary state. Target replacement begins only after a complete package is prepared. Helper/package uploads use the existing bounded transfer budget rather than the short command budget. Checksums, signed release consumption, SBOM, provenance and product signing remain required.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Redeven owns compiler preparation, target packaging, cache isolation and product signing. Published ReDevPlugin owns execution, containment and Worker contracts; cross-compilation cannot qualify an upstream runtime defect. Native target execution and the production Desktop update path require separate acceptance; architecture emulation and main-process harnesses do not certify native containment or GUI interaction.

sections.title: Evidence
sections.body:
November4,2026:three deterministic cases reproduce release pruning unlinking open Zig archives,including package-preparation with temporary cleanup disabled. Namespace-limited traversal preserves tool/Cargo/source/manifest/unknown owners while obsolete release/assets still prune.

Unmocked Desktop main-process update starts empty toolchain/Cargo/package caches separately per target,prunes every100ms during actual download/extract/probes (>2300passes/target),builds checksummed published3.15.0 on macOSarm64,validates staticPIE/signature/evidence,installs and reaches runtime_ready on nativeamd64Linux/arm64Docker. Subsequent requests verify source-package cache. Offline absence/refused download/cancel preserve installed bytes/process inventory and leave no transient tool directories. These are production-method tests,not GUI clicks.

Earlier same-day first/cache build timings:amd64116/5s,arm64109/5s. Real Worker64MiBFS/HTTP and WS/TCP/UDP pass on both native targets;published cancel/isolation and hardenedDarwin pass functionally,without performance thresholds. amd64 emulation fails containment/final inventory and is not native substitute. Published3.15.0 duplicate TCP-close revocation error remains unaccepted despite closed resources/pending rejection;no unpublished fix consumed. [Prior qualification](redevplugin-performance-qualification.md) retains it.

After rebase preserving main,Floe0.90.4 passes154plugin browser/156focused Desktop/product integration;ordinary hooks all three groups pass.

- `redeven:scripts/prepare_redevplugin_build_toolchain.mjs:1` - Compiler preparation owner.

concepts.title: ReDevPlugin 3.15 performance qualification
concepts.summary:
ReDevPlugin 3.15.0 improves measured warm execution and Redeven restores only
initially visible plugin placements. Opened surfaces retain their independent
slots, drafts, selection and pending work when hidden. This is conditional lazy
opening, not a concurrency cap or iframe reuse. Platform mechanisms and release
ownership remain in [the host boundary](../architecture/redevplugin-boundary.md).

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Consume the coordinated published Go/npm/Rust release, without local overrides.
Rust 1.98.0 builds the Wasmtime 50 runtime. The macOS helper keeps hardened
runtime with exactly the executable-memory exception required by upstream;
staging, cache identity and consumption verify the actual signed entitlement.
The executable is product-built; source-package provenance is not product
signing evidence. Release signing still requires the product identity.

Each first open captures current context/revision. Unopened close succeeds and
prevents later opening. Visibility never cancels an already started invocation,
replays an uncertain write or reuses revoked authority. Ordinary Worker errors
remain application-owned; they do not destroy a Surface. See
[recovery](../architecture/redevplugin-surface-recovery.md).

sections.title: Measurement
sections.body:
November 3, 2026, macOS/arm64, Node 26.7.0, Go 1.27.3 and Rust 1.98.0. Redeven
baseline is 2433435341c55aa34013de78c1ab023277d96639. Both UI variants use published
ReDevPlugin 3.15.0/Floe 0.87.2 and the same production Integration HTTP server,
including durable Host state. The old component alone is substituted in the
test build. Fifteen alternating fresh-browser pairs per scenario produce 60
trials; paired ratios use 10,000 deterministic bootstrap resamples.

| Scenario | Baseline median | Candidate median | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| One visible placement, active ready | 132.4 ms | 57.5 ms | Paired 2.315x, 95% interval 2.167–2.371 |
| One visible, incremental process-tree RSS | 867.59 MiB | 105.86 MiB | 87.8% less; ten frames versus one |
| First deferred activation | 0.1 ms | 49.1 ms | Candidate P95 53.99 ms; explicit first-use cost |
| Ten visible, all ready | 134.3 ms | 133.8 ms | No material regression; ten independent frames |
| Fresh Worker process/state, total | 335.68 ms | 504.05 ms | +168.37 ms; below predeclared 1 s echo budget |
| First Worker call | 6.05 ms | 4.39 ms | Excludes setup |
| 64 KV writes, individual versus batch | 225.5 ms | 4.55 ms | Paired 50.34x; exact values and rollback |
| Six schema statements, individual versus transaction | 48.15 ms | 8.15 ms | Paired 5.63x; trigger behavior retained |

Cold results use fifteen alternating pairs with identical historical 3.14 echo
guest bytes, fresh Integration/process/plugin state and warm OS file cache.
Candidate install/grant/prewarm is 186.86 ms versus 78.49 ms. Current 3.15 author
output also passes a separate live hardened-runtime smoke. These are not heavy
editor startup or network SLAs. Batch figures compare existing transports under
3.15, not a claim that every plugin becomes 50x faster. The six-statement case
does not measure complete Memos Worker bootstrap.

The product resource path preserves 1/32 MiB content; observed read chunks are
at most 2 MiB. Upload source Blobs are resident, so no bounded upload-memory
claim is made. Process-tree RSS includes shared pages and is not a leak proof.

Upstream paired production calls (ten rounds) reduce C4/C8 P95 from
7.721/15.530 ms to 4.165/7.662 ms; throughput increases from 765/735 to
1,751/1,662 requests/s. Mix/sort full-call paired speedups are 3.98x/8.49x.
Implementation attribution is b314dc13590bacb756579fc509334dd69ef1520b;
8b9b9fc12e273f86091a9d1029d7adb1ecdd43cf adds hardened-runtime qualification.
Both feature and main 13-stage gates, Quick CI and v3.15.0 public completion
passed. Release manifest SHA256 is
335563f292c5302b21a8cb93cf151b2882bc408f28792285d4c88c1deb572d5c.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
These observations qualify only their recorded workloads, releases and sources. Resource RSS includes shared pages/retained allocations; bounded endurance is not leak proof. Different author guests prevent paired throughput/memory comparison. Deferred opening is neither a concurrency cap nor iframe reuse.

Do not infer arbitrary native-library, shell, WASI or sandbox-escape support. Measurements justify no Store pool, persistent native cache, wider SQLite pool or four-surface cap. Production tracing is not a new public contract. The separate complete Desktop I/O workflow remains unqualified pending the release/native work recorded below.

sections.title: Evidence
sections.body:
## Qualification outcomes
Component tests cover reveal/visibility/opening/close/disposal, context/retry, unknown outcomes and sibling retirement. Production resource/UI fixtures verify input, native undo, selection, veto, focus, fresh origins and zero final frames. Upstream finite fuel/deadlines, memory, cancel/revoke, Linux static PIE/clone3/seccomp and macOS hardened workloads pass. Product Docker lifecycle, published-source consumption and live author execution pass. An isolated native Desktop starts its local environment/Plugin Center and its bundled signed runtime executes the published author Worker through production Integration; this alone is not full Desktop I/O acceptance.

Both independent 30-minute endurance runs pass. Browser: 100 unique-origin churn cycles, 357 input/visibility/selection checks, native undo/veto/sibling preservation; final frames, page/HTTP errors and guest long tasks all zero. Input+switch P95: candidate 22.83 ms, baseline 23.02 ms. Candidate process-tree RSS: 1,065.02 MiB initial, 502.25 MiB last live, 505.95 MiB after cleanup. Worker: 30m4.40s, 359 batches, 1,436 correct calls, 359 expected application rejections, three gateway renewals and successful Integration close/host-runtime exit. RSS: 71.55/63.78/78.13 MiB initial/final/peak. Baseline: 30 minutes, 1,432 correct calls, 358 expected rejections; author guests differ.

Expanded acceptance found Floe 0.87.2 Monokai hover contrast 4.3187 below the unchanged 4.5 threshold. Upstream 0.87.3 fixes the foreground; consumed Floe 0.90.0 includes it. All 168 upstream theme/variant/engine cases pass; hover is 4.6178. Product 28-theme comparison and connection/management/Workbench checks pass: 154 browser cases requalified on 0.90.0 after concurrent main changes. Single-line actions assert exact 16-pixel layout/scroll heights before/after selection, avoiding transformed rounding.

The Desktop fixture uses published Worker SDK/reviewed connection contracts. Product adapter/localized review require effective admin/read/write/execute authority and exact private prefixes. Isolated Linux uses authenticated public Local UI. Actual Worker I/O verifies 64 MiB filesystem SHA256, 64 one-MiB HTTP requests/direction, oversize rejection and 100 WS/TCP/UDP echoes each without changing released quotas. Native Desktop checks installed inventory while paused, panel dismissal and five reopens; market failure no longer suppresses installed refresh.

Native revocation exposed upstream TCP close-after-cancel returning an erroneous unknown mutation despite closed resources. Deterministic TCP/UDP regressions and focused/performance/stress/property gates pass for the fix. The 3.15.1 exact-main gate/Quick CI passed but immutable Linux source qualification failed: the runaway test could hit its independent deadline before fuel exhaustion. 3.15.2 sets a small test fuel budget and asserts typed failure, changing no production policy. At 0.1 CPU, original fails/ten corrected runs pass; all 186 Linux runtime tests pass. Its 13-stage feature gate passes, including first-attempt performance, 64 revoke acknowledgements at 1 ms P95 versus 500 ms and hardened macOS execution. Public release completion/downstream native requalification remain pending; this is not a complete Desktop I/O pass.

## Provenance

- External evidence: redevplugin-implementation, November 3, 2026, task 01a1a274-ecbc-7370-8ebf-e111bf8adee9. Raw trials/harnesses/source identities/failures/acceptance ledger are evidence, not dependencies/configuration.

sections.body:

Retain every complete pair, immutable candidate/fixture identity, source/response count, missing presentation and exclusion reason. Retry only a named fixture repair or discriminating hypothesis, changing one variable. CPU is percent of one core; whole-tree resources and incremental Viewer costs remain distinct, never silently replaced by baseline subtraction.

Adopt published v0.22.48 optional negotiated six-frame Linux delivery; retain legacy/macOS four-frame behavior and unsupported Windows physical capture. Before retrying the first-round tail, correlate capture/encode, accepted write, encrypted transport, decode and confirmed paint with bounded clock uncertainty. Outbound stalls alone cannot isolate SSH/kernel/network/client scheduling; unchanged runs are not diagnosis.

## Published preparation
Read C01 crossover, C02 receipt rejection, C03/C04 window comparison and P03/P04 timing history before C05. Bound motion samplers at 300 seconds and use two 50-click batches to avoid the C04 timeout. Rebuild fixtures with new process identities; never join pre/post-reboot intervals or reuse stale credentials/geometry. Restore verified SHA-checked published native service after diagnostics; exclude credentials.

## Experiment decisions
C01 is historical counterevidence. C02 receipt batching has no production benefit; C03 exhausted-window timer is rejected. C04 supports optional Linux six-frame throughput, not parity, recovery or causality. Git retains older procedures; C05 owns current outcomes.

## Comparison criteria
Official baseline: RustDesk `1.5.0`, source `fada664df7a294d1d1a9ca3e7cd3637069122f17`. Three paired alternating rounds retain physical output, resolution, refresh, content viewport and delivered detail quality, with one measured Viewer at a time.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Results apply only to recorded hardware/path/workload/published versions/fixture and valid intervals. Missing source input invalidates ordinal latency association; missing presentation with complete source input is an adverse result. Later favorable rounds erase neither earlier failures nor uncertainty about cause. Cross-time measurements do not prove causality.

Release/compatibility gates qualify only named contracts, not LAN performance. A reboot creates a distinct fixture identity. Unsupported physical platforms inherit no Linux qualification; hardware decode/photon latency remain unclaimed. Performance never waives security, authorization, input, ordering or recovery.

sections.title: Evidence
sections.body:

Full parity, historical repeatability and three-round stability remain unaccepted; 52–53 FPS diagnostic peaks cannot replace them.

concepts.title: Gateway v6 independent device protocol
concepts.summary: Gateway v6, authority epoch 70, defines independent client-device trust and Runtime attachments. The public protocol and private host API are separate surfaces on the same service, with independently verified device access and host authority. Cloud machine management and publication are absent.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Identities and wire fields
The stable gateway_id is independent of Desktop connection_id. RuntimeAttachment uses attachment_id and attachment_version. Catalogs contain attachments; Gateway metadata contains endpoints and tls_root_pem shared by clients and Runtimes. Device identities are not user memberships. Internal package/file names do not add a Cloud or user authority.

Client public routes are pairing/challenge, pairing/complete, identity, catalog, access/open and access/service under /gateway/v6. Runtime-owned routes use /v6/attachment for invitation-exchange, join, cancel-join, update-endpoints, rotate, leave and connect. Current attachment certificate/version and signed Runtime service identity are required.

Host-only routes issue invitations/client codes, list/revoke devices, update addresses/network/egress policy, remove or reevaluate attachments and query operation results. They are not registered on the public listener. ManageAttachments and ManageNetwork are request capabilities from verified host context, never device roles. Host proof grants both together; network settings, shared endpoint edits and attachment egress reevaluation consistently check ManageNetwork. Client trust administration requires current private host proof. OpenAPI declares each route surface explicitly. This alignment changes no route or signed payload, so protocol v6, epoch 70 and attachment schema 6 remain unchanged. Trust schema 4 retires historical host classification without replacing identities. Private host authentication is independent of device access; supplied signatures must still verify and address proofs retain their requested binding audience.

## Freshness and state
Runtime metadata versions do not gate attachment admission. Wire/authority mismatches fail explicitly; no old protocol translator or Cloud fallback is installed. Schema 6 attachment state rejects unsupported input unchanged. Expected attachment and policy versions fence relevant mutations; operation IDs recover known results and preserve uncertainty.

The runtime alone carries exactly com.apple.security.cs.allow-unsigned-executable-memory=true for Wasmtime executable pages. Keep hardened runtime and library validation; do not grant the exception to Desktop shell or plugin documents. Staging and macOS consumption verify the signed entitlement dictionary and hardened flag, not just the source plist. Development Cargo cache identity includes signing profile and verifier bytes. Emit binary/SPDX/resolved provenance/notices/signature/certificate. Release Sigstore binds tag workflow; ephemeral Ed25519 fails --require-release. Cosign3 flags --new-bundle-format=false/--use-signing-config=false retain workflow/OIDC/transparency checks.

redeven.redevplugin_runtime_build.v1 binds publication/product files/target/tools/source/workflow/signer. Consumption rechecks descriptor/target/profile/signature. Startup uses expected marker digest, never self-hashed trust. Runtime archive exactly Redeven/ReDevPlugin runtime/six evidence files/license/notices.

## Desktop/collector
Before .bundle/<target> replacement validate name/closed flat inventory/Go target/native policy. Gateway separate; full evidence beside Redeven. macOS exclusion matches only independently signed runtime; preserve its bytes/evidence while Redeven/Computer/Sparkle/bridge remain signable. After Electron assembly copy full Computer resources/licenses. Validate startup before signing and after refreshing only signer-visited Runtime/Computer descriptors, just before outer seal.

Inspect final DEB/RPM/read-only DMG; emit v2 installer-bound runtime/six-file receipts. Upload installers/receipts/latest-linux*.yml only. Apple tools/system text suffice without rg; consume full pipefail pipelines. Require Team/signature/hardening/updater key/staple/distribution; Sparkle lipo places binary before -verify_arch. Linux relink source/object archives separate. Derive epoch/windows from reviewed contract, normalize feeds before signed inventory.

DEB: POSIX ustar/GNU regular files/directories,bounded long names,metadata-only root. RPM disables build-id symlinks. Bounded no-follow snapshots reject noncanonical/duplicate paths, links/devices,privileged modes,sparse/PAX,malformed trailers/trailing bytes/oversize.

Collector requires four Runtime/Gateway,four Desktop,two Center directories. Exact inventory:four Redeven/four Gateway archives,two DEBs/two RPMs/two DMGs,six receipts/identical shared metadata and two Center archives/receipts per [CI](ci-and-release-gates.md). Open once no-follow,hash/copy same descriptor,check inode/metadata,fsync/link without replacement; delete partial output on failure.

Internal Windows managed_wsl_archive binds one Linux amd64 archive to version/source/size/digest and rejects redeven.exe. Formal collector rejects all Windows until signing/update certification, never optional fifth target.

Final release requires release-only consumption,signed checksums/safe_extract_tar.py,complete draft name/size/hash readback before publish. [Installer](self-contained-installer.md) owns verify-before-run/immutable activation/retention.

concepts.title: Self-contained installer distribution
concepts.summary: Release builds macOS/Linux amd64/arm64 self-contained installers without CGO and renders entry from exact binary digests, all signed via SHA256SUMS. Receiving hosts need no Go/Cosign/Python/OpenSSL/package manager, but require shell, HTTPS downloader and SHA256 utility.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Trust and acquisition
The HTTPS bootstrap is the initial trust boundary. Its reviewed fixed digest authenticates the installer before execution. Upstream Cosign Blob API verifies exact repository workflow, OIDC issuer and tag through authenticated TUF roots, certificate transparency and Rekor. Accept detached .sig plus PEM/base 64 PEM only; no format guessing, mutable trust overrides, disabled verification or fabricated markers. Signature/digest failure never executes Runtime.

TUF requests are cancellable/time-bounded without writing user trust cache. Bound log responses before SDK parsing and admit detached X.509 hashedrekord/0.0.1 only; reject OpenPGP-capable/other types before the general parser. Pass unchanged bytes to upstream cryptographic checks.

Default installation resolves GitHub latest unless an exact version is supplied. Explicit managed channel uses the public version manifest and GitHub-first sources; self-upgrade environment semantics remain. Automatic resolution cannot downgrade a known version; explicit rollback can.

## Activation transaction
A no-follow nonblocking lock serializes the root. Closed bounded archive membership rejects links, duplicates, traversal, missing/extra files, bad trailers and changed bytes. Published artifact-cache owns verified acquisition/storage.

Stage complete suites in .redeven-runtime-suites/<archive-sha256>, sync, read back digests/inventory/version and prepare pinned ripgrep before atomic redeven symlink replacement. Ripgrep 15.2.0 uses Linux musl archives on both architectures. New/reused executables must actually run and report that version; missing loader, timeout, wrong version or oversized output leaves prior activation unchanged. Detect concurrent changes; restore and verify prior entry after post-switch failure. Distinguish unchanged from committed-but-unconfirmed errors.

Retain published suites and legacy flat resources: live older processes can still need them after multiple upgrades. Installer owns no process lifetime, so removal needs an explicit unused/rollback assessment; disk usage grows with distinct archives.

Fresh install uses a writable user directory without implicit sudo. Idempotent bash/zsh/fish blocks update future PATH; print the current-shell command or direct path for unknown shells. Upgrade changes no shell profile and starts/restarts no service. Runtime owns maintenance/re-exec after success.

## Publication and promotion
From v0.13.13, authenticated redeven-installer-contract.json declares minimum installer, closed targets and archive contract; older installers stop before incompatible acquisition. Render GitHub and Portal bootstraps from one template and four actual installer hashes; sign both through aggregate checksums. Portal uses its official mirror fallback, not another implementation.

Publish assets with --latest=false. Before promotion, check-distribution authenticates inventory/contract and each bootstrap's complete digest, tag, channel and four pins without relying on the current default. After promotion, --check-active-entry requires GitHub byte equality; Portal authenticates its active bootstrap against its own signed release and candidate minimum installer, permitting an older recommended Runtime. Read back GitHub's default independently.

README selects generated GitHub bootstrap; The Portal UI and install endpoint redirect to the generated Portal entry under its channel contract. Redirects confer no signature trust. No placeholder hashes/missing assets may activate. Public deployment is explicit. Rollback selects compatible immutable signed releases, never obsolete external-tool installers or duplicated shell code. Historical upgrade/native execution/page integration remain explicit acceptance, outside ordinary push gates.

## Dependency security
Consume checksum-verified published Cosign/Rekor patches. Require go-jose >=4.1.6 and no imported legacy golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp packages; preserve identity, signing time, roots and transparency. Qualify official releases plus tampering/cross-tag denial. The distinct general SDK OpenPGP finding and its format-rejection boundary remain documented below; a nonzero scanner is never a clean audit.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:

The bootstrap cannot defend against compromise of its original HTTPS script.
Cross-compilation alone does not certify execution on every target OS.

The dependency audit fixes the reviewed gRPC findings by selecting released
`v1.83.1`. The general SDK still imports the deprecated OpenPGP implementation
reported by `GO-2026-5932`; symbol scanning can continue to report it. The
installer rejects those input formats before SDK parsing. Do not describe a
nonzero scanner result as a clean audit, add a blanket suppression, or remove
this boundary without reviewing the upstream replacement and genuine fixtures.

Maintained knowledge describes stable boundaries and does not need a prose rewrite for each version number.

A failed gate can leave a candidate on the ephemeral runner's local main, but it is never published. Each run removes only its own temporary worktree and private branch.

concepts.title: Local UI exposure, HTTPS identity and explicit certificate changes

frontmatter.title: Local UI exposure, HTTPS identity and explicit certificate changes

concepts.summary: Runtime owns public listeners, saved HTTPS identity and session admission; Desktop presents explicit next-start changes. Network exposure requires concrete authority and password, while certificate trust remains a separate user action. TLS failures never downgrade or expose the private Desktop bridge.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Network exposure
### HTTPS certificate ownership
[Local UI certificates](#certificates) owns creation, import, replacement, removal, validation, and client trust. It never creates or repairs certificate material, installs trust, or falls back to HTTP. Certificate replacement affects the next start; the running TLS identity and sessions remain intact.

### Listener and origin boundary
The public listener accepts only canonical authorities derived from its actual bound addresses.
An HTTP loopback listener also routes the exact plugin child origins derived
from its current parent authority and port exclusively to ReDevPlugin's Web
resource handler. Child routing strips parent credentials and never enters
Local UI management. A removed parent, different port, network-only address,
or HTTPS listener cannot use this loopback resource route. The platform still
validates each asset session, origin, ticket, and surface lifetime.

Its isolated `flowersec-private-loopback/1` profile is unchanged and cannot authorize public clients.

### Native Desktop default-port recovery
Only native Desktop launches with saved default `localhost:23998` and no explicit one-start bind override opt in through `--local-ui-default-port-fallback`. Other errors, custom ports, numeric loopback overrides, network binds, and wildcard binds never silently select another port.

External bookmarks containing the old fixed port cannot follow the temporary address.

### Network changes and current reports
While network exposure is enabled, Runtime enumerates eligible interfaces every two seconds. Its public list is explicit, including `[]`; private bridge endpoints cannot supply missing public addresses.

Address failures affect public availability and never assert that the Runtime process has stopped or expose private management URLs.

### Admission and lifecycle
A network listener starts only for a concrete non-loopback IP or wildcard with a fixed nonzero port and an effective password.

Occupied explicit ports fail with a startup error instead of silently selecting another port.

Flowersec owns admission, session establishment, liveness, handler dispatch, close, and lease release; Redeven does not copy those loops.

### Server-owned access configuration
[Runtime two-factor authentication](runtime-two-factor-authentication.md) owns the persistent credential authority, one-time bcrypt verifier migration, TOTP enrollment, recovery, replay protection, and ordinary-session revocation. Explicit password changes remain next-start settings when MFA is disabled; MFA-enabled settings cannot clear/replace that password or downgrade HTTPS.

Failed catalog saves roll back verifier initialization as well as replacement and clearing.

## Certificates
### Identity and trust
The user explicitly creates a device CA with `local-authority device-ca generate` and inspects it with `status`. Runtime startup never generates, replaces, or repairs certificate material.

Public export contains certificate material only, never the key.

### Explicit certificate changes
`import`, `regenerate`, and `remove` require `--confirm`. Reject malformed or extraneous PEM blocks, trailing text, encrypted/mismatched keys, invalid dates, invalid chains, missing SANs, and certificates unsuitable for server authentication.

This supports process-interruption recovery; it does not promise an OS trust rollback or filesystem power-loss durability.

### Coverage during network changes
[Local UI network exposure](#network-exposure) owns the two-second interface refresh and atomic public snapshot.

A signing failure retains only current addresses covered by the previous valid leaf and reports `certificate_refresh_failed`; retries recover automatically. Startup and explicit saved-identity preflight retain their strict validation boundary.

### Desktop interaction and private input
The compact HTTPS panel presents certificate validity, expiry, and system trust separately. Public path, fingerprint, and bounded selectable diagnostics live in the expandable details section.

Saving next-start HTTPS settings remains possible with an unusable certificate, with an explicit startup warning.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Installing trust in each HTTPS client is an explicit user action outside Runtime startup. Browser capabilities requiring a secure context remain unavailable with feature-specific guidance; browser security is never disabled. The private Desktop profile still requires exact preload provenance and numeric loopback, independently of explicit public HTTP support.

Runtime owns saved identity validation and replacement; Desktop owns explicit management presentation and private file acquisition. Certificate operations cannot silently restart Runtime, install system-wide trust, or expose private material to the renderer.

concepts.title: Permission policy and filesystem scope
concepts.summary: Runtime policy is authoritative even after control-plane session authorization. Clamp grants by local permission policy and scope every file-facing feature to explicit directory roots. Product controls present that decision; they never widen permissions or infer access from paths.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism
The local permission policy is a three-bit read/write/execute cap.

Explicitly configured read-only roots remain read-only; session caps, canonical path boundaries, and host filesystem permissions still constrain every operation.

Redeven persists only product authorization audit and does not maintain an approval queue, receipt, generation, revision, or recovery lifecycle.

## Descriptor-based reads

Repository-rule discovery and delivered-file reads use Registry.OpenRead. It
resolves current policy, rechecks the selected root, walks canonical components
through pinned os.Root handles, rejects substituted symlinks and compares opened
identities before returning a descriptor. Metadata comes from that descriptor.
A previously authorized pathname is not a reusable read capability.

sections.title: Boundaries

Browser state, display-only Home hints, provider metadata, and UI affordances cannot widen runtime permissions.

Provider wire configuration may enable multi-call generation, but it cannot grant permission, bypass approval, or alter runtime scheduling.

concepts.title: Plugin platform integration security
concepts.summary: ReDevPlugin accepts authenticated host identity and source policy, never browser-claimed trust. HTTP checks auth/origin/CSRF/action; direct calls check owner/action/resource. Source identity, execution approval, update eligibility and permissions remain independent and fail closed on identity or scope mismatch.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Sessions and permissions
process.local is an explicit high-risk grant, rechecked by method on every Worker Process Broker call. Hosts inherit neither the complete Redeven environment nor session cookies/plugin tokens/credentials. [Process sessions](../architecture/plugin-process-sessions.md) owns lifecycle.

Resolve only stored channel metadata with exact nonempty channel/user/environment identities. Cache by owner-session hash; all four hashes must match. No guessed owner sweeps or local teardown registries.

Canonical HTTP route: /_redevplugin/api/plugins. Resolve method effects before local policy clamps; shared runtime management stays admin-only. Plugin Center reads grants and explicit policies via released APIs, never registry writes/default catalog grants. Catalog identity is not permission. Official/community classifies repository origin for display only.

## Package and network admission
Install/update validates source policy, publisher/plugin/version, exact package hashes and Host capability contracts. Plugin signatures, trusted-publisher admission and release references are absent. Reject malformed content, fabricated provenance, owner/scope mismatch, unapproved source changes and same-version content replacement. Explicit consent and durable request receipts bind installation; permissions and runtime revocation remain independent.

VPN/proxy/enterprise DNS is routing, not evidence of malice. Package downloads retain source/redirect/integrity checks through normal host routing. Authorized HTTPS connectors use released transport after grants; routing grants no extra destinations/methods, private-prefix bypass or ambient credentials. Proxy discovery/timeouts/TLS failures reject only their operation. Construction performs no discovery; plugin readiness cannot gate core Runtime. Keep TLS validation; proxy credentials stay on that hop. Never retry writes with unknown outcomes.

## Confirmation and runtime trust
Validate capability preflight against the Host-known response schema before confirmation. Reserved redevplugin.capability.risk_plan.* values must satisfy strict v1: reject unknown/malformed reserved versions without generic fallback. Replacement/replay needs new confirmation.

Descriptors bind version/target/IPC/WASM ABI/artifact hash. Darwin Developer ID signing precedes product digest/Sigstore evidence; Desktop signing preserves those nested bytes. Startup cannot trust a digest computed from its own field binary.

Business adapters run only after platform lifecycle/permission/confirmation/lease/quota/revocation/audit resolution. Never expose raw errors, tokens/secrets/cookies/query strings/absolute paths/full URLs in public or durable diagnostics.

## Web isolation
Plugin documents use distinct product origins and the published surface handler. Local UI/AppServer strip parent auth before delegation. Desktop binds private bridge credentials to actual frame origin. Frame-less workers instead require Electron's initiator origin in the owning Runtime partition, matching the exact private origin; missing/opaque origins fail. Present frames remain authoritative. Workers inherit no frame-only host-access/Tessiven claims. Center binds child routes to authenticated parents and cancels preparation on revocation; Gateway checks expected namespace/target.

Plugin DOM/rendering freedom grants no product-session/filesystem/process/credential/management authority. Released platform owns asset sessions/bridge/permissions/revocation.

Main-process session.fetch also enters Electron's hook. Contextless other requests retain authorization only with exactly one already-present matching private bridge token from the owning Runtime session and no frame/WebContents/initiator. Missing provenance grants nothing; destination must still be the exact private origin. Renderer/worker provenance remains authoritative; never inherit frame-only claims.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Desktop control tokens, direct sessions, Gateway/RCPP credentials and Flower grants are not ambient plugin authority. Redeven adapters may narrow authority, never mint platform tokens, weaken routes, edit opaque state or replace released brokers.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Session authority and lifetime
The gate alone decides channel authorization when registering the channel and its lifetime cancellation callback under one lock. Callers supply verified private-management identity or an ordinary login session ID, never an `unlocked` assertion.

Runtime restart clears in-memory sessions and incomplete operations; it preserves committed authentication state.

EnvAppShell binds remote access readiness to the exact connected client after access.status/access.resume succeeds. Each replacement channel must confirm access independently; late success or failure from a retired channel cannot authorize or disconnect its replacement. Protected Terminal catalog loading consumes this readiness, never transport connectivity alone. Local transport retains its Runtime-authorized channel admission contract.

## Browser Cookie scope and continuity
Local UI alone issues, reads and clears `redeven_local_access_<http|https>_<port>`. Forwarded headers cannot select the scope.

Only an incorrect password or factor produces input validation feedback; transport failures and cooldowns retain their own messages.

## Desktop consumption and forwarding
Desktop Flower retains the complete Runtime-issued access-cookie `name=value` pair and returns it unchanged. It never derives the name from a bridge or forwarded client port.

No upstream platform capability changes are required for this product authentication policy.

sections.title: Boundaries

Center login cannot replace Runtime accessgate or create Desktop management. [Center security](web-center-access.md) owns the independent entry authority.

Desktop Web Service handoff cookies are HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict.

Cookies isolate presentation scopes but cannot extend or create authorization.

Native transport never acquires trusted Desktop management identity.

Native/SSH management has separate authority; missing/corrupt state fails closed and recovery blocks access until new credentials commit.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Enrollment and management
Desktop Environment Settings / Access presents one two-factor row. If a different environment password has been saved for the next start, restart before configuring MFA; the old running verifier cannot overwrite the newer saved authority.

These commands do not alter SSH keys, sshd policy, PAM, host passwords, or execution identity.

## Session authority
[Runtime access sessions](runtime-access-sessions.md) owns ordinary session deadlines, browser Cookie scope and refresh continuity, challenge binding, native editor delegation, and revocation. MFA management changes revoke ordinary authority through that single gate; they do not create a second browser or Desktop authentication lifecycle.

## Persistence, replay and recovery
`access-auth.sqlite` is a versioned, private SQLite authority, separate from the transport authorization database. The committed database and initialized key become the sole authority; deletion, malformed data, unsafe modes, symlinks, unknown schema, or key loss cannot fall back to the retired verifier.

Authentication state and secrets are not diagnostic export inputs.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Password-only challenges grant no ordinary product data access. Loopback addresses, Cloud administrator claims and forwarded headers cannot establish private host authority. concepts.summary: Center has one administrator and multiple devices. Center, Gateway and Runtime authorize independently: directory/open access never bypasses Runtime login or grants host management. Device revocation cancels all derived admissions while retaining unrelated devices and routes.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Setup/storage
Owner redeven-center setup --state-root issues a mandatory15-minute credential. Password/verified TOTP/recovery-code confirmation commit atomically; partial setup grants nothing. Passwords:12–72 UTF-8 bytes; recovery codes replace only factor.

Unix socket checks service UID/root, never SSH/tunnel/loopback/header claims. recover fences business and authorizes setup; recover --offline --origin needs stopped exclusive state. Unsupported peer checks fail.

Exclusive lock protects AES-GCM SQLite. center.key pins instance/origin/initialization; missing/corrupt committed state fails. Back up key/database together. DTOs omit secrets/private keys; only owner commands print temporary credentials. Audit keeps closed sensitive-action categories, never payload/credential-derived digest. Expiring challenges/grants alone bind exact actions; bcrypt verifies passwords. Schema2 atomically redacts v1 audit refs before readiness, preserving events/unrelated state; damaged/future stores stay unchanged.

## Authentication
Password creates a five-minute browser/action/session/revision challenge, <=five factor failures; password alone grants nothing. Atomic TOTP-step/recovery consumption survives restart. Login rotates device/browser sessions; security changes revoke sessions/challenges/grants/connections.

Limit16 devices, one-hour idle/twelve-hour absolute sessions. Only trusted visible input renews idle, never frozen pages/output/polls/heartbeat. Revocation preserves other devices; restart invalidates sessions but retains credentials/directory/audit.

Sensitive changes need fresh password/factor and ten-minute action/target/payload/revision grants. Password-change bindings use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256,600000 iterations/32 bytes, domain-separated random login-device-ID salt, mirrored in Web Crypto; no raw-password SHA256. Recheck expiry/revision/session after derivation. Bounded same-session/request receipts prevent repeated effects. Viewing/opening valid sessions needs no extra MFA.

## Admission
Bound auth concurrency and persist administrator/direct-peer budgets through restart. Failures back off/expire, never permanently lock. Forwarded headers cannot select identity. Revocation/recovery cancels catalog/pairing; limits2/device/source,8/device,32 global preserve logout/other sources.

Limits:16 Gateways,128 routes,128 receipts (<=32/device),16 live root/child operations/device; concurrent proxy16/access-owner,48/device,192 total. Reopening cannot monopolize receipts. Revoke live admission immediately; five-minute tombstones retain outcomes. Bound JSON/headers, stream files, restrict egress to signed approved endpoints.

Child reopen makes fresh browser handoff and reuses authority only for exact parent/resource-kind/ID/Runtime-instance/login-cookie-name/value; paths may vary within resource. Cancel/expire repeated handoff preserves existing owner; owner revoke invalidates pending reuse. Reuse consumes bounded receipts and cannot bypass resource limits.

Runtime accessgate owns login/channels. Binding/revision/device scope prevents cross-route/device replay; children add resource scope. Binding revoke fences admission/channels, not unrelated paths. Children cannot invoke Env APIs, spend sibling artifacts or set parent cookies. Changed proofs fail without downgrade. Deny portal framing; child framing follows Runtime.

concepts.title: Adaptive desktop and mobile navigation
concepts.summary: Desktop and mobile remain distinct interaction modes; narrow desktop regions use temporary drawers without rewriting saved placement. Mobile panels and Flower navigation preserve business-page/editor identity and explicit focus choices. Published geometry controls safe areas without product drag or snap lifecycles.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Desktop adaptation
### One interaction mode
Desktop Welcome and Desktop-hosted Env App configure `mobileQuery: 'not all'`; the Env App recognizes its native host through the existing Desktop bridge.

Resizing a desktop browser cannot rewrite its saved Activity/Workbench choice or activate mobile terminal input.

A hidden toolbar action must retain an explicit reachable entry.

### Temporary desktop navigation
Shell, Flower conversations, Files/Git navigation, and Terminal sessions measure their own shared navigation/content region. When that region cannot fit the current sidebar width plus 480 CSS pixels of main content, the sidebar becomes a transient left side drawer.

Files/Git navigation begins with its mode switch, without a separate Files title row or reserved header space. The switch uses the published field height, including its border and padding, so the sidebar and single-row file toolbar dividers align at every interface scale. The mobile close action shares that row; desktop drawers retain their accessible dialog title and dismissal. Sidebar resizing and local tree scrolling remain available.

File filtering and entering or leaving idle path editing never add header feedback or change toolbar height. The shared bottom status bar owns the filtered item count and view indicator. Path editing keeps Enter submission, Escape cancellation, and blur cancellation without an instruction row; pending navigation and errors retain their accessible header feedback.

Mobile navigation retains its product-specific bottom/side panel behavior under the [mobile Shell](#mobile-shell) and [Flower](#mobile-flower) contracts.

## Mobile Shell
### Persistent navigation and tools
The existing ordered page tabs remain horizontally scrollable.

Download counts and failure attention derive from the same download manager used on desktop. A newer panel request cancels an outgoing handoff.

### Panel boundary and dismissal
One transient requested state selects closed, plugins, More, or a tools subpage.

No drag, snap, or persisted geometry is owned by the product.

## Mobile Flower
The bottom Flower tab enters Flower and opens its conversation drawer.

Background summaries cannot open or close the drawer.

A later focus choice, especially returning to the composer, wins; restoration must not reclaim focus, scroll the page, or interrupt the keyboard session.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
### Flower welcome
Desktop Flower retains its mark, title, introduction, working directory, four complete starter suggestions, and keyboard hints even when the chat region is 767 CSS pixels or narrower. Container queries adjust spacing and the suggestion grid; they cannot hide content or switch interaction mode.

Narrow layouts may ellipsize selection titles; explanations remain normal prose and mobile suggestion cards retain their compact presentation.

The shared local dialog has no global aria-modal claim. Initial focus goes to a close button, never search.

Desktop transitions close mobile navigation and restore the framework toolbar without recreating the active business page.

The [Activity companion](flower-activity-companion.md#companion) owns product placement. The shared [floating boundary](env-app-floating-layer-order.md) owns visible viewport geometry and safe areas.

Flower composer fields expose explicit localized names in both ordinary and private-input forms. Existing thread status, controls, menus, live announcements and collapsed/inactive view boundaries remain authoritative.

Adding roles must not claim keyboard behavior that a surface does not implement.

## Shared business-control localization
Env App, Desktop and Code App consume the coordinated Floe 0.87.0 release set. Env App I18nProvider supplies the published Floe LocaleProvider from its atomically activated locale dictionary. DesktopWelcomeShell uses DesktopFloeLocaleProvider over the existing launcher language snapshot and explicit Desktop catalogs. Desktop core remains a build-only dependency; both renderers pin the same published release and declare its optional Pele/KaTeX peers to preserve diagram rendering. Every shipped locale explicitly defines the full floeControls catalog; keys and placeholders match the upstream public vocabulary. Count labels use neutral labels plus a number so one template does not imply incorrect plural inflection. Language switches update mounted controls without a second locale owner. The product keeps document language/direction and existing domain-specific string adapters.

Select uses combobox/listbox/option semantics; Dropdown remains an action menu. Form identity, validation relationships, popup keyboard ownership, native submission/reset, and civil-date mechanics belong upstream. Product adapters must consume released APIs rather than clone controls. TerminalLayoutPicker spreads the published Popover trigger binding onto its real button so the panel relationship follows upstream identity. Generic Calendar and Breadcrumb come from /ui; legacy umbrella meanings remain unchanged.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Floe Webapp 0.84.0 removes the ambiguous `description` parameter from `Dialog` and `ConfirmDialog`. Custom headers and title JSX must not recreate the removed explanatory subtitle.

This contract changes no application connection, process, or window lifecycle.

## Header-safe bounds

Global dialogs and drawers reserve the visible application header before allocating
their body height. The shared Redeven stylesheet applies the larger of the native
Desktop titlebar and Floe's visible shell top bar plus its top safe inset, followed
by the published presentation gap. Floe owns the visible viewport, keyboard
response, remaining safe edges, panel maximum height, focus and dismissal. The
single product top-padding override is intentional because the published Dialog
sets that padding inline. Do not reintroduce per-dialog viewport subtraction or
minimum heights that can overflow short windows.

The shell header contract is Floe's `h-10` content plus its one-pixel border. A
headerless mobile shell adds no phantom header; inactive KeepAlive views do not
count as visible headers. Surface-local dialogs and Workbench window confirmations
stay within their existing host below the shell header without subtracting it a
second time. Side drawers keep their edge-attached presentation.

Headers, close controls and footer actions remain reachable while long content
scrolls inside the body. Flower settings, nested editors and conversation rename
use the published Dialog. Preserve the bounded loading geometry defined in
[page-loading continuity](page-loading-continuity.md#page-continuity).

Published Floe reserves a stable scrollbar gutter when the default Dialog body
owns scrolling. Panel and body widths stay fixed as content crosses the scrolling
threshold during the existing smooth height transition. Custom layouts that
replace body scrolling retain their full width without an empty gutter. Floe
continues to own height observation, animation and reduced-motion behavior.
